name: NIK-driven non-canonical NF-kB signalling
rationale: The direct members all concern NIK activation and its licensing of non-canonical NF-kB signal transduction, and this branch is the upstream/parallel counterpart to the child theme's TAK1-dependent canonical NF-kB and JNK activation, making 'non-canonical NF-kB signalling' the smallest umbrella that adds the direct members without restating the child.

name: Vesicular trafficking to endosomes and lysosomes
rationale: No collision with parent or siblings; name is distinct and specific.

name: Mechanotransduction and stimulus detection
rationale: Overlaps parent 'Sensory perception and mechanotransduction'; members include auditory/gravity/mechanical detection and general stimulus detection, distinct from sibling's taste/pain sensory perception.

name: Drug-resistant FLT3 mutants
rationale: No siblings, and the name is already more specific than the parent by naming the specific receptor tyrosine kinase (FLT3).

name: Drug-resistant FLT3 mutants
rationale: All four pathways describe FLT3 kinase domain mutants that evade inhibition by a specific tyrosine kinase inhibitor (KW-2449, gilteritinib, sorafenib, sunitinib) while retaining constitutive downstream signalling.

name: Actin-driven membrane protrusion and macropinocytosis
rationale: Covers the child's Arp2/3-based lamellipodium/nucleation biology plus the direct members on ruffle assembly, filament bundling regulation, cell projection assembly and macropinocytosis, all centered on actin remodeling at the cell cortex driving membrane protrusions and fluid uptake.

name: Mesangial cell differentiation and matrix formation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Glomerular capillary development and filtration' via shared 'capillary development' wording; narrowed to mesangial cell differentiation/matrix aspects, distinguishing from PDGF receptor signalling sibling which covers precursor signalling specifically.

name: Notch, Wnt and Hedgehog signalling in development
rationale: Both children and all members concern Notch/Wnt/Hedgehog receptor processing and transcriptional output as it patterns organs and tissues; no direct members extend beyond this developmental signalling axis.

name: mRNA transcription and splicing coupling
rationale: Distinct from parent (RNA processing and turnover) and sibling (RNA metabolism and transcription); specifically names the coupling of transcription and splicing, which neither neighbor conveys.

name: TGF-beta superfamily signalling regulation
rationale: No siblings present and name is more specific than parent, distinguishing regulatory aspect from general receptor signalling.

name: TGF-beta superfamily signalling regulation
rationale: Covers the TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD child plus direct members on activin and NODAL signalling regulation and extracellular ligand maintenance, all part of the broader TGF-beta superfamily receptor system rather than restated as SMAD signalling alone.

name: Beta cell transcriptional identity
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Pancreatic beta cell development and function' and 'Insulin and incretin secretion'; narrowing to transcriptional identity maintenance distinguishes it from secretion-focused and developmental siblings.

name: Transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair
rationale: Repeated generic parent concept 'DNA repair' too broadly; renamed to match the specific transcription-coupled NER mechanism of the parent theme.

name: Cardiomyocyte and skeletal myoblast proliferation
rationale: Overlapped with 'Muscle tissue growth and remodelling' and 'Skeletal muscle development and regeneration'; narrowed to proliferation of specific muscle cell types rather than general growth/remodelling.

name: Blood pressure and stress homeostasis
rationale: Covers renin-angiotensin-driven blood pressure/volume regulation and osmotic/mechanical stress responses, the two children, with no direct members to broaden further; narrower terms like 'renin-angiotensin signalling' would miss the osmotic/mechanical stress child.

name: GTPase-driven trafficking and localization
rationale: Both children cover small GTPase signalling coupled to vesicle trafficking or subcellular localization control, and the sole direct member, RHOBTB GTPase Cycle, is another Rho-family GTPase cycle, so the union stays within GTPase-mediated localization/trafficking rather than broadening to all signal transduction.

name: Constitutively active receptor tyrosine kinase fusions and mutants
rationale: The child covers drug-resistant RTK point mutants, while the direct members add fusion-driven constitutively active FGFR1, PDGFRA/PDGFRB, and FLT3-ITD kinase signalling; the umbrella covers both ligand-independent mutant and fusion RTK activation without invoking drug resistance specifically, since two of the three direct members are not about resistance.

name: GPCR and lipid mediator signalling
rationale: Covers eicosanoid synthesis/signalling plus GPCR-based direct members (purinergic receptors, G-beta:gamma effectors) that act through the same cell-surface receptor superfamily; broader than 'eicosanoid signalling' alone but excludes non-GPCR immune or metabolic pathways.

name: Incretin-mediated regulation of insulin secretion
rationale: Sibling 'Pancreatic development and insulin secretion' shares the same core members (insulin secretion, regulation of insulin secretion, HALLMARK_PANCREAS_BETA_CELLS), so the current name equally describes it; the GLP1/incretin members are what distinguish this theme.

name: Microtubule-based mitochondria and lysosome transport
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Microtubule-based organelle and vesicle transport'; specifying the organelle types (mitochondria, lysosomes) distinguishes it from vesicle-focused transport.

name: General organelle localization and transport
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Microtubule-based transport of neuronal vesicles and organelles', which also involves cytoskeletal transport of organelles; this theme is distinguished by its broader, non-neuronal organelle localization members like mitochondrion localization and RHOT1 GTPase cycle.

name: Mitochondrial urea and cofactor metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Amino acid, nucleobase and vitamin B6 metabolism' via shared 'amino acid' scope; narrowed to mitochondrial-specific urea cycle and cofactor processes to distinguish from sibling's cytosolic amino acid/vitamin focus.

name: Cardiac conduction system cell-cell communication
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Cardiac electrical conduction and coupling', which shares cardiac conduction and heart rate regulation members; the distinguishing feature of this theme is specialized cell-to-cell signal propagation (atrial to AV node, AV node to bundle of His, bundle of His to Purkinje), which the revised name captures without describing the siblings' broader repolarization/depolarization focus.

name: Sex hormone signalling and reproductive development
rationale: Covers steroid/retinoic acid receptor signalling and mammary development plus the direct members on androgen biosynthesis, male sex differentiation, and inner cell mass differentiation (weak at 0.44), all tied to hormone-driven reproductive and embryonic lineage commitment; narrower terms like 'androgen signalling' would exclude mammary and pluripotency members.

name: Nucleotide and nucleoside phosphate interconversion
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere in the hierarchy; renamed to reflect the mix of ribonucleoside/deoxyribonucleoside mono-, di-, and triphosphate metabolic processes present in this theme.

name: Mitochondrial protein import and cristae architecture
rationale: Distinct from parent (biogenesis/mitophagy) and siblings (general maintenance/QC, autophagic clearance); specifically names protein import and cristae architecture.

name: Calcium and chloride ion transport
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Sodium and potassium ion transport' and 'Metal ion homeostasis and cellular stress response'; narrowing to the specific ions distinguishes it.

name: Protein folding and turnover
rationale: Union covers chaperone-mediated folding of proteins and tubulin plus ubiquitin-proteasome degradation, deacetylation and related proteostasis machinery; the smallest umbrella spanning both children without invoking unrelated biology.

name: Cardiac chamber and valve morphogenesis
rationale: Cardiac tissue and cell development is essentially what sibling "Heart development" describes (cardiac muscle/cell tissue development); the theme's actual members are about chamber, valve, and outflow tract morphogenesis, which better separates it from that sibling.

name: Junction assembly regulatory proteins
rationale: Repeats parent 'Tight and adherens junction assembly' and is indistinguishable from sibling 'Cell-cell adhesion and junction organization'; needs a more specific descriptor of its actual member scope.

name: Cytotoxic lymphocyte activation control
rationale: No siblings present, and the name is distinct from both parents, covering activation control rather than cytotoxicity mechanisms or cytokine secretion specifically.

name: Neurite outgrowth and collapse signaling
rationale: Overlapped with parent's general morphogenesis scope and sibling's structural development theme; narrowed to the specific outgrowth-promoting and collapse-inducing signaling pathways that distinguish this theme.

name: N-linked and O-linked glycosylation
rationale: Repeated the parent name; distinguished from sibling by covering general glycosylation pathways rather than dystroglycan-specific disorders.

name: Regulation of protein degradation and localization
rationale: The current name mentions 'cell death signalling' which is not represented in members; no sibling collision found, but name overreaches beyond member content (no cell death signaling members present), so narrowed to protein degradation/localization/modification regulation actually reflected in the members.

name: Kinetochore-microtubule attachment
rationale: Repeated parent name exactly; kinetochore-microtubule attachment distinguishes this theme's mechanism from fidelity checkpoints and structural maintenance siblings.

name: Platelet activation, adhesion and degranulation
rationale: Extends the single child (platelet activation/coagulation signalling) with direct members on negative regulation of platelet activation, homotypic cell-cell adhesion, and platelet degranulation, so the umbrella covers activation, its restraint, adhesion, and granule release without adding unrelated coagulation-cascade biology.

name: DNA repair and cell cycle checkpoints
rationale: Overlapped with parent's genome maintenance scope and with p53-driven DNA damage response sibling; narrowed to non-p53 DNA repair and checkpoint mechanisms.

name: Cell-matrix adhesion dynamics
rationale: No siblings to collide with and name is distinct from parent, which is broader (migration process vs adhesion dynamics).

name: Cardiac tissue and pericardium development
rationale: The original name would also describe the sibling's outflow tract/valve morphogenesis members; this theme's distinct members are broader heart/atrial/ventricular tissue development and pericardium formation, not vasculature.

name: Regulation of neurite outgrowth and extension
rationale: Overlaps with siblings 'Axon guidance and growth cone signalling' and 'GTPase-mediated axon guidance signalling', which share the axon guidance/ephrin members; this theme is distinguished by its emphasis on regulating neurite/axon extension and growth rather than guidance signalling itself.

name: Smooth muscle contractile and vascular remodeling programs
rationale: Both children concern contractile/cytoskeletal gene programs and vascular or wound remodeling, and the direct member (regulation of vascular endothelial cell proliferation) fits within vascular remodeling; the umbrella covers contractile phenotype and tissue remodeling without invoking generic 'signalling' or 'processes'.

name: Lipid droplet storage and glycerophospholipid biosynthesis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Phospholipid metabolism and dephosphorylation'; the distinguishing focus here is triglyceride/lipid droplet storage and glycerophospholipid synthesis rather than general phospholipid turnover.

name: tRNA and snRNA modification
rationale: Sibling 'Nucleolar RNA processing and ribosome biogenesis factors' also involves ribosomal/rRNA processing and shares snoRNP assembly and snRNA modification, so 'Ribosomal and tRNA maturation' overlaps it; renaming to focus on tRNA/snRNA modification distinguishes the theme's actual members from the rRNA-processing sibling.

name: Monoamine catabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent (metabolism and transport is broader, covering synthesis/transport too) with no siblings to collide with.

name: HPA axis hormone secretion regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers hormone secretion generally) and sibling (gonadotropin-specific); this theme specifically addresses HPA axis regulation.

name: Xenobiotic and drug metabolism
rationale: All members describe the phase I/II enzymes and transporters that metabolise, conjugate and clear drugs and xenobiotic compounds.

name: RHOA, RHOF and CDC42 GTPase cycles
rationale: Repeats the parent name 'Rho family GTPase cycles' almost verbatim; renamed to specify the particular GTPases covered by this theme's members.

name: Stem and progenitor cell population homeostasis
rationale: Covers the child (progenitor proliferation/commitment regulation) plus direct members on hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis, kidney progenitor proliferation, and somatic stem cell maintenance regulation, all concerning maintenance of stem/progenitor pool size and fate balance.

name: Anteroposterior neural tube patterning
rationale: Actually the current name 'Neural tube dorsoventral patterning' is distinct from parent 'Anteroposterior neural tube patterning' since dorsoventral differs from anteroposterior; no revision needed.-

name: Cranial and visceral organogenesis
rationale: All members describe patterning and morphogenesis of head/neck and endodermal organs (facial nerve, thyroid, gut, face, lung buds, salivary gland) via shared reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal and neural crest/pharyngeal arch mechanisms.

name: Antigen presentation and T cell response
rationale: Both children cover MHC-restricted antigen processing/presentation, and the direct member adds T cell mediated immunity downstream of that presentation, so the parent must span presentation plus the T cell response it triggers.

name: Viral replication and assembly
rationale: The members describe viral genome replication, translation, and virion assembly/maturation, not host antiviral defence; 'host antiviral defence' overlaps with sibling 'Host-virus interactions and antiviral interferon regulation', so narrowing to the viral life-cycle processes actually present separates it.

name: Neurotransmitter release and vesicle recycling regulation
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Synaptic vesicle trafficking and recycling', which shares identical members (synaptic vesicle recycling, synaptic vesicle recycling via endosome); revised to emphasize neurotransmitter release/uptake regulation distinguishing this theme.

name: Ghrelin and leptin appetite signaling
rationale: Repeated parent's wording closely; sibling 'Somatotropic axis growth regulation' covers growth hormone axis, so this theme should specify the appetite-hormone side (ghrelin/leptin) to distinguish it.

name: DNA replication licensing and synthesis
rationale: All three pathways describe origin licensing, replisome assembly and processive DNA synthesis during genome duplication.

name: Interstrand cross-link repair
rationale: As broad as the parent 'Interstrand cross-link and strand break repair' and would equally describe the sibling 'Nucleotide excision repair'; the members specifically concern cross-link repair, distinguishing it from nucleotide excision repair.

name: Nephron and renal tract morphogenesis
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and name is more specific than either parent by combining nephron and renal tract structures.

name: Glycogen metabolism and storage disease
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than the parent, which covers dietary sugar metabolism broadly.

name: Post-Golgi trafficking to the plasma membrane and cilium
rationale: All members concern vesicle-mediated delivery of proteins from the Golgi/post-Golgi compartments to the cell surface or ciliary membrane, broader than the single named child but not extending to generic Golgi or membrane raft biology.

name: Lipoprotein particle remodeling and assembly
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; revised to emphasize particle remodeling/assembly processes, distinguishing from the sibling's dietary absorption focus.

name: Muscle growth and differentiation regulation
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from the parent 'Smooth and cardiac muscle remodelling', specifying growth and differentiation regulation.

name: Nucleotide biosynthesis, salvage and metabolism
rationale: Covers both children (de novo/general nucleotide metabolism and purine/nucleoside salvage) plus the direct members on pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate synthesis and adenine salvage defects, without narrowing to any one nucleotide class or route.

name: DNA damage repair from oxidative stress
rationale: Too broad and overlapped conceptually with parent's oxidative stress focus; narrowed to specific damage repair mechanism distinguishing it from sibling's homeostasis/xenobiotic focus.

name: Cyclic nucleotide and GPCR signalling in neuromodulation and secretion
rationale: All children involve cAMP/cGMP or GPCR-linked signalling and its downstream effects on neural, secretory or muscular targets; the direct members (copulation, smooth muscle contraction regulation) are behavioural/contractile outputs of exactly this signalling, so the parent broadens to cover both the signalling machinery and its physiological output without repeating any single child's name.

name: Mitochondrial energy metabolism and transport
rationale: Both children concern respiratory ATP production and its redox regulation, and the direct members add oxidative phosphorylation machinery and the mitochondrial transport systems that supply and export substrates for it.

name: Guanine and phosphate nucleotide metabolism
rationale: Core members at 1.00 (GTP biosynthesis, GTP metabolism, NTP biosynthesis, phosphorus metabolic process) all concern synthesis and interconversion of GTP/nucleotide triphosphates and phosphate transfer chemistry. Organophosphate metabolic process (0.72) is broader but still centers on phosphate/nucleotide handling. Weaker members nucleoside diphosphate catabolic process (0.35) and nucleotide transmembrane transport (0.44) extend into catabolism and transport but are excluded from the core claim.

name: Drug-resistant receptor tyrosine kinase mutants
rationale: No siblings and name is more specific than parent (drug-resistant subset), no collision.

The members split into two unrelated groups—polyamine biosynthesis/transport/regulation, and protein post-translational modifications (hydroxylation, histidine modification, methylation)—with no common biological thread linking them.

name: Glucose homeostasis and insulin secretion
rationale: Covers the child (hormone secretion regulation tied to insulin) plus direct members on carbohydrate homeostasis, beta-cell identity, and ABCC8-linked glycemic defects; tighter terms like 'insulin secretion' alone would exclude the carbohydrate-homeostasis and beta-cell direct members.

name: Adenylate cyclase-coupled receptor signalling
rationale: The broad term 'cyclic nucleotide signalling' equally fits both siblings which are cAMP-based; this theme is distinguished by adenylate cyclase activation/regulation via GPCRs, not shared by the CREB or generic cAMP/calcium siblings.

name: L-amino acid selective transporters
rationale: Repeats parent 'Neutral amino acid membrane transport' concept without distinguishing itself; revised to specify selectivity distinguishing it from general neutral amino acid transport.

name: Chromatin organization and genomic imprinting
rationale: The current name overlaps heavily with sibling 'Chromatin and histone modification in epigenetic regulation', which shares similar members. This theme's distinct members emphasize chromatin organization and imprinting/zygotic programming rather than histone modification specifically.

name: Hemophilia-associated factor VIII/IX defects
rationale: Distinct from parent (specific to factor VIII/IX deficiencies rather than general coagulation disorders) and from sibling (platelet activation), so no revision needed.

name: Gonadotropin signalling in the ovulatory cycle
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers meiotic progression broadly) and sibling (reproductive development/gametogenesis); this theme specifically addresses gonadotropin signalling in ovulatory cycling.

name: Small GTPase signalling regulation
rationale: All members concern GEFs, GAPs, GDIs or effectors that regulate small GTPase activity and downstream localization/signalling outputs.

name: Endolysosomal membrane trafficking and autophagy
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent, distinguishing endolysosomal/autophagy mechanisms from general vesicular trafficking.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation fidelity
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'DNA repair and cell cycle checkpoints' and sibling's genome stability scope; narrowed to the mitotic division/segregation focus distinguishing it from checkpoint repair and telomere senescence themes.

name: Triglyceride and phospholipid storage metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; no collision with bile acid, cholesterol, dietary lipid, adipocyte, or ketone-focused themes.

name: Nuclear pore transport and RNA/protein export
rationale: Covers both children (pore complex-mediated transport/envelope reassembly and nucleocytoplasmic transport of RNA and protein cargo) plus the direct member on viral hijacking of the nuclear export machinery, without broadening beyond nuclear transport processes.

name: Mitochondrial GABA and nucleobase catabolism disorders
rationale: Overlaps sibling's branched-chain amino acid/keto acid catabolism theme; own members center on GABA degradation, 2-oxoglutarate/2-hydroxyglutarate interconversion, and pyrimidine catabolism plus related deficiencies, distinguishing it from the BCAA-focused sibling.

name: Mitotic checkpoint surveillance
rationale: Not directly repeating parent, but 'Mitotic cell division' describes a broader process than checkpoint control; revised to specify mitotic checkpoint mechanisms, distinguishing from G1/S checkpoint control and phase transitions.

name: Telomere-linked senescence and genome stability
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader checkpoint/repair processes) and sibling (division/integrity); focuses specifically on telomere-linked senescence mechanisms.

name: Sensory perception and receptor biology
rationale: The union spans photoreceptor biology, general sensory receptor biology, and sour taste perception, all covered by the existing child name 'Sensory perception and receptor biology' which already encompasses photoreceptor biology as a subset.

name: Long-chain and very long-chain fatty acid metabolism
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent by specifying chain length categories rather than repeating peroxisomal beta-oxidation.

name: Long-chain and very long-chain fatty acid metabolism
rationale: All four members concern elongation, desaturation, or peroxisomal oxidation of long- and very-long-chain fatty acids, including the omega-3 precursor alpha-linolenic acid processed through the same elongase/peroxisomal machinery.

name: Forebrain and cerebellar neurodevelopment
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; specifies forebrain/cerebellar development outcome versus neural tube patterning process, no collision.

name: Fasting-induced lipolysis and ketogenesis
rationale: Distinct from parent's storage/transport focus and siblings; narrows to hormonal/nutrient regulation of lipolysis and ketone body production.

name: Central carbon, lipid and cofactor metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent 'Amino acid catabolism' and siblings focused on amino acid/nitrogen/sulfur metabolism; this theme covers central carbon, lipid, and cofactor metabolism, a clearly different scope.

name: Endoderm germ layer specification
rationale: Collides with siblings 'Endoderm organ development and epithelial specification', 'Endoderm-derived epithelial organ development', and 'Endoderm-derived organ morphogenesis and differentiation'; narrowed to the germ-layer specification step distinct from those organ-development themes.

name: Neurodegenerative proteinopathy and glial fate regulation
rationale: Union spans amyloid-beta/tau pathology control and gliogenesis/glial proliferation control, two CNS regulatory programmes with no direct members adding further scope.

name: Glomerular mesangial cell and capillary tuft development
rationale: All members at inclusion \u22650.5 concern mesangial cell differentiation, proliferation and development or glomerular capillary tuft morphogenesis and filtration regulation, driven by PDGF/Notch signalling; the weakly included cell migration in kidney development (0.30) is excluded as a broader nephrogenesis process.

name: Immune cell differentiation and inflammatory signalling
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings, which focus on adhesion/hemostasis while this covers differentiation and inflammatory signalling.

name: Presynaptic vesicular neurotransmitter transport
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Presynaptic neurotransmitter release and reuptake'; narrowed to focus on vesicular loading/transport rather than release and reuptake mechanisms.

name: Endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLR signalling
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than both parents by specifying the nucleic acid-sensing TLR subset and endosomal signalling context.

name: Endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLR signaling
rationale: All members concern endosomal/lysosomal Toll-like receptor detection of viral nucleic acids, their trafficking/maturation, and downstream IRF/NF-kB activation leading to interferon production.

name: Platelet-mediated hemostasis and vascular signalling
rationale: Both children—platelet activation/adhesion/degranulation and GTPase-driven cytoskeletal/vascular signalling—converge on platelet-based hemostatic and vascular response biology, with no direct members to extend beyond this.

name: Cardiac excitability and electrical conduction
rationale: Unites the three children on cardiac membrane excitability, pacemaking and cell-to-cell electrical coupling; the direct member (negative regulation of potassium ion transport) fits as one of the modulatory mechanisms tuning that excitability, so the umbrella need not broaden beyond cardiac electrophysiology.

name: Constitutively active kinase fusions in oncogenesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader mutant/fusion signalling) and sibling (specifically RTK mutants/fusions); this theme covers non-RTK constitutively active kinase fusions.

name: Amino acid and small solute transport
rationale: Covers both children (amino acid transport, amino acid and GABA transport) plus the direct member oxalate transport, which is a small organic anion carried by related solute-carrier systems; broader wording is needed only to admit oxalate transport alongside amino acid transport.

name: Nutritional immunity and metal sequestration
rationale: Overlapped with parent's antimicrobial focus; the members specifically involve metal ion sequestration mechanisms, distinguishing from sibling's humoral effectors and parent's broader phagocyte mechanisms.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase signal transduction
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no repeated parent (root) or collision with sibling names.

name: Glycolysis and pyruvate/NAD(P)H cofactor metabolism
rationale: Core members (pyruvate metabolism, nucleoside diphosphate catabolism, pyridine compound catabolism, both glycolysis entries) center on glycolytic flux, pyruvate handling and NAD(P)/NADPH cofactor turnover tied to glycolysis. Oxygen transport (0.40) and NAD+ metabolic process (0.33) are below threshold and excluded; oxygen transport shares no glycolytic biology with the rest.

name: Calcium-cAMP-CREB signalling
rationale: No siblings present and name is distinct from both parents, specifying a calcium-cAMP-CREB axis not implied by either parent name.

name: Interstrand cross-link and strand break repair
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'DNA damage repair' (too generic) and shared members with 'Base excision repair of abasic sites and strand breaks'; new name emphasizes the ICL/NEIL3-specific repair focus unique to this theme.

name: Epidermal and hair follicle differentiation
rationale: No siblings present, and name is distinct from parent (differentiation process vs. cornified envelope formation/keratinization outcome).

name: Central carbon and small-metabolite metabolism
rationale: Covers pyruvate/central carbon metabolism plus glycerol, alditol, and alanine metabolism, all small-molecule central metabolic pathways feeding or branching from core carbon metabolism.

name: Chylomicron and triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remodeling and clearance
rationale: All three members concern lipoprotein lipase-mediated processing of chylomicrons/triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and remnant clearance by the liver.

name: Smooth muscle contraction regulation
rationale: The sibling 'Muscle contraction and ion homeostasis' shares the same core members (muscle system process, muscle contraction, regulation of muscle contraction), so 'Muscle contraction' fits it too; this theme is distinguished by its focus on smooth muscle contraction and its regulation.

name: Nucleic acid sensing and type I interferon signalling
rationale: Already distinct from parent and sibling; specifically covers nucleic acid sensing coupled with type I interferon signalling, distinct from broader antiviral defence and host-virus interaction sibling.

name: Cholesterol biosynthesis pathway
rationale: All three cover post-squalene cholesterol synthesis (Bloch/Kandutsch-Russell routes) and its transcriptional regulation via SREBF/mevalonate genes.

name: GTPase-mediated axon guidance signalling
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Axon guidance and neurite outgrowth control', which shares the same axon guidance/neurite theme; this theme's distinct focus is small GTPase (Rho/ephrin/Robo) signal transduction, so specifying that mechanism separates it.

name: Sensory perception and mechanotransduction
rationale: Covers both children—sensory organ development/function and mechanical/pressure sensing—reflecting the shared theme of stimulus detection and transduction across sensory modalities, without narrowing to any single sense.

name: Amino sugar and nucleotide-sugar metabolism
rationale: All members concern synthesis, interconversion or catabolism of amino sugars (GlcNAc, sialic acid, glucosamine) and nucleotide-sugar donors (UDP-GlcNAc, GDP-mannose, GDP-fucose) that feed glycosylation, including carbohydrate phosphorylation as the entry step and catabolic routes that recycle these sugars back to central metabolism.

name: Ubiquitin-proteasome regulation of cell cycle and p53 turnover
rationale: The high-inclusion members (COP1 autodegradation, TP53 degradation, Cdc25A degradation, PD-L1 degradation, and regulation of protein modification/localization to chromatin) all converge on ubiquitin ligase- and phosphorylation-controlled proteasomal turnover of key regulatory proteins governing cell cycle checkpoints and p53 stability; the weakly included negative regulation of PTM member (0.39) is broader but still consistent with this control layer.

name: Ubiquitination and proteasome assembly
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Proteasomal protein degradation and its regulation' which also covers proteasomal degradation broadly; renamed to specifically reflect ubiquitin conjugation (polyubiquitination, Neddylation, K48-linked ubiquitination) and proteasome assembly, which are the distinguishing members.

name: Coagulation factor defects and cascade activation
rationale: The term 'Hemostasis' overlaps with the sibling 'Platelet activation and coagulation signalling', whose top members are literally hemostasis pathways; this theme's members focus on coagulation factor defects and cascade initiation/amplification, which better distinguishes it.

name: Long-term potentiation signalling
rationale: Overlapped with parent's 'synaptic signalling' and sibling 'synaptic glutamate receptor regulation'; narrowing to LTP-specific plasticity mechanisms distinguishes it from receptor regulation and cytoskeletal remodeling siblings.

name: RNA polymerase elongation, splicing and rRNA maturation
rationale: The original name overlapped with sibling 'Transcription termination and mRNA processing/decay' since both cover transcription termination and mRNA 3'-end processing; the theme's distinct focus is elongation, splice site recognition, rRNA maturation and Pol III transcription.

name: Mitotic spindle and chromosome segregation
rationale: All three children and the direct members (Rho GTPase cycle, mitotic cell division, cytokinesis) converge on spindle-based chromosome segregation and its coupled cytokinesis; no broader cell-cycle phase is implicated.

name: Sulfur amino acid metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Amino acid catabolism' and sibling 'Nitrogen and amino acid metabolism'; narrowed to sulfur-containing amino acid pathways specifically.

name: Cholesterol and HDL transport regulation
rationale: Distinct from parents and siblings; no other sibling covers cholesterol/HDL transport specifically.

name: Hemostasis and coagulation factor disorders
rationale: Distinct from parent (vascular injury response is broader) and sibling (fibrotic remodelling is a different process); adequately specific.

name: Insulin and glucagon substrate signaling
rationale: Nearly synonymous with parent 'Hormonal regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism' and overlaps sibling scope; narrowed to specify the hormonal axis distinguishing it.

name: Neuronal vesicle transport along microtubules
rationale: Sibling 'Cytoskeletal transport of organelles' covers general organelle localization including mitochondria; this theme is specific to neuronal vesicles and synaptic/dendritic cargo, which the revised name makes clearer while dropping the redundant 'organelles' overlap.

name: Phosphate ion metabolism
rationale: Collided with sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism' and echoed parent 'Phosphate group transport and metabolism'; narrowing to phosphate ion handling distinguishes it from the nucleotide-focused sibling.

name: Hemostasis and platelet-mediated cell adhesion
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; no other theme covers hemostasis/platelet adhesion specifically.

name: Neural tube regional patterning
rationale: All members concern dorsoventral or anteroposterior patterning of the neural tube/plate and forebrain/midbrain-hindbrain territories, establishing regional identity via SHH, WNT, BMP and FGF signalling; cell fate determination (0.43) and neural plate pattern specification (0.45) are more general but still fit this patterning theme.

name: Cyclic nucleotide and calcium second messenger signalling
rationale: All three children concern cAMP/cGMP or calcium-based second messenger cascades, and representative members (cAMP synthesis/degradation, guanylyl cyclase signalling) fit this union without adding new biology; no direct members require broadening further.

name: Viral replication and host antiviral defence
rationale: All members centre on the virus life cycle inside host cells (entry, genome replication, assembly/budding) and the host restriction/sensing machinery that opposes it, exemplified generically by the GO terms and specifically by HIV reverse transcription and virion assembly. The SARS therapeutics pathway (0.41) is excluded, as it mixes entry factors with unrelated host inflammatory drug targets.

name: Regulation of neurotransmitter transport and uptake
rationale: The current name would equally describe the sibling 'Glutamatergic synaptic signalling and neurotransmitter release', which shares nearly identical release-related members; this theme is distinguished by its emphasis on transport and uptake regulation rather than glutamatergic release specifically.

name: cAMP-CREB signalling in cellular response
rationale: Name collided with another theme; also overlaps heavily with sibling themes sharing identical top members (cAMP biosynthetic process, cyclase activity), so specificity toward CREB and cellular response distinguishes it.

name: Oro-gastric secretion and sensation
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no parent to collide with.

name: Germ cell meiosis and fertilisation
rationale: Union covers gonad development, meiotic gamete formation and sperm-egg fusion, spanning both children without extending beyond reproductive germline biology.

name: Skeletal muscle development and regeneration
rationale: Distinct from siblings like "Muscle tissue growth and remodelling" and "Cardiac and skeletal muscle growth and proliferation" since it specifically covers skeletal muscle development and regeneration processes, not cardiac or generic muscle remodelling.

name: Mitotic recombination and telomere maintenance
rationale: Repeats parent's 'Recombination-based telomere and chromosome maintenance'; narrowed to mitotic recombination specifics matching own members.

name: Hippo and MAPK/ERK pathway regulation
rationale: Three members directly regulate Hippo signalling, while ERK inactivation, MAPK negative regulation and RSK activation (0.44) all concern the RAS-ERK cascade's activation and shutoff; together these form a growth-signalling regulatory theme spanning both pathways.

name: Circadian clock gene expression
rationale: Distinct from all siblings and does not repeat either parent name.

name: Circadian clock gene expression
rationale: All members describe the core circadian oscillator: the CLOCK/BMAL1/NPAS2-PER-CRY transcriptional feedback loop, its phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and the broader rhythmic processes it generates.

name: Monocyte and neutrophil biology
rationale: Distinct from siblings which cover other lineages (myeloid/megakaryocyte differentiation, lymphocyte identity, phagocyte effector mechanisms); name specifies monocyte/neutrophil biology uniquely.

name: Redox homeostasis and ferroptosis regulation
rationale: The sibling 'Oxidative damage response and protein repair' shares nearly identical members (response to oxygen radical, cell redox homeostasis, ferroptosis), and the current name's 'mitochondrial energy metabolism' claim is unsupported since no members concern energy metabolism; the revised name reflects the actual redox/ferroptosis focus.

name: Mitochondrial and cytosolic gene expression
rationale: Union covers translation (cytosolic and mitochondrial), mitochondrial gene expression, and the direct member mitochondrial rRNA processing, all steps in producing proteins from nuclear and mitochondrial genomes.

name: cGAS/RIG-I-driven type I interferon induction
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing and antiviral interferon signalling'; specifying the cGAS/RIG-I sensors distinguishes it from that parent and from the TLR-driven sibling.

name: Activity-dependent synaptic plasticity
rationale: Repeats parent 'Synaptic architecture and plasticity' and overlaps sibling 'Neurotransmitter release and synaptic signalling'; narrowing to plasticity mechanisms driven by activity distinguishes it.

name: Amino acid and small solute transport
rationale: placeholder

name: Calcium-mediated muscle contraction
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; also this theme's members focus on calcium ion transport and contraction regulation, distinguishing it from the assembly-focused sibling and the excitability-focused sibling.

name: Fertilization and reproductive process regulation details
rationale: Overlaps too closely with sibling 'Gametogenesis and meiotic division' since both cover meiosis/gametogenesis; revise to emphasize fertilization and reproductive process events like acrosome reaction, zona pellucida penetration, and reproductive process regulation, distinct from the meiotic division focus of the sibling.

name: Selectin-mediated leukocyte rolling
rationale: Nearly restated the parent concept of leukocyte-endothelial adhesion control; narrowed to the specific rolling/selectin mechanism, distinguishing it from the mechanotransduction sibling.

name: Leukocyte-endothelial adhesion regulation
rationale: All four pathways concern up- or down-regulation of leukocyte adhesion to vascular endothelium and the subsequent extravasation step, spanning adhesion molecule production, endothelial adhesiveness, and diapedesis restraint.

name: Glucose and lipid metabolic regulation
rationale: Too broad and overlapped with siblings like insulin secretion, HPA axis, and steroid biosynthesis; narrowed to the metabolic regulation aspect distinct from those specific endocrine axes.

name: Autophagic clearance of mitochondria and organelles
rationale: The child (mitochondrial quality control) plus direct members (macroautophagy, mitochondrion localization, pexophagy) converge on selective autophagic turnover of mitochondria and related organelles like peroxisomes, broader than mitochondrial quality control alone since it includes general macroautophagy and pexophagy, but tight to organelle clearance rather than all autophagy or metabolism.

name: Oxidative stress response and antioxidant defence
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent (which also covers ferroptosis regulation), so it remains distinct.

name: Antioxidant defence and redox homeostasis
rationale: All members center on detoxifying reactive oxygen species (superoxide dismutases, catalase, peroxiredoxins, thioredoxin/glutathione systems) and maintaining cellular redox balance, including the NFE2L2-driven transcriptional response; the weakly included cell redox homeostasis and chemical stress response members fit the same antioxidant/thiol-redox core.

name: Nucleotide-sugar and amino sugar metabolism
rationale: The members are biosynthetic/catabolic processes, not disease states, so 'disorders' misdescribes them; renamed to reflect nucleotide-sugar and amino sugar metabolic pathways, distinguishing it from the sibling's transport focus.

name: Biogenic amine catabolism and transport
rationale: Covers the monoamine/serotonin metabolism child plus catecholamine uptake and amino acid catabolism among direct members; bile acid transport (0.29) is below threshold and excluded from consideration.

name: Cytochrome c release and apoptosome formation
rationale: Repeated parent 'Mitochondrial apoptotic signalling' essentially verbatim; renamed to specify the distinct downstream steps this theme covers.

name: Mucopolysaccharide and glycoprotein degradation disorders
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Glycan, glycolipid and galactose metabolism' on generic glycan metabolism; narrowed to the mucopolysaccharidosis/glycoprotein degradation enzyme defects that distinguish this theme.

name: Epidermal differentiation and cornification
rationale: Union of the epidermal/hair follicle development child with keratinization and cornified envelope formation, all centered on terminal epidermal differentiation into the keratinized barrier; broader than 'keratinization' alone to include the developmental child, but restricted to skin/appendage differentiation rather than epithelial differentiation generally.

name: Coagulation cascade regulation
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent 'Platelet activation and coagulation'; renamed to focus on the coagulation cascade regulation aspect distinct from platelet activation.

name: Dendritic morphogenesis and synaptic signalling
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and name is distinct from parent by specifying dendritic morphogenesis and synaptic signalling versus the broader neuronal morphogenesis process.

Members mix phosphatase regulation, mTOR-linked cell size control, muscle homeostasis, caveolar endocytosis, surface protein trafficking and RHOBTB GTPase biology, with no single mechanism or compartment shared by all high-inclusion members beyond a loose theme of muscle/membrane signalling regulation that would be an invented generalisation.

name: RNA Pol II elongation, termination, and mRNA 3'-end processing
rationale: Sibling 'Spliceosome assembly and RNA polymerase transcription termination' shares the same termination members, so the name must emphasize elongation and 3'-end processing to distinguish it.

name: Macrophage cytokine-driven inflammatory activation
rationale: Union covers macrophage/myeloid TLR- and Fc-receptor-driven cytokine and inflammatory mediator production plus its regulation, broader than the single TLR-specific child but restricted to macrophage/myeloid inflammatory mediator output rather than immune signalling generally.

name: Taste and pH sensing
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, but the current name is too broad relative to its parent 'Sensory organ development and function' and the members, which specifically concern taste perception, pH response, and ion channels rather than sensory perception generally.

name: Aquaporin-mediated water transport
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Osmotic and water homeostasis'; specifying aquaporin channels distinguishes the mechanism from general osmotic homeostasis.

name: Glycan and proteoglycan biosynthesis disorders
rationale: Both children and all members concern sugar-chain assembly on proteins - N/O-glycosylation and glycosaminoglycan/proteoglycan synthesis - and the diseases arising from their disruption, with no direct members requiring broader scope.

name: tRNA modification and processing
rationale: Nucleolar also fits the sibling "Ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing", which involves nucleolar snoRNP assembly; the theme's own members are almost entirely tRNA modification/processing events, so narrowing to that removes the overlap.

name: Diverse small-molecule metabolic pathways
rationale: The current name asserts 'solute transport' and 'homeostasis', which none of the members (xenobiotic, fatty acid, urea cycle, amino acid, galactose, nucleotide metabolism) actually reflect; also risks overlap with siblings like 'Ion homeostasis and transport'. Revised to describe the actual shared theme of small-molecule/metabolic biosynthesis and catabolism.

name: Dopaminergic reward and motivation regulation
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Dopaminergic modulation of locomotor behavior'; distinguishing by reward/motivation focus rather than locomotion.

name: Systemic phosphate and mineral ion homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with 'Skeletal mineralization and matrix glycosylation'; narrowed to emphasize systemic phosphate/ion regulation rather than skeletal matrix-specific mineralization.

name: Excitation-contraction coupling
rationale: Already distinct: it names the specific electrical-to-mechanical coupling process, unlike the parent (hypertrophy regulation) and siblings which focus on growth signaling and general contraction/calcium regulation.

name: Renal tubule and ureter morphogenesis
rationale: Repeats and broadens parent's specific glomerular endothelial vasculature focus; renaming to a more specific structural scope distinguishes it from parent.

name: Amyloid-beta homeostasis and lipoprotein signalling
rationale: Covers the amyloid-beta production/clearance/aggregation child plus the direct members: lipoprotein particle signalling, neurofibrillary tangle regulation, and amyloid fibril formation control, all converging on amyloid handling and its lipoprotein-linked regulation.

name: NCAM and neurofascin adhesion signalling
rationale: Very similar to sibling 'Axon growth, myelination and glial adhesion' which shares the same top members (myelin formation, axon ensheathment, Neurofascin interactions); this theme is better distinguished by its emphasis on NCAM1/Neurofascin adhesion molecule signalling and NMJ development.

name: Nucleotide-excision, mismatch, and cross-link repair
rationale: The generic name overlaps with siblings covering excision/base-excision repair and could describe any repair pathway; renamed to reflect its distinct members (nucleotide-excision, mismatch, and interstrand cross-link repair) not covered by the base-excision or recombination siblings.

name: GTPase cycle regulation by GAPs and GEFs
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'Small GTPase signalling' and 'Rho GTPase signalling'; specifying regulation via GAP/GEF cycling distinguishes it from general signalling siblings.

name: Bile acid and alcohol biosynthesis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Bile acid and fat-soluble vitamin metabolism' on bile acid scope; narrowed to alcohol-specific processing distinct from vitamin handling.

name: Amino acid and micronutrient metabolism
rationale: Overlapped conceptually with parent's glucose/lipid focus and was too vague versus siblings like pancreatic function or adipocyte regulation; narrowed to the specific small-molecule classes distinct from glucose/lipid/hormone pathways.

name: Ribosome biogenesis and nuclear RNA processing
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically names ribosome biogenesis and nuclear RNA processing, unlike the broader parent and the sibling's focus on gene expression/protein biosynthesis.

name: Germ cell and oocyte maturation control
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader gonadal development) and sibling (meiotic gametogenesis focuses specifically on meiosis, while this covers germ cell/oocyte maturation broadly); no collision.

name: PI3K/AKT signalling via growth factor receptors
rationale: All three concern receptor-driven activation of class I PI3K and downstream AKT signalling, including its aberrant constitutive activation in cancer and its IRS-mediated route from IGF1R.

name: Cadherin expression and adhesion regulation
rationale: The child covers E-cadherin adhesion/turnover; direct members add CDH11 and type II classical cadherin transcriptional control, CDH1 mRNA translational regulation by microRNAs, and TGFBR3 signalling/expression that feeds into cadherin regulation. The umbrella is cadherin-family expression and adhesive function control, broader than the single child but not a generic adhesion or TGF-beta label.

The single child covers RNA turnover and silencing pathways, while the lone direct member concerns inflammatory mediator production—an unrelated immune signalling process with only weak (0.25) inclusion; no honest umbrella narrower than 'gene expression regulation and immune response' unites them, and that would be near-vacuous.

name: Meiotic chromosome and spindle dynamics
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers broader meiotic division processes) and sibling (gametogenesis/reproductive development); this theme specifically covers chromosome and spindle mechanics.

name: Sensory signal transduction
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Sensory organ function and perception'; renamed to specify the perceptual signaling/transduction aspect distinct from organ structure/function.

name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium reuptake
rationale: No siblings, and the name is already more specific than the parent (reuptake vs. broader cycling), distinguishing it clearly.

name: SR calcium reuptake for relaxation
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Calcium sequestration and reuptake for muscle relaxation'; narrowed to specify sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) reuptake mechanism distinct from the general parent theme.

name: Sister chromatid cohesion and mitotic recombination
rationale: Overlaps with 'Telomere maintenance and cellular senescence' sibling given telomere maintenance via recombination; more specific name reflecting cohesion and recombination processes distinguishes it from telomere-focused sibling and other cell cycle siblings.

name: Post-Golgi transport to the vacuole
rationale: Repeats parent's mention of vacuole/lysosome transport without distinguishing; renamed to specify post-Golgi to vacuole routing, matching members like Golgi to vacuole transport and post-Golgi vesicle-mediated transport, distinct from sibling's generic COPII/secretion focus.

name: General ER stress and UPR overview
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Unfolded protein response regulation' and duplicates parent's ER stress focus; needs to distinguish itself as a broader overview rather than the specific regulation covered by the sibling.

name: Glycolysis and TCA cycle regulation
rationale: Overlapped parent's 'carbon metabolism' term and sibling's ketogenesis focus; narrowed to the specific glycolytic/TCA pathways this theme actually covers.

name: Platelet activation and thrombin/PAR signalling in hemostasis
rationale: No collision with parent or siblings; name is already distinct and specific.

name: Oncogenic kinase signalling by mutant and fusion proteins
rationale: Both children and all representative members describe constitutively active kinases—receptor tyrosine kinase fusions/mutants and downstream kinase fusions/mutants like MAP2K—driving ligand-independent oncogenic signalling.

name: Embryonic tissue and organ patterning
rationale: The child covers germ layer and cell fate commitment, while direct members add neural crest fate, diaphragm development, and endothelin-mediated blood pressure regulation—broader developmental patterning and morphogenesis events beyond fate specification alone.

name: Mitochondrial redox and oxygen homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitochondrial respiration and its regulation', which covers core electron transport chain/oxidative phosphorylation; this theme's members focus on ROS, oxygen response, and membrane potential/permeability regulation, so renamed to reflect redox and oxygen homeostasis rather than respiration itself.

name: Cytoskeletal remodeling in neurite and synapse growth
rationale: Repeats the parent name almost verbatim; both siblings also concern dendritic/synaptic plasticity. This theme's members focus specifically on cytoskeletal/structural remodeling (microtubule nucleation, filopodium assembly, actin organization, receptor diffusion), distinguishing it from the regulatory and postsynaptic-maintenance siblings.

name: Regulation of ER stress sensor signalling
rationale: All members concern control of IRE1 or PERK arms of the unfolded protein response, via chaperones, phosphatases and feedback loops that tune sensor activity and duration.

name: Glycosaminoglycan metabolism and lysosomal storage disorders
rationale: Collided with sibling 'Glycosaminoglycan metabolism and related skeletal disorders'; narrowed to specify lysosomal storage disease scope rather than skeletal focus.

name: Non-coding RNA processing and modification
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; no collision detected.

name: Nucleotide excision repair
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere; members are dominated by nucleotide-excision repair and GG-NER processes, distinguishing it from the broader sibling theme 'DNA repair'.

name: Circadian and light-responsive signalling
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no other theme addresses circadian rhythm or light-responsive signalling.

name: Glutamatergic excitatory synapse organization and signaling
rationale: Covers the child (excitatory postsynaptic assembly) plus direct members on glutamatergic transmission, receptor clustering, adhesion molecules and trans-synaptic/EPSP regulation; tighter than generic 'synaptic signaling' since all members concern excitatory glutamatergic synapses.

name: Membrane excitability and ion channel regulation
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; covers general membrane excitability/ion channel regulation, not specific to cardiac context like the siblings.

name: Systemic fluid balance regulation
rationale: Too close to parent themes covering vasopressin and aquaporin water transport mechanisms; renamed to emphasize whole-body regulatory outcome, distinguishing it from the molecular mechanism parents and the cellular-level sibling.

name: Regulation of cardiac membrane excitability
rationale: Union covers the child (cardiac repolarization) plus membrane depolarization regulation and cardiac action-potential/conduction communication; the AV-node communication member is weakly included (0.27) but fits the same excitability theme.

name: Dietary sugar and glycogen metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; it specifically covers dietary sugars and glycogen metabolism, unlike hexose transport or polyol/pentose metabolism.

name: Deoxyribonucleotide metabolism and catabolism
rationale: Nearly identical to parent name and overlaps both siblings which cover general nucleotide/purine salvage; this theme's members are specifically deoxyribonucleotide (dNMP/dNTP) metabolism and catabolism, distinguishing it.

name: Skeletal and dental mineralization and morphogenesis
rationale: Covers the child's chondrocyte/osteoblast differentiation plus direct members on bone mineralization, skeletal morphogenesis, cementum mineralization and odontoblast differentiation, spanning both skeletal and dental hard-tissue formation without over-generalizing to all skeletal biology.

The single child theme already spans EMT, terminal secretory maturation, and ERBB2-EGFR signalling, so the parent would just restate that one child's name rather than offer a tighter or genuinely broader umbrella.

name: Sex hormone biosynthesis and differentiation
rationale: Repeated 'steroid hormone' from both parent themes; narrowing to sex hormone biosynthesis and differentiation distinguishes it as a specific downstream process rather than general steroid metabolism/secretion.

name: Adrenal and gonadal steroid hormone synthesis
rationale: Members cover androgen and estrogen biosynthesis, adrenal cortisol synthesis defects (CYP11B1, CYP21A2), and male sex differentiation driven by androgen/AMH signalling, all rooted in steroidogenesis from cholesterol precursors. The weakly included negative regulation of glucocorticoid biosynthesis (0.27) is excluded as it concerns restraint rather than synthesis itself.

name: Branched-chain amino acid and mitochondrial alpha-keto acid catabolism disorders
rationale: Core members (MMAA/MMA, DBT/MSUD2, MSUD, DLD/MSUD3, MCC deficiency) are inborn errors of branched-chain amino acid and propionate/methylmalonate catabolism converging on mitochondrial alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase and related cofactor-dependent enzymes; weaker members (protein lipoylation, 2-oxoglutarate/2-hydroxyglutarate interconversion) share the cofactor/enzyme machinery but are more peripheral.

name: Sensory receptor signaling mechanisms
rationale: Name is identical to a sibling theme; narrowed to focus on receptor signaling mechanisms distinct from organ development sibling.

name: Actin-driven membrane ruffling and pathogen entry
rationale: Covers the Arp2/3 lamellipodium child plus macropinocytosis, ruffle assembly, and Listeria internalization, all of which use actin-driven membrane ruffling to engulf fluid or invading bacteria; narrower terms like 'actin nucleation' alone would miss the pathogen-entry members.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint regulation
rationale: Repeated/broader than parent 'Chromosome segregation checkpoint control'; narrowed to focus on cell cycle checkpoint regulation, distinct from sibling's meiosis and fertilisation focus.

name: Cadherin-mediated adhesion and EMT
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically identifies cadherin-mediated adhesion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, not covered by the sibling's broader junction organization scope.

name: Proteoglycan and glycosaminoglycan metabolism
rationale: Current name closely repeats the parent's 'glycoprotein and proteoglycan glycosylation' and overlaps with the sibling's glycan metabolism theme; the members are specifically GAG/proteoglycan synthesis and degradation, which distinguishes it.

name: tRNA and rRNA processing and modification
rationale: Members are dominated by tRNA/snoRNA/snRNA modification and processing events plus mitochondrial translation; the current name asserts a broad 'nuclear and mitochondrial gene expression machinery' scope not well supported, and could overlap with sibling's translation focus. Renaming to reflect the RNA processing/modification theme keeps it distinct from 'Cytoplasmic translation' while remaining true to all members.

name: Chromatin condensation and cohesion establishment
rationale: The current name's cohesion component also fits the sibling 'Chromatin-associated genome stability maintenance', whose members are all sister chromatid cohesion maintenance; narrowing to condensation and establishment (not maintenance) distinguishes it.

name: Mitochondrial DNA replication and repair
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Mitochondrial gene expression' and overlapping with sibling's gene expression scope; renaming to focus on genome maintenance aspect (replication/repair) distinguishes it from both.

name: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulation
rationale: All members concern control of HPA-axis hormone output—corticotropin, glucocorticoid, or steroid hormone secretion/synthesis, including growth-axis and adrenal enzyme defects that feed into this endocrine regulation.

name: Meiosis and gametogenesis
rationale: Name collides with another theme elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to emphasize meiotic recombination and division processes central to this theme's members.

name: Excitatory postsynaptic assembly
rationale: All three concern building and organizing the postsynaptic density and specialization at excitatory (glutamatergic) synapses via trans-synaptic adhesion and scaffold proteins.

name: Selective autophagy of organelles
rationale: Covers mitophagy (child) plus macroautophagy, autophagosome maturation and pexophagy, all forms of organelle-targeted autophagic clearance; broader terms like 'autophagy' alone would miss the organelle-selective focus shared here.

name: Protein modification and hemostatic regulation
rationale: The children cover clot formation/dissolution (Hemostasis) and regulated proteolysis, while the direct members add post-translational modification and adhesion regulation that underlie these processes; the umbrella spans protein modification and its role in hemostatic control without broadening to all signalling or metabolism.

name: Neural plate and axial mesoderm patterning
rationale: The original name broadly described axis formation, which also fits the sibling 'Early mesoderm formation and axial segmentation' (gastrulation, axis specification). This theme's members center on neural plate, midbrain-hindbrain boundary, and axial mesoderm formation, which the sibling's members do not cover.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation
rationale: Parent 'Meiotic division machinery' concerns meiosis; current name conflates mitosis with cytokinesis, an unrelated process, so narrowing to chromosome segregation clarifies distinction.

name: Mesenchymal fat versus bone lineage commitment
rationale: The child (adipocyte differentiation and lipid storage) and direct members (fat cell differentiation regulation, adipose tissue development, osteoblast differentiation) together describe the reciprocal commitment of mesenchymal progenitors to adipocyte versus osteoblast fates and the resulting lipid-storage phenotype; broader terms like 'metabolism' would not capture the shared progenitor-commitment theme.

name: RhoA GTP-GDP cycling
rationale: Repeated parent 'GTPase cycle regulation by GAPs and GEFs' concept and overlapped with sibling 'Small GTPase signalling regulation'; specifying RhoA nucleotide cycling distinguishes it.

name: Phosphate and inositol phosphate metabolism
rationale: Duplicated an existing theme name elsewhere; this theme's members center on GTP/phosphate and inositol phosphate synthesis, distinct from the sibling's nucleotide/pyrimidine focus.

name: Nuclear RNA biogenesis and nucleocytoplasmic transport
rationale: All children and members concern the life cycle of RNA and associated machinery from nuclear transcription/processing through ribosome assembly to transport across the nuclear envelope; broad enough to unite transcription termination/decay, RNA/protein nuclear transport, and ribosome biogenesis without invoking unrelated cytoplasmic biology.

name: Genome maintenance and transcriptional control of proliferation
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling, which focus on gene expression, RNA/protein trafficking, and biogenesis machinery, while this theme covers genome maintenance and proliferation control.

name: Lymphocyte effector cytokine secretion regulation
rationale: Too similar to 'Lymphocyte cytotoxicity and antigen-driven activation' and 'T cell activation and differentiation'; narrowing to cytokine secretion output distinguishes it from activation and cytotoxicity-focused siblings.

name: CD8 T cell differentiation and activation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'TCR signaling and general T cell activation' and siblings which cover CD4 subsets; narrowing to CD8 T cells distinguishes it.

name: Spindle assembly and cytokinetic apparatus
rationale: Nearly duplicated sibling 'Mitotic spindle positioning and cytokinesis'; renamed to emphasize structural assembly/machinery components rather than positioning regulation.

name: Calcium-mediated contraction control
rationale: Repeated parent 'Muscle contraction' too closely; renamed to specify the calcium-signalling mechanism regulating contraction, distinguishing it from potassium homeostasis aspects of the parent.

name: General skeletal muscle contraction and regulation
rationale: Name overlapped closely with parent's 'General muscle contraction and ion homeostasis'; specifying skeletal/general muscle distinguishes it from the smooth muscle sibling and parent.

name: Amino acid transmembrane transport
rationale: All members concern carrier-mediated movement of L-amino acids (glutamate, aspartate, and amino acids generally) across plasma and organellar membranes.

name: Positive regulation of DNA binding and RNA polymerase II transcription
rationale: All members concern upstream control of transcription factor DNA binding or positive regulation of RNA polymerase II-driven transcription/RNA output, converging on the same preinitiation and activator machinery.

name: Th17 and Treg lineage commitment
rationale: Repeated parent scope (CD4 T-helper subset differentiation / Th1/Th2 differentiation) without adding specificity; renamed to reflect the distinct subset lineages it covers.

name: Calcineurin-NFAT hypertrophic signaling
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Muscle contraction and calcium regulation' in calcium theme; narrowed to specific calcium-dependent hypertrophy pathway distinct from contraction/coupling siblings.

name: Synaptic vesicle trafficking and recycling
rationale: Union of the vesicle trafficking/fusion child with synaptic vesicle recycling via endosome, presynaptic endocytosis, and RAB geranylgeranylation (weak, 0.36, supporting Rab-dependent membrane traffic) converges on the presynaptic vesicle cycle as an addition to general trafficking.

name: Negative regulation of ion transport
rationale: The child (cardiac repolarization) is one instance of damping ion/potassium flux, and the direct members generalize this to negative regulation of ion transmembrane transport broadly, including non-cardiac transport; naming stops short of positive regulation, which is absent.

name: Unfolded protein response and ER stress signaling
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent name 'Stress-induced translational control and proteostasis'; members specifically concern UPR/ER stress regulation (IRE1, PERK), distinguishing from sibling's eIF2α/integrated stress response focus.

name: Ras GTPase effector signaling
rationale: Repeats parent 'Ras GTPase signal transduction' too closely and overlaps with sibling 'Small GTPase-driven cytoskeletal signalling'; renamed to specify Ras-specific downstream effector pathways distinct from cytoskeletal signalling.

name: Telomere length regulation and protein recruitment
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than the parent (which covers genome instability broadly, not telomere length regulation/protein recruitment specifically).

name: Dermal collagen matrix formation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Cornified envelope formation and keratinization' via shared 'keratinization' term; narrowing to the collagen matrix aspect distinguishes it.

name: Keratinization and collagen matrix assembly
rationale: The theme spans two structural biology strands: cornification/keratinization of epidermis (keratinization, cornified envelope formation, intermediate filament organization) and collagen biosynthesis/assembly (collagen formation, chain trimerization). All members at or above 0.5 inclusion fit one of these two structural protein assembly processes, so both are named rather than one being dropped.

name: Negative regulation of protein turnover and localization
rationale: The child covers ubiquitin-proteasome control of cell cycle and p53; direct members add PTEN localization control, AKT1 constitutive signaling, and nuclear export restraint. All share regulatory control over protein stability, activity, or subcellular localization via post-translational modification, broader than the child's cell-cycle/p53 focus but not a generic 'signalling' label.

name: Protein and small-molecule post-translational modification
rationale: Direct members span protein PTM machinery (post-translational protein modification, peptidyl-amino acid modification, NOS3-mediated nitric oxide regulation) while the unnamed child's samples concern polyamine biosynthesis, metabolism and transport; the smallest honest umbrella is biosynthesis and modification of small nitrogenous/protein biomolecules, though the union is heterogeneous enough that this label is a stretch.

name: Ras GTPase signal transduction
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Small GTPase cycle regulation' and 'Rho GTPase signalling'; narrowing to the Ras subfamily distinguishes it.

name: Cytokine and TNF activation of non-canonical NF-kB
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Non-canonical NF-kB signaling' without adding specificity; revised name clarifies the specific inputs driving the non-canonical pathway.

name: Regulation of lipid and ketone metabolism
rationale: Covers the child (upregulation of lipid biosynthesis) and direct members regulating ketone and fatty acid metabolism, including the weakly-included negative regulation of lipid biosynthesis; broader than any single direction of control but tied to lipid/ketone metabolic regulation specifically.

name: Chemokine-driven leukocyte trafficking
rationale: Covers CCR7-dependent dendritic cell trafficking, the chemokine cluster and chemokine receptor-ligand binding, all centered on chemokine-directed immune cell migration; the weakly included PGE2 response member (0.32) also feeds into this same CCR7/chemokine homing axis.

name: Homologous recombination strand invasion
rationale: Name repeated the broader parent scope 'Homologous recombination repair' instead of naming its specific sub-process; narrowed to distinguish from sibling 'Mismatch repair and homologous recombination synthesis'.

Members mix unrelated biology—nucleotide/purine membrane transport, blood-brain barrier junction regulation and drug transport, microRNA-mediated drug resistance—sharing only a loose theme of transport/barrier regulation too broad and heterogeneous to name tightly.

name: Alarmin-driven neutrophil and type 2 inflammatory signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader IL-1/TNF signaling) and sibling (IL-1-driven leukocyte recruitment); this theme specifically covers alarmin-driven neutrophil and type 2 inflammation pathways.

name: Coagulation factor defects and cascade regulation
rationale: Overlapped parent 'Coagulation cascade initiation and propagation' and included platelet-mediated language that duplicates the sibling 'Platelet activation, adhesion and degranulation'; revised to emphasize the coagulation factor defect content unique to this theme.

name: Cadherin-based adhesion dynamics
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically about cadherin-mediated adhesion rather than general adhesion/junction biology.

name: Electron transport chain complex regulation
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'Mitochondrial respiration and redox homeostasis'; narrowed to focus on regulation of respiratory chain complexes themselves rather than broader redox homeostasis.

name: Spindle assembly checkpoint signaling
rationale: Overlaps heavily with parent 'Spindle assembly checkpoint regulation' and sibling 'Kinetochore-microtubule attachment regulation'; narrowing to checkpoint signaling mechanisms distinguishes it from attachment regulation and mitotic exit.

name: IL-1-driven inflammatory response
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and name is distinct from parents (leukocyte recruitment vs general inflammatory response; more specific than cytokine receptor pathways).

name: Mismatch repair coupled recombination
rationale: Overlaps parent name 'Homologous recombination repair'; renamed to emphasize mismatch repair-recombination crosstalk, distinguishing it from both the parent and the sibling 'DNA damage response'.

name: Base excision repair, AP site formation and depyrimidination
rationale: Repeats the parent name exactly with no added specificity; revised to reflect the actual member processes (AP site formation, depyrimidination, glycosylase recognition) while remaining true to all members.

name: Kinetochore-microtubule attachment regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically addresses kinetochore-microtubule attachment, not condensation or overall segregation fidelity.

name: Kinetochore-microtubule attachment regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader fidelity concept) and sibling (checkpoint control vs. attachment regulation); no collision.

name: Kinetochore-microtubule attachment regulation
rationale: All four members concern regulation (or positive regulation) of spindle microtubule attachment to kinetochores and metaphase plate congression, centered on the chromosomal passenger complex and CDK1 activity.

name: Insulin signalling to glucose uptake
rationale: Distinct from parents and siblings; specifically about insulin-driven glucose uptake, unlike broader metabolic, beta cell, adipocyte, or RTK themes.

name: Oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase mutants and fusions
rationale: Covers both drug-resistant RTK point mutants and constitutively active PDGFRA/PDGFRB/ALK fusion or resistant forms, unified by ligand-independent RTK activation in cancer, broader than the resistance-only child but not extending to normal RTK signalling.

name: Steroid and vitamin D hormone metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parents (which emphasize hydroxylation and biosynthesis pathways) and from the sibling (secretion regulation); this theme focuses on metabolism of steroid and vitamin D hormones specifically.

name: Smooth muscle contraction regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (which focuses on overall vascular tone/BP) and sibling (angiotensin-specific signaling); this theme is specifically about smooth muscle contraction mechanisms.

name: Skeletal development and mineralization control
rationale: Both children (osteoclast-mediated bone remodeling regulation, skeletal/dental mineralization) plus direct members concern building and tuning cartilage/bone tissue: chondrocyte and skeletal maturation, matrix glycoprotein production supporting cartilage/bone matrix, and mineralization regulation. 'Anatomical structure maturation' (0.26) is weakly included and not required to fit precisely.

name: Small nuclear and nucleolar RNA processing and modification
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent by naming the RNA class (snRNA/snoRNA), so it is already distinct.

name: Dopaminergic modulation of locomotor behavior
rationale: Already distinguishes itself from parent by naming dopamine specifically and locomotion, and from siblings by focusing on locomotor behavior rather than general behavioral regulation or circuit-level control.

name: Vesicle transport and organelle positioning
rationale: The child covers vesicle traffic to the vacuole/lysosome; the direct members add cytoskeleton-based vesicle movement and organelle localization more generally, so the umbrella must extend beyond vesicle-to-organelle delivery to include organelle positioning itself.

name: Lipoprotein particle assembly and clearance
rationale: Near-duplicate of sibling 'Triglyceride and lipoprotein particle metabolism' which shares the same core members; renamed to emphasize assembly and clearance processes distinguishing this theme.

name: Inositol phosphate metabolism and signalling
rationale: No parent to repeat, and it is distinct from its sibling 'Phosphoinositide and phosphatase signalling'.

name: Epidermal wound healing and keratinocyte migration
rationale: Sibling 'Actin-based adhesion and migration dynamics' shares the same adhesion/migration theme and members; this theme's distinguishing focus is epidermal wound healing and keratinocyte-specific migration.

name: Renal amino acid reabsorption and transport
rationale: All members concern amino acid transport across epithelia, dominated by proximal tubule reabsorption (cystinuria via SLC3A1/SLC7A9, iminoglycinuria via SLC36A2, proline/glycine transport), with the broader amino acid metabolism/transport member also centered on liver and kidney handling.

name: Apical junction and adhesion organization
rationale: Repeats parent name 'Cell-cell junction organization and assembly' nearly verbatim, giving no added specificity; revised to reflect apical junction assembly and EMT-related adhesion members.

name: B lymphocyte development and antibody diversification
rationale: All members at inclusion ≥0.5 concern B cell developmental stages (pro-B, pre-B) or the immunoglobulin diversification machinery (V(D)J recombination, class switching, somatic hypermutation) that generates antibody diversity and regulates its production; the weakly included classical NHEJ pathway (0.27) is excluded as a general DNA repair mechanism not specific to B cells.

name: Antigen presentation and immune receptor modulation
rationale: Covers both children: MHC-based antigen presentation/T cell response and Nef-mediated downregulation of immune receptors (MHC, CD4) at the presenting/target cell surface; no direct members exist to broaden further.

name: LDL and VLDL particle remodeling
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'HDL and plasma lipoprotein remodeling'; narrowed to the non-HDL lipoprotein classes to distinguish it.

name: HDL reverse cholesterol transport
