rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Lipoprotein remodeling and transfer' and sibling 'Plasma lipoprotein particle remodeling'; narrowing to HDL's specific role in reverse cholesterol transport distinguishes it.

name: Smooth and striated muscle contraction
rationale: Sibling 'Muscle contraction and calcium cycling' shares the same generic top members (muscle system process, muscle contraction, regulation of muscle contraction), making 'Muscle contraction regulation' equally applicable to it; this theme's distinguishing content is smooth and striated muscle specific contraction terms.

name: Arp2/3-mediated actin nucleation and lamellipodium formation
rationale: All members concern branched actin nucleation (largely Arp2/3-dependent) and its regulation in building or restraining lamellipodial protrusions; the weakly included regulation of actin filament organization (0.39) is broader but still centers on the same nucleation/branching machinery.

name: Translation and protein biosynthesis
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Transcription and RNA processing machinery' by including gene expression/transcription language; renaming to focus on translation distinguishes it from the parent and from the sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and nuclear RNA processing'.

name: Amino acid and GABA membrane transport
rationale: Both children cover amino acid (and bile acid) membrane transport, and the direct members add GABA-specific secretion and transport; the umbrella must span amino acid/bile acid solutes plus GABA handling without invoking neurotransmission generally.

name: E2F-driven cell cycle regulation
rationale: The sibling 'Cell cycle phase transitions and checkpoints' shares G1/S and G2/M checkpoint members, making the current name equally applicable there; this theme's distinguishing feature is E2F target gene regulation and broader mitotic cell cycle control.

name: Death receptor complex assembly regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'NF-kB signalling and inflammatory apoptosis' on NF-kB and apoptosis themes; narrowed to the death receptor complex assembly/regulation aspect that distinguishes this theme.

name: Transcription-coupled NER pathway
rationale: The current name simply restates the general repair topic shared by both parents; the sibling 'Global genome NER pathway' shows this theme covers the complementary transcription-coupled branch of nucleotide excision repair, which is more specific and distinguishing.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression and tRNA maturation
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers coordination between mitochondrial and nuclear expression broadly) and sibling (which covers general expression machinery); this theme specifically addresses mitochondrial gene expression and tRNA maturation.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression and tRNA modification
rationale: All members concern maturation/modification of tRNAs (including threonylcarbamoyladenosine installation) or regulation of mitochondrial transcription/translation, both converging on translational fidelity for oxidative phosphorylation.

name: microRNA biogenesis, stability and turnover
rationale: The child covers miRNA biogenesis/silencing; the direct members add regulation of miRNA catabolism (0.96) and of 3'-UTR-mediated mRNA stabilization, i.e. post-maturation control of transcript and miRNA turnover. The low-inclusion kinase-activity member (0.27) is excluded as it falls below threshold and is not specific to this biology.

name: microRNA biogenesis and silencing
rationale: Name is not identical to parent and includes biogenesis, which parent lacks; no siblings to conflict with.

name: Cytosolic innate immune sensing and inflammasome activation
rationale: Distinct from parent (parent is broader, covers general inflammatory mediator production) and sibling (nucleic acid sensing/antiviral vs inflammasome activation).

name: Lipid storage and transport metabolism
rationale: All children and direct members concern storage, transport, or regulation of lipids (bile acids, cholesterol/HDL, dietary lipids, triglycerides, ketones) including the bile acid transport and lipoprotein signalling direct members; broader terms like 'metabolism' alone would be too vague, but the union is unified by lipid handling rather than any single lipid class or organelle.

name: Histone methylation and heterochromatin regulation
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Chromatin and epigenetic gene regulation' which shares the same core members (chromatin organization, epigenetic regulation of gene expression); the distinguishing members here are histone demethylation, methylation, and heterochromatin organization.
The single child, Hemostasis and coagulation, already covers the full scope of these members; no tighter or genuinely broader umbrella term exists that isn't just a restatement of that child.

name: Dystroglycanopathy pathways
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Protein glycosylation and glycosylation disorders' and sibling 'Protein glycosylation'; narrowed to the specific dystroglycan-related disorder focus.

name: Congenital disorders of glycosylation
rationale: All three concern inherited defects in protein glycosylation (N-linked, O-linked, and dystroglycan matriglycan assembly) that disrupt glycan-dependent cell and matrix functions.

name: Mitochondrial translation
rationale: Two members explicitly describe mitochondrial protein synthesis machinery; the broader 'Translation' pathway is included but its distinctive shared content with the others is the mitochondrial translation system, so the tighter name reflects the common core rather than the full cytosolic translation apparatus described only in that one member.

name: Myeloid phagocyte effector function
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; it specifically denotes cellular (myeloid phagocyte) effector function versus humoral/complement effectors.

name: Glutamatergic synaptic plasticity
rationale: All members centre on excitatory glutamate receptor signalling (NMDA/AMPA) and its downstream effects on postsynaptic organization and long-term synaptic strengthening, including the weakly included AMPA receptor pathway (0.27).

name: mRNA surveillance and decay
rationale: Repeated parent name 'Ribosome biogenesis' and overlapped with sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and RNA processing'; narrowing to mRNA surveillance/decay distinguishes it as the NMD/quality-control focus rather than ribosome assembly.

name: Myeloid transcriptional differentiation and platelet formation
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to specify transcriptional regulation and platelet/megakaryocyte outputs, distinguishing it from hematopoietic lineage siblings.

name: Glomerular endothelial vasculature development
rationale: Overlapped with parent's vascular scope and sibling's capillary focus; narrowed to endothelial-specific vasculature to distinguish from mesangial cell and capillary development sibling.

name: Nucleotide excision repair
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; members focus on NER and UV damage repair, distinguishing it from the sibling's strand-break and crosslink repair.

name: Hedgehog signaling
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Wnt signaling' by including Wnt; splitting into Hedgehog-only distinguishes it clearly.

name: Sensory organ development
rationale: Overlapped with parent term 'development' and duplicate siblings covering perception/receptor biology; narrowing to organ development distinguishes this theme.

name: Meiotic spindle and cytokinesis in gametogenesis
rationale: Adds spindle assembly and cytokinesis events completing meiotic division, beyond the recombination/pairing focus of the child; the weakly included negative regulation of reproductive process (0.25) is excluded.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase and phosphoinositide signalling
rationale: Covers PI3K/AKT signalling, ALK and LTK receptor tyrosine kinase signalling (which converge on PI3K/RAS pathways), and general phosphatidylinositol-mediated signalling; broader than the single child but still specific to receptor-driven phosphoinositide/RTK cascades rather than signalling generally.

name: Type I interferon signaling and RIG-I pathway regulation
rationale: The original name overlapped with sibling 'Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing and interferon induction', which also concerns cytosolic sensing and interferon; the revised name reflects this theme's specific focus on IFN signaling regulation and RIG-I/IRF3 pathway activation.

name: rRNA and small RNA modification
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'rRNA and mitochondrial ribosome biogenesis' and echoed the parent's rRNA/snoRNP focus; the members actually span rRNA, tRNA, and snRNA chemical modifications rather than ribosome assembly, which distinguishes it from both siblings.

name: Monosaccharide and amino sugar catabolism
rationale: The child covers galactose/pentose disorders while direct members cover catabolism and phosphorylation of sialic acid, amino sugars, glucosamine derivatives and glycosides, all monosaccharide/amino-sugar breakdown pathways feeding central carbohydrate metabolism.

name: Lipid droplet storage and turnover
rationale: Members focus on lipid droplet formation, lipophagy and phospholipid/triglyceride biosynthesis rather than glucose storage; also better separates from 'Lipid and energy metabolic homeostasis' sibling which covers lipoprotein/cholesterol handling.

name: Vitamin absorption and transport
rationale: Folic acid, riboflavin, vitamin B12 and vitamin E members all concern dietary vitamin uptake and delivery; fatty acid alpha-oxidation (0.47, weakly included) is only loosely tied via peroxisomal metabolism and not vitamin handling.

name: Gonadotropin secretion and action
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; focuses specifically on gonadotropin secretion and action rather than general hypothalamic-pituitary hormones or HPA axis hormones.

name: Sensory perception
rationale: Both children are subtypes of sensory perception and there are no direct members beyond them, so the parent is simply the general sensory perception category encompassing all modalities.

name: Ventricular wall growth and trabeculation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Cardiac chamber and vasculature morphogenesis'; narrowed to the specific growth process of ventricular wall thickening and trabeculation.

name: DNA damage response and repair
rationale: All children and sampled members concern detection and repair of DNA lesions—double-strand breaks, single-strand breaks, base excision and mitotic recombination control—broader than either named child but still restricted to genome repair rather than replication or damage signalling in general.

name: SARS-CoV-2 receptor entry mechanisms
rationale: Repeated both parents' phrasing ('virus-host interactions' and 'entry'); narrowing to SARS-CoV-2-specific receptor binding/entry distinguishes it from siblings focused on replication and assembly.

name: SARS-CoV-2 and dengue host interactions
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Viral entry, replication and host infection' which also covers entry/replication broadly; the theme's actual members are specifically about SARS-CoV-2/dengue infection and coronavirus protein maturation, so naming it after those specific viruses distinguishes it.

name: Osmotic and water balance response
rationale: Covers water/polyol channel transport, osmotic and salt stress adaptation, and the direct member response to hydrostatic pressure, all concerning cellular sensing and adaptation to fluid/tonicity changes.

name: Endoderm-derived epithelial differentiation
rationale: No siblings present, and name is distinct from parents which focus on fate specification and organ morphogenetic patterning rather than differentiation.

name: MITF-M target gene programmes
rationale: No collision with parent (none) or sibling 'Methylation'; name is already specific and distinct.

name: DNA polymerase-mediated repair synthesis
rationale: Nearly repeats parent name 'DNA replication and repair synthesis'; distinguishing from sibling (origin licensing) requires specifying the synthesis mechanism rather than repeating the parent's scope.

name: Nephron segment and collecting system development
rationale: Covers the child (collecting duct/tubule development) plus distal tubule, distal convoluted tubule, ureter, metanephric nephron epithelium and glomerulus development members, all being components of nephron/urinary tract patterning in kidney development.

name: Death receptor apoptosis signaling regulation
rationale: Overlaps with 'NF-kB and death receptor signalling in inflammation'; narrowed to focus specifically on apoptotic signaling cascade regulation rather than NF-kB/inflammatory outputs.

name: Meiotic chromosome pairing and recombination
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Germline meiosis and gametogenesis' which also covers oocyte differentiation and reproductive processes; narrowing to chromosome pairing/recombination distinguishes this theme's focus from the broader gametogenesis sibling.

name: Protein folding and turnover
rationale: Both children concern maintaining a functional proteome: one via proteolytic maturation/degradation, the other via folding and clearance of misfolded or aggregated protein, together spanning protein quality control from synthesis to turnover.

name: Coagulation factor activation
rationale: Too broad and overlapping with parent 'Coagulation cascade regulation' and siblings like fibrinolysis/platelet activation; narrowed to the specific clot-forming factor activation process.

name: Endothelial cell response to shear and hypoxia
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Vascular response to injury and hypoxia' and 'Vascular tone and blood pressure regulation'; narrowed to endothelial-specific mechanosensory/hypoxic stress response to distinguish from those siblings.

name: Regulation of ER stress and unfolded protein response
rationale: The name's nutrient sensing claim is unsupported by members and overlaps with sibling 'Cellular stress response and nutrient sensing'; members specifically concern UPR/PERK/IRE1 regulation, distinguishing it from the broader stress-response siblings.

name: Small GTPase-driven cytoskeletal and adhesion signalling
rationale: Both children converge on Rho/Ras-family GTPase switches controlling actin dynamics, adhesion and migration; no direct members extend beyond this scope.

name: Vascular injury response and repair
rationale: Both children concern the tissue-level response to vascular/tissue damage—clot formation and its factor-based regulation, and the subsequent repair, remodelling and inflammatory tissue healing—so the umbrella is the injury-to-repair continuum rather than coagulation or fibrosis alone.

name: Cardiac conduction system electrophysiology
rationale: No siblings and distinct from both parents, which cover development and ion channel modulation specifically.

name: Sensory perception, development and receptor biology
rationale: No parent to repeat, and no sibling covers sensory perception, development and receptor biology jointly; sufficiently distinct.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation fidelity
rationale: Distinct from parent (fidelity/checkpoint aspect vs general segregation) and sibling (cytokinesis); no collision.

name: CCR7-mediated dendritic cell and lymphocyte chemotaxis
rationale: No siblings present and name is distinct from parent, which covers leukocyte transendothelial migration generally while this specifies CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of dendritic cells and lymphocytes.

name: Chromosome segregation in mitosis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitotic cell division machinery'; renamed to emphasize chromosome segregation specifically, distinguishing it from the general machinery sibling.

name: Branched-chain amino acid and GABA catabolism
rationale: Sibling 'Urea cycle and mitochondrial shuttle transport' also includes the malate-aspartate shuttle, so 'carbon shuttling' overlaps; the distinguishing content here is branched-chain amino acid/GABA degradation and lipoylation defects.

name: Cardiac conduction system excitability
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Cardiac action potential regulation' and parent 'Cardiac ion channel regulation'; narrowed to conduction system-specific excitability.

name: Neuronal projection morphogenesis and growth regulation
rationale: The current name overlaps with sibling 'Axon guidance signalling' since it also contains axon guidance and ephrin/Roundabout pathways; renaming to emphasize neuron projection/cell growth regulation (its distinct members) separates it from the axon guidance sibling.

name: Carbohydrate transport and glycogen storage disorders
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Carbohydrate metabolism disorders', which shares the same disorder members; this name emphasizes the transport and glycogen-specific aspects unique to this theme.

name: RNA polymerase III transcription and spliceosome assembly
rationale: Most members concern either RNA polymerase III machinery (transcription, termination, abortive initiation, 5S rRNA transcription) or early spliceosome/splice-site recognition steps (3'-splice site recognition, U2-type prespliceosome assembly); mitochondrial RNA catabolism regulation (0.85) and 3'-5' exoribonuclease decay (0.29) are excluded as they concern RNA turnover rather than transcription or splicing.

name: Dendritic spine and postsynaptic structural plasticity
rationale: Distinct from parent (LTP signalling) and sibling (glutamate receptor signalling); focuses specifically on structural remodeling of spines/postsynapse rather than signalling cascades.

name: Contractile and wound-healing remodeling programs
rationale: Covers the SRF-driven contractile/matrix child plus direct members on inflammatory and vascular wound healing and UV-response downregulated genes, all converging on tissue remodeling/repair; broader than 'SRF targets' but narrower than general signalling.

One child concerns androgen receptor signalling while the other spans steroid conjugation/excretion and unrelated Y-chromosome dosage biology, sharing no coherent theme beyond generic hormone/genetics topics.

name: Myogenic differentiation and regeneration
rationale: All members concern skeletal muscle myoblast/myotube differentiation, its negative regulation, fusion, and regeneration; the broader 'regeneration' member (0.57) is included since it centers on satellite-cell myogenesis.

name: Ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation
rationale: All members involve ubiquitin or ubiquitin-like (NEDD8) tagging of substrates via E1-E2-E3 enzymes leading to proteasomal or other proteolytic destruction, controlling protein turnover.

name: Ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation
rationale: All members concern ubiquitin (or NEDD8) tagging of substrates via E1/E2/E3 enzymes, primarily targeting proteins for proteasomal degradation, including K48 chains, polyubiquitination, neddylation activation of cullin-RING ligases, and the downstream proteolysis; the broader post-translational modification member is included as it centers on the same ubiquitin machinery.

name: Germ layer patterning and cell fate commitment
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than the parent, distinguishing itself as germ layer/fate commitment rather than general organ patterning.

name: Ion channel modulation of cardiac potentials
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Cardiac action potential dynamics'; narrowed to focus on ion channel-based regulatory mechanisms, distinguishing it from siblings covering broader electrophysiology and coupling.

name: Neuromodulatory control of behaviour and movement
rationale: Both children (reward circuitry, locomotor/exploratory circuits) plus the direct members (general behaviour, response to amine, NGF-stimulated transcription) share neuromodulator-driven (dopamine, amine, neurotrophic) signalling shaping behavioural and locomotor output; broader terms like 'signalling' would lose the behavioural focus, while a narrower term would exclude the general behaviour or NGF member.

name: Transcriptional and microRNA regulation of cadherin and TGF-beta receptor expression
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no other theme addresses cadherin/TGF-beta receptor expression regulation by transcription factors and microRNAs.

name: DNA methylation and chromatin marks
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Chromatin and epigenetic regulation'; narrowed to specify methylation and histone/chromatin marks as distinct from broader epigenetic regulation and from nuclear gene expression machinery sibling.

name: Regulation of kinase phosphorylation activity
rationale: Repeats the parent name; members include broader phosphorylation and serine/threonine kinase regulation beyond MAPK specifically, so a more general phrasing better fits all members while differing from the parent.

name: Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis, degradation and related disorders
rationale: Both children cover glycosaminoglycan metabolism and its associated diseases; the direct member (SLCO2A1/PHOAR2) is itself a GAG-related metabolic disease, so the union stays within this scope without broadening further.

name: Lysosomal glycan catabolism
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Glycan and glycolipid biosynthesis and degradation'; narrowed to lysosomal catabolic focus, distinguishing it from sibling dolichol/GPI biosynthesis pathway.

name: Apoptotic signalling and its regulation
rationale: All members converge on triggering, restraining or executing programmed cell death (mitochondrial permeabilization, calcium and membrane potential control, death-receptor and stress-induced apoptosis), broader than the mitochondrial-apoptosis child but not extending to unrelated cellular processes.

name: Polyol and pentose sugar metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parents and siblings; no other sibling covers polyol pathway or pentose sugar metabolism.

name: microRNA biogenesis and silencing
rationale: All members center on miRNA maturation (Drosha/DGCR8, Dicer) and Argonaute-mediated silencing, with regulatory brakes on processing; the ncRNA and gene-silencing-by-RNA entries also include piRNA/tRNA-fragment branches as secondary content within the same core biogenesis-silencing framework.

name: Neutral amino acid membrane transport
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Amino acid and GABA membrane transport' and sibling 'Amino acid and bile acid membrane transport'; narrowing to the neutral amino acid transporters distinguishes it from both.

name: Cell cycle regulation and genome stability
rationale: Covers all children (DNA repair, chromatin/mitotic dynamics, cell cycle progression and machinery, telomere/senescence, and turnover/death regulation) plus the direct members, which are minor regulatory processes (nuclear export, ADP-ribosylation, p53 methylation) tied to cell-cycle and genome-maintenance control.

name: Nucleoside/nucleotide transporter function
rationale: Overlaps parents 'Nucleotide and phosphate group metabolism' and sibling 'Nucleotide and phosphate metabolism and transport'; narrowing to transporter-specific function distinguishes it.

name: Platelet adhesion, hemostasis and protein modification
rationale: Covers both children (cell adhesion/hemostasis and platelet adhesion signalling) plus the direct members on post-translational/peptidyl-amino acid modification, which are not covered by either child; a narrower umbrella would omit the modification members.

name: Lens fiber cell differentiation
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no parent to collide with.

name: Lens fiber cell differentiation
rationale: All four members describe the lens fiber differentiation programme itself or its positive/negative regulation.

name: Telomere-driven genome instability
rationale: Repeats 'Telomere maintenance' and 'genome stability' from parent names; revised to specify the causal link between telomere dysfunction and genomic instability, distinguishing it from p53-driven senescence.

The three high-confidence Reactome members concern erythrocyte membrane transporters (RHAG, SLC4A1/Band 3) and blood group antigen biosynthesis, while the GO/Hallmark members concern epithelial membrane polarity (apical surface proteins, basolateral secretion, raft partitioning). These are two distinct biologies—red cell membrane/antigen physiology versus epithelial protein sorting—with no shared mechanism beyond both involving membrane proteins, so no single non-invented name covers all members.

name: Unfolded protein response and ER stress signalling
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere in the hierarchy; members are specifically about ER stress, UPR (IRE1/PERK) and translational stress response rather than general nutrient sensing, so the revised name is both more specific and unique.

name: Growth factor receptor signalling and oncogenic mutants
rationale: Covers both children (growth-factor/kinase-driven growth signalling and its regulation) plus direct members, which are cancer-associated mutant forms of growth factor pathway components (SMAD2/3, TGFBR2, VEGFR2, AKT1).

name: Mitochondrial quality control and maintenance
rationale: Distinct from parent (proteostasis/biogenesis) and sibling (biogenesis/turnover); this theme covers quality control mechanisms like mitophagy and UPRmt.

name: Satellite cell proliferation and differentiation
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Skeletal muscle regeneration and homeostasis' and 'Cardiac and skeletal muscle development'; renamed to specify satellite cell-driven myogenesis, distinguishing it from broader regeneration/homeostasis and developmental themes.

name: Glomerular vascular and filtration development
rationale: Distinct from parent (organ-level kidney/lung morphogenesis) and sibling (epithelial branching); this theme specifically covers glomerular vascular and filtration structures.

name: Chemokine-driven leukocyte adhesion signalling
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Leukocyte chemotaxis and migration', which shares integrin-mediated migration and leukocyte migration members; this theme is distinguished by chemokine receptor signalling and adhesion mechanisms rather than migration itself.

name: Mitotic spindle attachment and cytokinesis
rationale: Overlapped sibling 'Mitotic and meiotic chromosome segregation' which covers chromosome segregation broadly including meiosis; this theme's members are specifically about mitotic spindle-kinetochore attachment and cytokinesis, distinguishing it from the meiotic/segregation focus.

name: Calcium sequestration and reuptake for muscle relaxation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Calcium-calcineurin signalling in muscle hypertrophy', which shares calcium import/transport regulation and calcineurin theme; this name now emphasizes the relaxation/sequestration aspect distinct from hypertrophic signalling.
The parent has only a single child, so any parent name would just restate 'Notch receptor processing and signalling' rather than provide a broader umbrella.

name: Type I interferon response
rationale: Covers both children (induction/regulation of type I IFN and its downstream antiviral effectors) plus the direct member regulating IFNA/IFNB signalling; tighter than 'innate immunity' since all members specifically concern the type I interferon axis.

name: Ubiquitin-proteasome mediated proteolysis
rationale: Overlaps conceptually with parent's 'protein modification' scope and needs distinction from hemostasis siblings; narrowed to the specific proteolytic regulation mechanism rather than the broad process.

name: Chemokine gradient sensing in leukocytes
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Leukocyte chemotaxis and migration'; narrowed to the chemokine receptor-gradient sensing mechanism rather than general chemotaxis/migration.

name: Reproductive and embryonic tissue differentiation
rationale: Core members (inner cell mass differentiation, decidualization, progesterone response) concern implantation and uterine/embryonic differentiation, while the higher-inclusion structure maturation and primitive erythrocyte members reflect broader developmental maturation of tissues including reproductive and blood lineages; the weakly included erythropoietin response (0.26) is excluded.

name: Heart development
rationale: No siblings present and name is distinct from parent 'Cardiac and tubular organ morphogenesis', clearly narrower/specific to heart.

name: Leukocyte effector functions in innate defense
rationale: Covers the child (neutrophil/myeloid degranulation) plus direct members: complement/pattern receptor-driven recognition, leukocyte-mediated immune effector activity, and phagocytosis, all being direct microbial/particle clearance actions of innate leukocytes rather than adaptive lymphocyte responses.

name: Lymphocyte immune checkpoint restraint
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'NK and gamma-delta T cell cytotoxicity' via shared NK cytotoxicity wording; narrowed to focus on the checkpoint/restraint mechanisms distinguishing this theme.

name: Vacuolar protein sorting pathway
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent 'Vesicular trafficking to endosomes and lysosomes'; narrowed to the specific vacuolar protein sorting machinery to distinguish it.

name: p53-mediated apoptosis regulation
rationale: All members concern how p53 activity and stability (via acetylation, methylation, ubiquitination, cofactor binding) tune the intrinsic apoptotic response to DNA damage, including its positive and negative regulation; the two broader Reactome TP53 transcription entries are included as they focus heavily on this same apoptotic/arrest decision axis.

name: mRNA 3' end formation
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and the name is more specific than the parent (which also covers spliceosome assembly), so it remains distinct.

name: Lipid droplet biogenesis and turnover
rationale: Repeated parent 'Phospholipid and lipid droplet metabolism' too closely; narrowing to droplet biogenesis/turnover distinguishes it from siblings covering glycerophospholipid biosynthesis and triglyceride storage/lipolysis.

name: Melanocyte pigmentation
rationale: All three cover melanocyte specification and melanin synthesis/transport governed by MITF and related regulators.

name: Nucleotide-sugar biosynthesis and amino sugar catabolism
rationale: No member relates to Golgi processing, and the name overlaps with sibling 'Sugar nucleotide and glycoconjugate metabolism'; the revised name reflects the actual biosynthetic/catabolic sugar processes listed.

name: Deoxyribonucleotide metabolism and salvage
rationale: Distinct from parent (de novo biosynthesis) and sibling (purine-specific salvage); this theme covers deoxyribonucleotide metabolism broadly.

name: Metallothionein-mediated metal detoxification
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Metal and porphyrin homeostasis' (shares 'metal' and 'homeostasis'); narrowed to the specific detox mechanism, distinguishing it from sibling heme/bilirubin pathway.

name: Antiviral innate immune response
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader host-virus interaction/evasion concept) and sibling (specific interferon/effector mechanisms); no collision.

name: cAMP metabolism enzymes
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'cAMP signalling'; narrowing to metabolic enzyme pathways (synthesis/degradation) distinguishes it from the signalling-focused sibling.

name: Chondroitin and hyaluronan metabolism disorders
rationale: The current name overlaps with the sibling's broad glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis/degradation scope; the members are specifically chondroitin sulfate and hyaluronan pathways and their associated transporter/enzyme defects, which distinguishes it.

name: Chaperone-mediated protein aggregate clearance
rationale: No siblings, and the name is already more specific than the parent (aggregate clearance vs. folding), so distinguishes clearly.

name: Eicosanoid synthesis and signalling
rationale: Covers the prostaglandin synthesis/signalling child plus leukotriene biosynthesis, prostaglandin E response, and the omega-hydroxylase P450 pathway (0.25, weakly included), all arachidonic acid-derived lipid mediator pathways.

name: Peroxisomal and isoprenoid-derived lipid metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; no other theme covers peroxisomal or isoprenoid-derived lipid pathways.

name: Monoamine neurotransmitter degradation and clearance
rationale: The child covers catecholamine/phenolic amine catabolism broadly, while direct members add specific MAOA/MAOB-mediated oxidative deamination and clearance of dopamine and related biogenic amines; together these describe termination and breakdown of monoamine neurotransmitters, without extending to unrelated amine catabolism.

name: p53-driven cellular senescence
rationale: Name repeated broader parent concept without distinguishing from sibling 'p53-mediated apoptosis and stress response'; narrowed to the senescence-specific branch of p53 signaling.

name: Xenobiotic and steroid biotransformation and transport
rationale: Already distinct from parent (adds steroid focus) and sibling (adds transport, omits conjugation emphasis).

Two members share clear sex-steroid hormone biosynthesis (androgens, estrogens), but the third centres on renal/hepatic steroid glucuronidation and excretion with unrelated kidney-epithelial genes, so no single description covers all three without becoming an uninformative catch-all like 'steroid metabolism'.

name: Regulation of apoptotic signalling
rationale: The child (apoptosis signalling) and the direct members (calcium influx restraint, hypoxia- and ROS-triggered intrinsic apoptosis, and negative regulation of execution phase/apoptotic signaling) all concern the control—often inhibitory—of apoptotic pathways rather than downstream execution itself, so 'regulation of apoptotic signalling' covers both without over-reaching into general cell death or calcium signalling broadly.

name: mRNA processing and turnover
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Non-coding RNA processing and turnover' and overlapped with sibling 'mRNA decay pathway mechanisms'; narrowed to mRNA-specific processing to distinguish from ncRNA-focused parent.

name: Origin licensing and pre-replication complex assembly
rationale: The child covers replication initiation and elongation broadly, while the direct members are specifically about ORC and CDC6 loading onto origins and pre-RC assembly; the umbrella must include both initiation/elongation and the licensing step, so origin licensing plus pre-RC assembly is the tightest phrase covering all without repeating the child's name.

name: Viral trafficking of host nucleocytoplasmic transport
rationale: Child covers viral assembly/replication/egress; direct members concern Vpr and viral nuclear import hijacking host nuclear export machinery (protein export from nucleus, IP3/IP4 transport). Weak member 'protein export from nucleus' (0.26) and IP3/IP4 transport (0.28) included as they reflect the host machinery exploited; the umbrella covers viral manipulation of nuclear-cytoplasmic transport during infection.

name: Insulin granule exocytosis
rationale: Too similar/broad relative to parent 'Insulin biosynthesis and secretion'; narrowed to specific exocytotic mechanism, distinguishing it from sibling's broader beta cell/glucose homeostasis focus.

name: Amino sugar catabolism and galactose disorders
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Sugar metabolism and interconversion' which also covers general sugar metabolism; revised to reflect the amino sugar catabolism and galactose-related disease focus specific to this theme's members.

name: Neuronal process outgrowth and guidance
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically names neuronal outgrowth/guidance rather than general shape remodeling or morphogenesis.

name: GPCR-mediated neuromodulation
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and the name is distinct from the parent, which covers second-messenger signalling and behavioural response broadly.

name: Notch, Wnt and Hedgehog signalling
rationale: Both children cover developmental signalling pathways acting via receptor processing/regulation (Notch) and morphogen signalling (Wnt/Hedgehog), with no direct members adding further scope; naming the union of the two children is the smallest umbrella.

name: Gene expression regulation and nuclear macromolecule biosynthesis
rationale: Children cover chromatin/transcription and full gene-expression machinery; direct members add RNA metabolism regulation (NPAS4 expression, RNA metabolic process) and polyamine biosynthesis/transport tied to nucleic acid synthesis, so an umbrella of nuclear gene-expression and biosynthetic regulation covers all without repeating either child's name.

name: Muscle growth, differentiation and adaptation
rationale: Covers both children (developmental/regenerative programs and adaptive growth regulation) plus the direct member on calcineurin signalling, which feeds into the calcium-dependent hypertrophy/adaptation pathways described.

name: Apoptotic signalling
rationale: Covers both extrinsic and mitochondrial (intrinsic) apoptotic signalling branches plus general apoptotic pathway members and mitochondrial membrane potential regulation tied to death commitment, without extending beyond programmed cell death signalling.

name: Notch signalling and target transcription regulation
rationale: Sibling 'Notch, Wnt and Hedgehog signalling' also involves Notch receptor processing and pathway regulation broadly; this name should emphasize the transcriptional/target gene regulation aspect distinguishing it, while remaining true to its members.

name: CD4 T cell activation and proliferation
rationale: Name specifies CD4 T cell activation and proliferation, distinct from parent's general T cell activation and sibling's differentiation focus.

name: Nucleotide sugar metabolism
rationale: All members concern biosynthesis, interconversion or catabolism of activated nucleotide-sugar donors (UDP-GlcNAc, GDP-mannose, GDP-fucose, sialic acid) that feed glycosylation, broader than the amino sugar catabolism child but not extending to glycosylation itself.

name: RSV and influenza gene expression and assembly
rationale: The current name closely restates the parent 'Viral protein synthesis, assembly and release'; the members are specifically influenza and RSV transcription, translation, and assembly processes, distinguishing it from the parent and from the HIV-focused sibling.

name: CD4 T-helper subset differentiation
rationale: Distinct from parent (priming and costimulation) and sibling (broader differentiation and activation); already specific to CD4 T-helper subset differentiation.

name: Origin licensing and pre-replication complex assembly
rationale: Distinct from parents (checkpoint regulation, replication/repair synthesis) and siblings (ubiquitination, DNA repair/segregation, spindle/cytokinesis); already specific to origin licensing and pre-RC assembly.

name: MHC class I antigen presentation regulation
rationale: All three concern control of MHC class I biosynthesis/expression, including NLRC5-driven transactivation, with the IFN-gamma hallmark included for its central role in inducing this same class I machinery.

name: Regulated exocytosis and secretory vesicle release
rationale: Overlapped with sibling themes like 'Vesicular membrane trafficking', 'Protein sorting, secretion and endosomal trafficking', and 'Golgi-derived vesicle transport'; narrowed to focus on regulated secretory exocytosis specifically.

name: Vesicular trafficking and membrane fusion
rationale: All members involve movement of membranes/cargo between organelles via vesicle fusion machinery (tethers, SNAREs, ESCRT), including endosome, MVB-lysosome and general intracellular transport pathways; reticulophagy fits as ER membrane delivery to the autophagic-lysosomal system.

name: Mitochondrial respiration and its regulation
rationale: Covers the oxidative phosphorylation child plus the direct members regulating cellular respiration, electron transport, and ROS produced by it, without repeating the child's name.

name: Photoreceptor development and maintenance
rationale: Sibling 'Sensory receptor cell biology' shares nearly identical members (retina homeostasis, photoreceptor cell morphogenesis, outer segment organization), so the current name equally describes that sibling; narrowing to developmental/maintenance processes distinguishes this theme.

name: p53-mediated DNA damage response
rationale: Core members (inclusion 1.00) are all p53-driven apoptosis/transcriptional stress programs; UV response and stress-response regulation members overlap heavily with p53 damage/repair/apoptosis targets, though those two are broader and included at lower weight (0.37 and 0.25).

name: GPCR-coupled cAMP signalling
rationale: All members concern GPCR-mediated activation of adenylate cyclase to raise cAMP (adrenergic, serotonergic and other GPCR routes) or its direct biosynthesis; response to caffeine is included at 0.91 via its adenosine-receptor/cAMP arm despite additional calcium-channel effects.

name: Chromatin assembly and genome stability
rationale: Covers both children (chromatin organisation/cohesion and chromatin-linked genome stability) plus the direct members on replication-coupled chromatin assembly and replication regulation, without invoking specific mechanisms like telomeres or acetylation that only some members touch.

name: Axon and dendrite morphogenesis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Synapse structure and function' on connectivity aspects; narrowing to morphogenesis of neuronal processes distinguishes it from synaptic structure/function and transmission siblings.

name: Base excision repair
rationale: Both the child theme and the direct members (BER, its Reactome counterpart, and depyrimidination as a base-loss step feeding into it) all describe the base-excision repair pathway and its initiating lesions.

name: GCN2-mediated amino acid stress signaling
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Integrated stress response and eIF2α signalling' by repeating 'Integrated stress response'; narrowed to the specific upstream kinase/nutrient-sensing branch.

name: Ureteric bud branching program
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Epithelial organ morphogenesis' and near-duplicated 'Kidney and lung morphogenesis'; renamed to specify the branching mechanism distinct from the glomerular filtration sibling.

name: Cardiac chamber and vasculature morphogenesis
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Heart and tube-organ development' and 'Kidney and lung morphogenesis', both covering tubular organ formation; narrowed to focus on cardiac/vascular structures specifically.

name: Growth factor receptor signal attenuation and endocytic trafficking
rationale: The child theme covers RTK signal termination/trafficking; direct members add PDGFR-beta signalling regulation and clathrin-mediated endocytosis, both mechanisms of receptor internalisation and signal control, so the union centres on growth factor receptor down-regulation via endocytic trafficking.

name: Heme metabolism and bilirubin excretion
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader porphyrin/metal homeostasis) and sibling (metal ion detoxification); no collision.

name: Heme synthesis, degradation and bilirubin clearance
rationale: All members concern the porphyrin/heme biosynthetic pathway, its breakdown to bilirubin, or the hepatic uptake and conjugation steps that clear bilirubin, including the two hyperbilirubinemia pathways caused by defects in that clearance machinery.

name: mTOR nutrient sensing pathway
rationale: Overlaps parent 'Stress and nutrient signalling with p53' by repeating both stress and nutrient signalling terms; narrowing to mTOR-specific nutrient sensing distinguishes it from sibling 'Cellular stress response'.

name: Host-dependent viral replication and assembly
rationale: Focuses on replication/assembly dependent on host machinery, distinct from parent's entry/assembly scope and sibling's SARS-CoV-2 entry focus.

name: Rho family GTPase cycles and effectors
rationale: Overlapping members with sibling 'Small GTPase signal transduction' and no Ras-specific members present; renamed to specify Rho family focus (RHOA, RHO, CDC42, RHOF, RHOU cycles and Rhotekin/Rhophilin effectors), distinguishing it from the broader small GTPase and regulation siblings.

name: p53-mediated apoptosis and transcriptional regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (cell cycle arrest) and sibling (DNA damage response and repair); no collision.

name: DNA damage checkpoint signalling
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'DNA damage response and genome maintenance' and sibling 'DNA damage response and repair'; narrowed to checkpoint signalling to distinguish from repair mechanisms.

name: Protein folding and chaperone-mediated quality control
rationale: Covers both children (autophagic clearance of misfolded proteins, chaperone folding) plus direct members like general protein folding, tubulin folding cofactor pathway, and heat-induced chaperone response, all centering on maintaining/restoring native protein conformation.

name: mRNA decay pathway mechanisms
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'RNA processing and turnover'; specifying mRNA decay mechanisms distinguishes it as focused on mRNA-specific degradation pathways rather than general RNA processing.

name: Prostaglandin and eicosanoid signalling
rationale: Distinct from parents (broader GPCR lipid/nucleotide categories) and sibling (biosynthesis of resolvins, not signalling).

name: Fluid and osmotic homeostasis signalling
rationale: Covers water/glycerol channel transport plus receptor-based signalling (guanylyl cyclase, calcitonin family) and organismal homeostasis that regulate fluid balance and osmotic tone, broader than the channel-transport child but not extending to unrelated signalling.

name: Oxidative stress response and ferroptosis regulation
rationale: Covers the antioxidant/redox child plus the direct members on chemical stress response and ferroptosis, all centered on cellular handling of oxidative/chemical damage; ferroptosis regulation is added since it is not subsumed by redox homeostasis alone.

name: Chromatin and epigenetic regulation
rationale: All core members (chromatin organization, epigenetic regulation of gene expression from both sources, PKMT histone methylation, KMT2D/MLL4 Kabuki pathway) concern chromatin packaging and covalent modification machinery controlling gene expression; methylation (0.76) broadly overlaps via SAM-dependent writers, and genomic imprinting (0.35, weakest) is a specific downstream application excluded from the tighter name.

name: Lipid mediator and GPCR-linked inflammatory signalling
rationale: Distinct from siblings, which cover differentiation, antigen presentation, cytotoxicity, and other signalling axes; this one is specifically lipid mediator and GPCR-linked pathways.

name: Membrane depolarization and muscle contraction regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Muscle contraction and calcium-dependent regulation' which also covers muscle contraction/calcium; this theme's distinctive members involve membrane depolarization regulation, not shared by siblings.

name: Chemosensory and photic stimulus detection
rationale: Too close to parent 'Mechanosensory and chemosensory transduction' and sibling 'Sensory stimulus transduction channels'; narrowing to chemosensory and light detection distinguishes it from the channel-focused and mechanotransduction siblings.

name: Dendritic spine and synaptic glutamate receptor regulation
rationale: Focuses specifically on glutamate receptor regulation, distinct from the broader plasticity signalling sibling and cytoskeletal remodeling sibling, and more specific than the parent.

name: Prostaglandin synthesis and receptor signalling
rationale: All three cover the arachidonic acid release and cyclooxygenase-driven prostaglandin production pathway plus the prostanoid receptors that transduce these lipid mediators.

name: Kidney and urinary tract development
rationale: Covers the child (nephron and kidney morphogenesis) plus direct members on nephric duct, ureter, metanephros and nephron development, all being urogenital organogenesis events broader than 'nephron' alone but not extending beyond kidney/urinary tract formation.

name: Autophagosome formation and maturation
rationale: Core members cover macroautophagy machinery and regulation of autophagosome maturation/fusion with lysosomes; the weakly included xenophagy regulation member (0.38) is a specific bacterial-clearance application of this same maturation machinery.

name: Mitochondrial translation and ribosome biogenesis
rationale: Overlaps sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing' which shares rRNA processing theme; narrowing to mitochondrial-specific focus (mitochondrial translation, ribosome assembly, mitochondrial rRNA processing) distinguishes it while remaining true to its members.

name: Collagen-based connective tissue integrity
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Proteoglycan turnover and remodeling' (too broad) and sibling 'Extracellular matrix remodelling in vascular repair'; narrowing to collagen-based structural integrity distinguishes it.

name: Extracellular matrix and connective tissue integrity
rationale: Members center on collagen synthesis and assembly (collagen formation, chain trimerization), the cytoskeletal/matrix scaffolding that supports tissue architecture (intermediate filament organization), and transporters whose loss disrupts connective tissue or skeletal matrix (SLC26A2, SLC2A10, SLCO2A1 disease pathways), all converging on connective tissue/matrix integrity and its disruption in skeletal and vascular disease.

name: Cytokine receptor signalling via JAK-STAT
rationale: Covers the IL-6/gp130-STAT3 child plus direct members on cytokine-mediated signalling, JAK-STAT receptor regulation, STAT-dependent surface receptor signalling and general immune cytokine signalling, all converging on cytokine receptor to JAK-STAT transmission rather than any single cytokine or broader immune signalling.

name: Nucleotide biosynthesis pathways
rationale: Repeated the parent 'Nucleotide metabolism disorders' name stem and overlapped with sibling 'Nucleotide and phosphate metabolism'; narrowing to biosynthesis pathways distinguishes it.

name: IL-6/gp130-JAK-STAT3 signalling
rationale: Name is specific and distinct from parent, no sibling collisions.

name: IL-6/gp130-JAK-STAT3 signalling
rationale: No duplication or sibling overlap indicated; name is specific and accurately describes its members.

name: Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesion
rationale: Both children concern cadherin-mediated junctional adhesion and its regulation; with no direct members, this parent generalizes only slightly to cover both without invoking non-cadherin junction types.

name: Strand invasion intermediate resolution
rationale: Repeated parent 'Strand invasion intermediate repair' and too generic vs siblings; narrowed to describe the specific repair step distinguishing it from replication restart and double-strand break repair siblings.

name: Early mesoderm formation and axial segmentation
rationale: Covers mesodermal fate commitment/gastrulation and somite-based axial patterning, the two children, without repeating either name.

name: Excitation-contraction coupling
rationale: Union covers calcium cycling and channel regulation feeding muscle contraction, ion channel excitability underlying electrical signaling to muscle, and direct members (actin-myosin sliding, cardiac contraction regulation, calcineurin signaling) that are downstream effectors/modulators of the same coupling process; broader than any single child but tighter than generic 'muscle physiology'.

name: Phagocyte antimicrobial effector mechanisms
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; it specifically denotes phagocyte antimicrobial killing mechanisms, not covered by any sibling.

name: Regulation of myogenic proliferation and differentiation
rationale: Too close to parent 'Muscle growth, differentiation and adaptation'; new name specifies the proliferation/differentiation regulation focus, distinguishing it from sibling 'Striated muscle development and regeneration' which centers on regenerative fusion events.

name: Lymphocyte and monocyte chemotaxis regulation
rationale: As written, the name would equally describe the sibling 'Leukocyte chemotaxis regulation', which also centers on chemokine-driven leukocyte movement; the members here emphasize lymphocyte and mononuclear cell migration specifically, distinguishing it from the myeloid-focused sibling.

name: ERAD and neddylation-mediated quality control
rationale: The original name duplicated the broad regulation/degradation theme of both siblings; members here specifically involve ERAD pathway, neddylation, and stress granule disassembly, distinguishing it from the purely proteasomal degradation and regulation siblings.

name: tRNA modification and processing
rationale: Own members are entirely tRNA/snRNA processing and modification events, not ribosomal or mitochondrial RNA maturation; name did not match actual member content and overlapped conceptually with parent's rRNA/tRNA scope, so narrowed to what members show.

name: Apoptotic and death receptor signalling regulation
rationale: Covers the two child themes on apoptotic/intrinsic signalling plus the direct members on Fas/activation-induced T cell death, which are death-receptor regulatory arms of the same programmed cell death network.

name: Retinoid metabolism and signalling
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and name is distinct from parent 'Fat-soluble vitamin transport and metabolism' by specifying retinoid pathway.

name: Axon regeneration and neurofascin interactions
rationale: Overlaps sibling names covering myelination/adhesion and neurotrophin signalling; the distinguishing members are axon regeneration processes and Neurofascin interactions.

name: Myogenic transcription factor regulation
rationale: Parent 'Satellite cell proliferation and differentiation' already covers general myogenesis regulation; narrowing to the transcription factor control aspect distinguishes this theme.

name: mRNA 3'-end processing and decay
rationale: Unites the deadenylation/decapping decay child with histone pre-mRNA 3'-end processing and general mRNA 3'-end processing members; 'mRNA 3'-end processing' covers the direct members while 'decay' covers the child, giving the smallest umbrella spanning both maturation and turnover of mRNA 3' ends.

name: Copper and manganese ion homeostasis
rationale: The current name overlaps with sibling 'Metal ion detoxification and acquisition' and 'Iron and metal ion homeostasis with heme metabolism', which also concern trace metal transport/detox; the actual members center specifically on copper and manganese ions, distinguishing it from those siblings.

name: Nuclear-mitochondrial RNA processing crosstalk
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitochondrial and cytosolic gene expression' and echoed parent's mitochondrial gene expression scope; narrowed to focus on RNA/protein processing machinery spanning nuclear and mitochondrial compartments.

name: Mitotic chromatin and nuclear envelope dynamics
rationale: Distinct from parent (which is broader, covering assembly/maintenance) and sibling (chromatin assembly and genome maintenance); this theme specifically covers mitotic chromatin condensation and nuclear envelope breakdown/reformation.

name: miRNA-mediated mRNA silencing and turnover
rationale: Distinct from parent (nonsense-mediated decay) and no siblings; name specifies miRNA-mediated mechanism clearly.

name: cAMP-PKA signal transduction
rationale: Collides with sibling 'cAMP metabolism and signalling'; narrowed to the PKA-mediated signal transduction aspect, distinct from cAMP metabolism/turnover.

name: Cell cycle progression and division
rationale: Children cover checkpoint control and mitotic phase transitions; the direct member 'cell division' broadens scope to genome duplication, segregation and cytokinesis generally, so the parent spans the full cell cycle and division machinery rather than checkpoints alone.

name: T cell activation and proliferation control
rationale: Original name overlapped with sibling 'T cell receptor signalling and differentiation', which explicitly covers T cell differentiation; this theme's members are actually about activation and proliferation regulation, not differentiation, so the name should reflect that distinction.

name: Virus-host interactions and antiviral restriction
rationale: All three children and the general viral-process members concern the interplay between viral replication stages and host restriction/defence factors, spanning general viral life cycle, HIV-specific replication, and molecular host-virus interactions; no direct members extend beyond this.

name: Glucose homeostasis and incretin signaling in insulin secretion
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Insulin biosynthesis and secretion' and echoed the parent's incretin/insulin theme; narrowed to glucose homeostasis, incretin action, and channel defects (ABCC8) distinct from the sibling's biosynthesis focus.

name: Regulation of muscle cell proliferation and regeneration
rationale: Repeats parent name closely and overlaps with sibling 'Myogenic differentiation and regeneration' which covers the same negative regulation of differentiation members; this theme's distinguishing members are muscle cell proliferation and regeneration, so the name is sharpened to reflect proliferation control rather than differentiation.

name: Cardiac chamber and valve development
rationale: Repeats parent theme name closely (Cardiac chamber and valve morphogenesis / Cardiac valve and chamber morphogenesis); revised to reflect the specific mix of chamber, valve, and septum development members while remaining distinct from the parent phrasing.

name: Telomere maintenance and cellular senescence
rationale: Covers the telomere capping/maintenance child plus the direct members, which are all forms or regulation of cellular senescence, including its telomere-linked triggers; broader terms like genome stability would exceed what the members actually cover.

name: PDGF receptor signalling in mesangial precursors
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Glomerular mesangial cell and capillary development' which also covers mesenchymal signalling; narrowed to specific receptor pathway distinguishing it from the broader developmental sibling.

name: PDGF receptor and related mesenchymal signalling
rationale: Three of five members concern PDGFRA/PDGFRB signalling and its regulation in mesenchymal cells; collagen-activated receptor tyrosine kinase and IL-11 signalling also act on mesenchymal/stromal cells with overlapping downstream effectors (SRC, matrix remodelling, fibrosis), so the shared theme is receptor tyrosine kinase and cytokine signalling driving mesenchymal cell behaviour and fibrotic remodelling.

name: Vascular and lymphatic development, growth and repair
rationale: Both children cover blood/lymphatic vessel formation, remodelling and its regulation including angiogenesis; the wound healing member also feeds into vascular repair, so the umbrella spans vessel development, angiogenic regulation and repair without invoking unrelated immune or metabolic biology.

name: Cytoskeletal signalling in cell and axon guidance
rationale: Both children concern directional cell/growth cone steering via cytoskeletal and GTPase signalling; the direct member, peripheral axon regeneration, extends this to axon regrowth, still fitting the shared theme of guided cellular/axonal outgrowth rather than generic cell morphogenesis alone.

name: Transcription elongation, 3'-end processing and HIV-Tat transcription
rationale: Current name overlaps with sibling 'RNA transcription termination and spliceosome assembly', which also covers termination; this theme's distinct focus is elongation, 3'-end processing, and HIV-specific transcription/Tat elongation members.

name: Intestinal lipid and cholesterol absorption
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader lipoprotein remodeling and lipid absorption) and sibling (triglyceride-rich lipoprotein clearance); already specific to intestinal absorption.

name: Vascular and lymphatic vessel development
rationale: Both children (VEGF/lymphatic development, angiogenesis/endothelial proliferation regulation) plus representative members concern blood and lymphatic vessel formation and its regulation via endothelial cell behaviour, without direct members forcing broader scope.

name: Cadherin-mediated adhesion regulation
rationale: Covers the child (E-cadherin adhesion regulation/turnover) plus direct members addressing cadherin-mediated adhesion regulation more broadly, including type II classical cadherins and CDH1 mRNA translation control by microRNAs, without restating the narrower E-cadherin-specific child name.

name: Strand invasion intermediate repair
rationale: Collided with sibling 'DNA damage repair' (near-identical name); narrowed to reflect the strand-invasion specific repair steps under the parent theme.

name: Epithelial tissue organization and remodelling
rationale: Covers epidermal/appendage differentiation, epithelial adhesion and EMT, plus the wound-healing epidermal spreading member, all concerning how epithelial tissue is structurally organized and remodelled.

name: Notch signalling in organ development
rationale: Name distinguishes itself from parent by narrowing to Notch signalling and to organ development context, and differs clearly from the sibling which covers all three pathways generally.

name: Base excision and cross-link repair
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; members focus on AP site resolution, strand break repair, and interstrand cross-link repair, distinguishing it from the sibling's general DNA/nucleotide-excision repair.

name: Cytoplasmic innate immune sensing and inflammatory mediator production
rationale: Both children plus the direct member concern cytosolic detection of microbial or viral cues and the resulting inflammatory/antiviral mediator output; this is broader than either child but excludes adaptive immunity and unrelated cell biology.

name: Host-virus molecular conflict
rationale: Name is distinct from parent (which covers viral entry/ER targeting) and sibling (viral life cycle/host interactions); it emphasizes molecular conflict dynamics.

name: VEGF-driven endothelial differentiation and vessel morphogenesis
rationale: No duplicate or sibling conflict, but the name repeated the parent's general scope; kept as-is otherwise since no collision or sibling overlap requires broader change.

name: Lipoprotein particle assembly and clearance
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Triglyceride and lipoprotein metabolism'; narrowed to particle assembly/clearance processes distinct from triglyceride metabolism.

name: mRNA deadenylation and decapping-mediated decay
rationale: Four members at 1.00 cover the core cytoplasmic decay pathway: mRNA catabolism, decapping, and deadenylation-dependent decay via deadenylation. The weaker member (3'-end processing regulation, 0.61) concerns polyadenylation/maturation rather than decay, but overlaps through shared complexes and mRNA lifespan control, so it is only loosely covered.

name: Epigenetic and chromatin regulation
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to reflect epigenetic imprinting and methylation members while remaining distinct from siblings focused on cell cycle, transcription, and nuclear export.

name: Ion channel-based excitability and intercellular electrical coupling
rationale: Both children concern excitable-membrane ion transport and cardiac conduction; the sole direct member, connexon trafficking, supplies the gap-junction/electrical coupling component that neither child's name captures alone.

name: Autophagy and endosomal-lysosomal degradation
rationale: Repeats parent's 'Vesicular trafficking and lysosomal degradation' theme; renamed to reflect the autophagy and endosome-lysosome fusion processes specific to its members.

name: Protein glycosylation and its disorders
rationale: Covers both children (glycan assembly machinery and its congenital disease consequences) plus the direct member, a specific O-glycosylation pathway, without repeating either child's name.

name: Rho GTPase signalling
rationale: Already more specific than sibling 'Small GTPase signalling'/'Small GTPase cycle regulation' since Rho GTPases are a specific subfamily; no collision.

name: Transcriptional regulation of RNA synthesis
rationale: Overlapped with parent's broad 'RNA processing and turnover' scope; narrowed to focus on transcriptional control distinct from the splicing-coupling sibling.

name: Stress-induced translational shutdown and nutrient deprivation response
rationale: No siblings present and the name already differs from parent p53-mediated stress response by specifying translational shutdown and nutrient deprivation focus.

name: Ribosome biogenesis and MYC-driven growth programs
rationale: The child covers nucleolar rRNA processing/ribosome maturation; direct members add RNA Pol III transcription (feeding rRNA/tRNA synthesis) and MYC target gene sets, which drive ribosome biogenesis and biosynthetic capacity for growth. Together these span nucleolar ribosome production and the MYC transcriptional program that fuels it, broader than the child alone but not a generic label.

name: Endosome-to-secretory pathway protein sorting
rationale: Overlapped with multiple sibling trafficking themes (Vesicular membrane trafficking, Golgi-derived vesicle transport, Endomembrane vesicular trafficking and secretion, Post-Golgi trafficking); narrowed to the endosomal-secretory sorting axis distinguishing it from generic vesicular/Golgi transport siblings.

name: Cartilage and endochondral bone development
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent, distinguishing endochondral bone/cartilage development from broader skeletal/dental regulation.

name: Mitochondrial carbon and nitrogen metabolism
rationale: Broadens the child (mitochondrial nitrogen/carbon metabolite handling) to include TCA cycle metabolism, 2-oxoglutarate conversion, and NADPH regeneration, all central mitochondrial carbon/redox pathways feeding or branching from the TCA cycle.

name: Nucleic acid sensing and antiviral defence
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling: focuses on nucleic acid sensors and antiviral interferon defence, unlike the inflammasome-focused sibling and the broader inflammatory mediator parent.

name: Non-proteinogenic amino acid and cofactor metabolism
rationale: Core members (vitamin B6, non-proteinogenic amino acid synthesis/degradation, serine metabolism, pyrimidine base catabolism) converge on small-molecule metabolism generating or clearing non-protein amino acids and related cofactors/neurotransmitter precursors; weakly included members (2-hydroxyglutarate interconversion, GABA degradation) touch related mitochondrial nitrogen/carbon shunts but are excluded from the core claim.

name: Steroid hormone and sterol metabolism
rationale: Covers the child (steroid/vitamin D hormone metabolism) plus direct members: sterol-derived P450 hydroxylation pathways and endogenous sterol handling, with 'miscellaneous substrates' being a residual catch-all under the same steroidogenic umbrella.

name: Thrombin generation and signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent 'Coagulation cascade regulation' and sibling 'Hemostasis and coagulation'; specifically about thrombin generation and signalling.

name: Behavioral and physiological regulation
rationale: The current name describes drug/reward responses, which actually fits the sibling (nicotine, cocaine, ethanol responses) better; this theme's members concern general behavior, locomotion, circadian rhythm and dopamine signaling regulation, not drug reward specifically.

name: Microtubule-based vesicle transport
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Microtubule-based organelle transport' by including organelles; narrowing to vesicle cargo specifically distinguishes it from that sibling and remains under the parent's broader organelle-and-cargo scope.

name: Dietary lipid absorption and lipoprotein metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically covers intestinal dietary lipid absorption and chylomicron/lipoprotein metabolism, unlike bile acid, cholesterol/HDL, adipocyte storage, or triglyceride/phospholipid themes.

name: Meiotic recombination and segregation
rationale: Repeated core meaning of parent 'Meiotic chromosome and spindle dynamics'; renamed to specify the meiosis-specific processes distinguishing it from that parent and from the maturation-control sibling.

name: Nucleoside and analogue metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism'; narrowed to focus on nucleosides and analogues, distinguishing it from the broader nucleotide metabolism sibling.

name: Amyloid-beta production and clearance regulation
rationale: All members concern regulation of APP processing into amyloid-beta and its clearance, spanning secretase activity, trafficking, lipid handling and inflammatory modulation.

name: p53-mediated DNA damage response regulation
rationale: No sibling collisions and it is more specific than the parent (DNA damage response regulation vs. apoptosis/transcriptional regulation broadly).

name: p53-dependent DNA repair pathways
rationale: Distinguishes from parent 'p53-mediated cell cycle arrest' (a different p53 output) and sibling 'apoptosis and transcriptional regulation'; focuses specifically on repair mechanisms rather than broader damage response.

name: Regulation of progenitor proliferation and self-renewal
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; clearly specific to progenitor proliferation/self-renewal regulation, not overlapping with 'Stem and progenitor cell differentiation' or other listed themes.

name: Cell junction assembly and signaling
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion' by repeating 'adhesion'; narrowing to junction assembly/signaling distinguishes it from the cadherin-based adhesion dynamics sibling.

name: Insulin secretion and incretin regulation
rationale: Covers the child (glucose homeostasis/insulin secretion) plus the direct members on GLP1/incretin control of insulin release; the extracellular-protein-localization member is weakly included (0.49) and left out.

name: Mitophagy and autophagosome biogenesis
rationale: Both children (selective organelle autophagy, autophagosome formation/maturation) plus the direct members (negative regulation of mitochondrial fission and of mitophagy) all concern mitochondrial quality control via autophagy and the machinery building the engulfing autophagosome.

name: Mismatch repair and DNA synthesis
rationale: Unites the DNA replication and repair synthesis child with the direct mismatch-repair members (MSH2-defect and strand elongation included, weakly at 0.33-0.6); narrower than general DNA repair since only synthesis/mismatch-correction mechanisms are represented.

name: Mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation
rationale: All members concern building/functioning of the mitotic spindle and separating sister chromatids, extending the child's checkpoint focus to include spindle formation itself (EML4/NUDC, HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE, sister chromatid separation).

name: Systemic glucose homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Beta cell glucose sensing and insulin release'; renaming to focus on whole-body glucose regulation distinguishes it from the parent's beta cell-specific mechanism and the sibling's broader beta cell biology.

name: Platelet dense and alpha granule secretion
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Platelet activation and adhesion signalling'; renamed to specify granule secretion mechanism, distinguishing from parent and from sibling 'Coagulation cascade'.

name: Intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway regulation
rationale: No member mentions calcium handling; the theme is entirely about intrinsic/BCL-2-mediated apoptotic signaling, so the calcium claim is unsupported. This distinguishes it from sibling 'Cellular stress response and apoptotic regulation', which centers on stress response rather than intrinsic apoptosis machinery.

name: Ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation
rationale: Both children involve building/removing ubiquitin marks and activating ligases that target substrates for proteasomal destruction, but neither child term alone covers the shared degradation-tagging biology.

name: PD-1/CTLA-4 checkpoint restraint pathways
rationale: Name essentially repeats both parents (Lymphocyte immune checkpoint restraint; Immune checkpoint regulation of lymphocyte activity) without adding specificity; naming the actual checkpoint pathways distinguishes it.

name: p53 stress and DNA damage transcriptional response
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to emphasize transcriptional regulation and stress response aspects distinguishing it from the sibling theme focused on apoptotic signaling pathways.

name: Hedgehog signalling in neural tube patterning
rationale: The child covers neural tube and CNS morphogenesis, while the direct members concern Hedgehog/smoothened signalling, a pathway central to neural tube patterning; together they form a coherent umbrella of Hedgehog-driven CNS morphogenesis without broadening to unrelated developmental signalling.

name: Aldosterone-driven osmotic balance
rationale: Name did not reflect the aldosterone-specific parent scope and overlapped conceptually with sibling's ion transport focus; narrowed to specify aldosterone-driven fluid/osmotic regulation distinct from ion transport mechanisms.

name: PI3K/AKT signalling
rationale: All members involve receptor-driven activation of PI3K and AKT (or the upstream kinase network feeding into it), spanning receptor tyrosine kinase, IGF1R, CD28 and oncogenic PI3K variants of this cascade.

name: Contractile-to-synthetic VSMC dedifferentiation
rationale: Repeated parent's phenotype switching concept without adding specificity; revised to name the specific transition process being described.

name: Xenobiotic metabolism and transport
rationale: The child covers drug/xenobiotic biotransformation; direct members add specific enzymes (FMO), organic anion transporters (SLC22), and a drug ADME example (ciprofloxacin), so the umbrella must include transport alongside metabolism of xenobiotics/drugs.

name: Adrenergic-linked cAMP signalling and secretion
rationale: Overlapped heavily with siblings 'Cyclic nucleotide signalling' and 'GPCR-cyclic nucleotide signalling and secretion control', which share nearly identical members; the adrenergic receptor focus (Alpha-2 adrenergic, adrenaline signalling) distinguishes this theme.

name: Inherited glycogen storage diseases
rationale: Two members are directly glycogen storage disease entries; 'Diseases of carbohydrate metabolism' is broader but is dominated by glycogen synthesis/degradation defects, so glycogen storage disease is the tightest common thread across all three.

name: Organic and inorganic anion exchangers
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Inorganic ion transport and homeostasis'; narrowed to specific anion exchanger/transporter proteins rather than general ion transport.

name: Ion channel defects and hormone regulation of insulin secretion
rationale: The original name also fits sibling 'Insulin secretion and beta cell function', which shares the same core members; this theme uniquely includes ABCC8 channel defects and incretin/GLP1 hormone regulation, distinguishing it from that sibling.

name: Nuclear genome maintenance and viral exploitation of host processes
rationale: Children span p53-mediated DNA damage response, nuclear genome regulation/cell division, and several virus-host interaction themes (viral nucleocytoplasmic transport, HIV replication, viral gene expression), plus a direct 'viral process' member; the union centers on host nuclear/genomic machinery and its co-option or regulation during viral infection. Polyamine metabolism and the low-inclusion microRNA-translation member are not fully covered but are minority inclusions.

name: GABA and acidic amino acid transport
rationale: The current name also fits the sibling 'Amino acid transport', which shares the same amino acid transport members; narrowing to GABA plus glutamate/aspartate transport distinguishes this theme.

name: Wnt and Hedgehog pathway components
rationale: Repeats parent name 'Wnt and Hedgehog signalling in development'; needs specificity distinguishing it as the core pathway components rather than repeating the developmental signalling scope.

name: Notch receptor signalling and regulation
rationale: All five members concern Notch receptor activation (ligand-induced or noncanonical), its proteolytic processing by gamma-secretase, and positive or negative regulation of its signalling output.

name: Immune-vascular cell trafficking and defence
rationale: Covers the children's mix of leukocyte-endothelial adhesion, immune signalling, antiviral defence and platelet/hemostatic function, plus direct members on cell adhesion, migration, and tissue cell-number homeostasis in immune/vascular contexts; broader than any single child but excludes unrelated metabolic or neural biology.

name: Wnt pathway components
rationale: Sibling 'Wnt and Hedgehog signaling' covers signaling; this theme is actually about pathway components per parent, so renamed for clarity and distinction.

name: Purine base salvage
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Purine and nucleoside salvage and catabolism' and sibling 'Purine nucleoside salvage and catabolism'; narrowing to purine base salvage (excluding catabolism and nucleoside-specific salvage) distinguishes it.

name: Nucleoside salvage and catabolism
rationale: Repeats parent 'Purine ribonucleoside salvage and catabolism' too closely and overlaps sibling 'Purine nucleoside salvage and catabolism'; broader term covering ribonucleoside/glycosyl compound metabolism distinguishes it while remaining true to members.

name: Polyamine metabolism and transport
rationale: Direct members cover polyamine biosynthesis, spermidine turnover, transport and ODC regulation, while the child covers a distinct protein hydroxylation/EEF2 modification biology; the umbrella must span both without collapsing into the child's name. The weakly included 'obsolete peptidyl-amino acid modification' (0.39) is excluded.

name: TCR signaling and general T cell activation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling themes on CD4 helper lineage differentiation and Th1/2 differentiation; narrowed to core TCR-driven activation distinct from helper subset specification.

name: Chromatin dynamics and mitotic genome maintenance
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent, focusing on chromatin/mitotic maintenance rather than general DNA damage response.

name: Microtubule cytoskeleton organization in division and cilia
rationale: Both children build microtubule-based structures — mitotic spindle/centrosome and ciliary axoneme — and direct-support members (spindle organization, spindle positioning, axoneme assembly) fall within this shared microtubule-organizing biology, broader than either child alone.

name: Regulation of VEGF-driven angiogenesis
rationale: Name repeated parent concept generically; narrowed to specify VEGF-driven regulation matching parent themes' focus.

name: Chemosensory and monoaminergic behaviour
