rationale: No parent to repeat, and no sibling addresses chemosensory/monoaminergic behaviour; distinct from all listed themes.

name: Lipoprotein particle turnover regulation
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Plasma lipoprotein metabolism' and closely echoes parent 'Lipoprotein particle assembly and clearance'; renamed to emphasize regulatory turnover aspect distinct from assembly/clearance and plasma-focused metabolism.

name: DNA damage response and genome maintenance
rationale: Covers the DNA damage response/repair children plus telomere maintenance via recombination, which shares the same recombination-based genome-stability machinery but extends beyond repair of damage per se.

name: Endosome-lysosome vesicle transport machinery
rationale: Repeated parent's scope (vesicular trafficking to endosomes/lysosomes) without adding specificity; revised to distinguish from sibling 'Vacuolar and lysosomal trafficking' by focusing on transport machinery/mechanism.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase signal termination and trafficking
rationale: All members involve attenuation of RTK signalling (VEGFR, generic tyrosine kinases, MET) via dephosphorylation, ubiquitination, endosomal sorting/degradation, or recycling that limits or shapes signal duration.

name: Axon regeneration and myelination
rationale: Covers all three children (axon-glial adhesion/myelination, axon growth/myelination/glial adhesion, neurotrophin signalling/axon regeneration) with no direct members, spanning both the regrowth of injured axons and their glial ensheathment.

name: Nucleic acid sensing and type I interferon induction
rationale: Repeats the parent's scope; no siblings present but the name essentially restates the parent 'Type I interferon induction and signaling regulation'. However since no true duplication or sibling overlap exists, keep as is.

Sphingomyelin/sphingolipid catabolism and biosynthesis, TNFR1 ceramide production form a coherent sphingolipid-metabolism cluster, but lipoprotein catabolic process and regulation of Golgi-to-plasma-membrane transport (both inclusion 1.00) concern unrelated biology (plasma lipoprotein clearance and Golgi vesicle trafficking), and Wnt protein secretion (0.37) is a weak outlier tied to lipidation rather than sphingolipids. No single description covers all the high-inclusion members without becoming an invented or overly broad umbrella.

name: Steroid and peptide hormone secretion regulation
rationale: Adds direct members on regulating IGF, corticotropin, and steroid hormone secretion to the child's steroidogenesis/sex differentiation scope, broadening from biosynthesis to secretion control of related endocrine axes.

name: Wnt and Hedgehog signalling in development
rationale: Repeated the parent name; distinguishes from sibling 'Notch signalling in organ development' by covering the Wnt and Hedgehog pathways instead of Notch.

name: Mitochondrial RNA transcription and processing
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'RNA processing and turnover'; narrowing to mitochondrial-specific transcription/processing distinguishes it from the broader RNA processing sibling.

name: FGFR signalling via PI3K and RAS/MAPK
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'PI3K/AKT axis' and sibling 'RTK to PI3K/AKT signalling'; specifying FGFR as the receptor and both downstream axes distinguishes it.

name: Adipose lipid storage and metabolic homeostasis
rationale: Not a duplicate and no sibling shares its focus on lipoprotein particle remodeling and triglyceride storage/transport.

name: Chondrocyte differentiation and endochondral bone formation
rationale: All three members concern chondrocyte maturation and its role in cartilage-to-bone conversion during skeletal growth.

name: Cell fate specification in embryonic patterning
rationale: The child (cell fate commitment) plus the direct members (dorsal spinal cord development, neural plate pattern specification) all concern embryonic regional patterning that assigns or commits cell identity in the nervous system and body axis; broader terms like general development would exceed what these members share.

name: Adhesion complex assembly
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Cell-cell junction organization' and overlaps parent 'Tight and adherens junction assembly'; renamed to emphasize adhesion complex formation broadly.

name: IL-1 driven inflammatory response
rationale: Core members (inflammatory response, HALLMARK inflammatory response, IL-1 family signaling, IL-1 processing, cell recruitment) converge on inflammasome/IL-1 cytokine maturation and downstream leukocyte recruitment; weaker members (positive regulation of response to external stimulus, IL-1 alpha production, CXCL1 production, each below 0.5) fit this same alarm-cytokine/inflammatory axis but are excluded from strict coverage.

name: TLR2 and LPS-mediated inflammatory signalling
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Innate immune sensing and inflammatory response', which shares inflammatory response and macrophage activation members; distinguishing by the TLR2/LPS-specific signaling emphasis unique to this theme's members.

name: Chromosome condensation regulation
rationale: Distinct from parents and siblings; focuses on condensin-mediated compaction rather than segregation fidelity, structure maintenance, kinetochore attachment, or cohesion.

name: Mitochondrial transcription and translation
rationale: Name duplicated parent theme's title 'Mitochondrial gene expression regulation'; revised to specify the transcription/translation processes, distinguishing it from the sibling theme focused solely on tRNA aminoacylation.

name: Sodium and potassium ion transport
rationale: All members involve plasma-membrane transporters, channels and pumps (chiefly Na+/K+-ATPase, cotransporters and channels) that move sodium and potassium ions or maintain their homeostasis.

name: Sodium and potassium ion transport homeostasis
rationale: All members concern maintenance or regulation of transmembrane sodium (and, in two, potassium) gradients via Na+/K+-ATPase, cotransporters, channels and their regulators; the broader inorganic ion homeostasis and import entries (0.89-1.00) are included because sodium/potassium handling dominates their described machinery.

name: Regulation of muscle contraction and excitability
rationale: One sibling is also literally named 'Sarcomere assembly and contraction' and includes muscle contraction/system process members, making the current name equally descriptive of it; the distinguishing feature of this theme is regulatory control of contraction and membrane excitability rather than the contraction process itself.

name: Chromatin, transcription and nuclear gene expression
rationale: Both children cover chromatin/DNA regulation and the general nuclear machinery producing gene expression, and the direct members extend into RNA polymerase II elongation and chromosome-linked gene regulation, all converging on nuclear control of gene expression.

name: IL-1-driven leukocyte recruitment
rationale: Distinct from parent (specifies IL-1 branch and leukocyte recruitment outcome vs broader IL-1/TNF signaling) and from sibling (alarmin/neutrophil/type2 focus differs from IL-1-driven leukocyte recruitment).

name: Nephron and collecting duct morphogenesis
rationale: The single child covers segment and collecting system development; direct members add patterning and duct formation events (proximal/distal pattern formation, nephric duct formation, general nephron development), so the parent needs a broader term covering formation and patterning as well as segment differentiation, without expanding beyond renal tubule morphogenesis.

name: Vascular tone and blood pressure regulation
rationale: Both children (angiotensin/endothelin hormonal control and smooth muscle contraction) plus the endothelin-mediated pressure regulation member converge on how vascular tone and pressure are physiologically controlled.

name: p53-mediated apoptotic stress response
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Cellular stress response and nutrient sensing' which shares the generic stress-response theme; narrowing to p53-driven apoptotic regulation, consistent with HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY and apoptosis-related members, separates it.

name: Heavy metal and drug detoxification
rationale: Overlapped with 'Metal ion homeostasis and cellular stress response', 'Metal and porphyrin homeostasis', and 'Xenobiotic and small-molecule conjugation metabolism'; narrowed to heavy metal detoxification and drug metabolism specifically.

name: Sensory and homeostatic behavioral processes
rationale: Repeated the parent name 'Behavioral neural circuits'; members involve olfactory/pheromone responses, respiratory regulation, sleep cycles, and social interaction rather than locomotor/exploratory behavior, which distinguishes it from the sibling.

name: Nucleotide catabolism and drug detoxification
rationale: Near-duplicate of sibling 'Nucleotide pool sanitation and catabolism'; this theme's members include TPMT/ribavirin drug metabolism and APRT salvage defects, which the sibling's deoxyribonucleotide-focused members lack.

name: Cardiac conduction system communication
rationale: The name 'Cardiac electrical activity' is broad enough to also describe the sibling 'Cardiac electrical repolarization', whose members are also cardiac electrical activity; this theme's members focus specifically on cell-to-cell conduction pathways and action potential propagation through the conduction system.

name: Chromatin remodeling in imprinted loci
rationale: Repeated parent's scope of histone/DNA marks; no siblings but name should specify imprinting context rather than generic chromatin modification.

name: Homologous recombination repair
rationale: Nearly indistinguishable from sibling 'DNA repair'; renamed to reflect its specific role in homologous recombination strand invasion, its parent theme.

name: DNA replication and translesion synthesis
rationale: Name collides with an identical theme elsewhere; revised to reflect its specific mix of replication and translesion synthesis members, distinguishing it from siblings covering recombination and general DNA repair.

name: RIG-I-mediated interferon induction pathway
rationale: Near-duplicate of parent name 'Type I interferon induction and signaling'; renamed to emphasize the RIG-I/IRF3 induction mechanism captured by its members, distinguishing it from the parent and from siblings focused on ISG effector mechanisms and inflammasome signaling.

name: Neurotransmitter transport and secretion regulation
rationale: Repeated the parent's theme ('Neurotransmitter release and transport') and overlapped with sibling's synaptic transmission focus; members are specifically about transport/secretion/uptake regulation, distinguishing it from the sibling's receptor clustering and GABAergic transmission focus.

name: Ciliary motility and left/right axis patterning
rationale: The child covers axoneme/cilia motility; the direct members are laterality-determination outcomes (heart tube, hindgut, digestive tract) driven by motile cilia at the embryonic node, so the union spans cilium-driven left/right patterning of developing organs.

name: Ribosome biogenesis
rationale: The RNA metabolism portion duplicated the parent 'mRNA metabolism' and overlapped siblings 'RNA processing and turnover'/'mRNA processing and turnover'; narrowing to ribosome biogenesis isolates the distinct ribosomal assembly focus.

name: Fibroproliferative wound healing response
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Vascular response to injury and hypoxia' and 'Cell adhesion and contractile machinery in tissue repair'; narrowed to the fibroproliferative/wound-closure aspect distinct from hypoxia-driven vascular signalling.

name: Leukocyte trafficking
rationale: All three children and representative members concern how leukocytes are recruited, adhere to endothelium and migrate into tissue via chemokines and integrins; 'trafficking' covers chemotaxis, adhesion and migration without repeating any child's exact name.

name: Mitotic cell cycle and organelle partitioning
rationale: No siblings and name is distinct from parent 'Cell cycle checkpoint control', covering mitotic progression and organelle partitioning rather than checkpoint control specifically.

name: Fibrinolysis and clot regulation
rationale: Repeats parent name 'Hemostasis and platelet-mediated cell adhesion' and duplicates sibling 'Hemostasis' exactly; needs to specify the distinct regulatory aspect it covers.

name: Cross-generational epigenetic memory maintenance
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Chromatin marking and imprinting' and repeated parent's chromatin theme; narrowed to focus on maintenance of imprinting across generations.

name: Locomotor and exploratory behaviour circuits
rationale: All five GO terms describe whole-organism locomotor or exploratory behaviours (locomotion, exploration, swimming, walking) and the dopaminergic/synaptic signalling that tunes them, with neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental genes contributing to circuit integrity underlying these behaviours.

name: Smooth muscle and fibroblast phenotypic remodeling
rationale: The name asserts an SRF mechanism not evidenced by the members, which describe smooth muscle/fibroblast differentiation, migration, and phenotypic switching rather than SRF signaling specifically; revised to describe the actual biological content while remaining distinct from the sibling's shear-stress/leukocyte trafficking theme.

name: Cell-matrix adhesion and cytoskeletal dynamics
rationale: Both children and all representative members concern integrin-based adhesion to substrate/matrix coupled to actin cytoskeletal regulation controlling migration; broader than either child individually since it spans adhesion regulation and actin bundling/assembly together.

name: Vascular wall remodelling and leukocyte trafficking
rationale: Covers smooth muscle phenotypic plasticity/contractile gene program and endothelial control of leukocyte extravasation, plus direct members on SRF-driven contractile genes, wound healing and connective tissue turnover in the vessel wall; broader than either child alone but still specific to vascular wall biology, not generic tissue remodelling.

name: Gene expression and post-translational protein modification
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; post-translational modification focus separates it from both.

name: Amino acid, nucleobase and vitamin B6 metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent 'Nitrogen assimilation pathways' and sibling 'Mitochondrial amino acid, cofactor and nitrogen metabolism'; no collision.

name: Spindle attachment and cytokinesis
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation and cell cycle control' which also covers sister chromatid separation; renamed to emphasize spindle-kinetochore attachment and cytokinesis, which are the distinguishing members of this theme.

name: Plasma membrane L-amino acid transport
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; also repeats parent term. Members specifically involve plasma membrane transport of L-amino acids, distinguishing from GABA-inclusive sibling.

name: Leukocyte adhesion and recruitment signalling
rationale: Both children cover leukocyte movement into tissue via chemotaxis/adhesion, and the direct members add chemokine/integrin/receptor signalling modules and inflammatory myeloid responses that drive the same recruitment process, so the parent broadens to the signalling underlying leukocyte adhesion and recruitment without becoming a generic immune-signalling label.

name: Muscle cell proliferation and differentiation
rationale: All four pathways concern control of proliferation (striated, general muscle, myoblast) or differentiation of muscle cell lineages, sharing overlapping growth factor and myogenic transcription factor regulation.

name: Craniofacial and cranial nerve development
rationale: Both children concern patterning and morphogenesis of head, face and pharyngeal structures; representative members like facial and vestibulocochlear nerve formation extend this to cranial nerve development, so the umbrella covers craniofacial organogenesis plus cranial nerve/organ formation without broadening to general embryonic patterning.

name: Myeloid and leukocyte differentiation
rationale: All three concern transcriptional and signalling control of haematopoietic progenitor commitment to leukocyte/myeloid lineages, including granulopoiesis regulators.

name: Galactose and pentose metabolism disorders
rationale: All three concern monosaccharide metabolism (galactose Leloir pathway or the glucuronate-xylulose pentose pathway) and the enzyme defects that disrupt it, including two galactosemia subtypes and essential pentosuria.

name: Myeloid and megakaryocyte differentiation
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to reflect the specific myeloid/megakaryocyte/platelet lineage focus of the members, distinguishing it from the other identically named theme.

name: Cortical spindle orientation cues
rationale: Collided with sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinesis machinery'; narrowed to cortical positioning cues distinct from the machinery components sibling covers.

name: Extrinsic apoptotic signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; clearly names the death-receptor pathway branch of apoptosis.

name: RTK signalling to RAS/MAPK
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Receptor tyrosine kinase signal transduction'; renamed to specify the RAS/MAPK downstream branch, distinguishing it from siblings covering oncogenic ERBB2 signalling and PI3K/AKT signalling.

name: Hematopoietic and immune cell differentiation
rationale: Covers the child's progenitor self-renewal regulation plus direct members spanning hematopoietic progenitor, leukocyte, lymphocyte and T cell differentiation, without narrowing to any single lineage.

name: Coagulation factor defects and cascade regulation
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent name 'Coagulation cascade and hemostasis'; revised to reflect the specific focus on clotting factor defects and cascade steps seen in the members.

name: NF-kB-driven inflammatory gene induction
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Death receptor-induced apoptosis and its regulation' on death receptor signaling; narrowed to NF-kB transcriptional inflammatory output to distinguish from apoptosis-focused sibling.

name: ERBB2 and RTK-driven oncogenic signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings: specifically about ERBB2/RTK oncogenic drivers, not general RTK signal transduction or PI3K/AKT signalling.

name: Neuronal signalling and synaptic connectivity
rationale: The two children cover synaptic neurotransmitter release/receptor signalling and broader neuronal connectivity/synaptic function; with no direct members to add, an umbrella spanning both signalling and structural connectivity of neurons fits without exceeding them.

name: Notch receptor processing and signalling
rationale: All members concern proteolytic and glycosylation-based processing of Notch receptors and regulation of the resulting signalling pathway.

name: Mitotic spindle and cell division
rationale: Covers both children (spindle/chromosome segregation, cytokinesis, organelle inheritance) plus the direct member centrosome localization, all steps of organizing the mitotic apparatus and dividing the cell; broader terms like 'cell cycle' would exceed what's present.

name: Kidney and glomerular development
rationale: Both children concern building the kidney's tubular and vascular architecture (nephron/kidney morphogenesis and mesangial/capillary tuft development), and no direct members exist to broaden this further.

name: G1/S checkpoint control
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers broader checkpoint control) and from siblings (phase transitions, mitotic division); G1/S checkpoint control is specific to that particular checkpoint.

name: RNA polymerase I and III transcription and rRNA processing
rationale: Repeats parent's theme too broadly; sibling 'Nuclear and mitochondrial RNA polymerase transcription' also involves RNA polymerase I transcription elongation, so specifying Pol I/III and rRNA processing distinguishes this theme.

name: Ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing
rationale: Repeated the parent 'Ribosome biogenesis' and overlapped ambiguously with sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and mRNA surveillance'; specifying rRNA processing distinguishes it from the mRNA-focused sibling.

name: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'mRNA processing and turnover' and sibling 'mRNA stability regulation'; narrowing to a specific decay pathway distinguishes it.

name: Catecholamine and phenolic amine catabolism
rationale: All three pathways center on oxidative/conjugative degradation of catecholamines and related phenolic amines via MAO, COMT, sulfotransferases and the dopamine transporter, terminating their signalling.

name: Wnt and Hedgehog signalling
rationale: Covers the Hedgehog/GLI child plus the direct Wnt pathway members (canonical and beta-catenin), the two morphogen cascades that co-occur here; no broader category term is needed.

name: Sarcoplasmic calcium transport in muscle contraction
rationale: Overlaps with siblings both named around calcium signalling and muscle contraction; this theme is distinguished by sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium transport and striated muscle-specific contraction regulation, not general calcium/membrane signalling.

name: Ribosomal RNA transcription and ribosome assembly
rationale: Distinct from parent (parent covers rRNA processing generally, this focuses on transcription and assembly) and from sibling (RNA biogenesis and processing is broader/different scope).

name: Regulation of lipid biosynthetic processes
rationale: Nearly duplicates parent 'Lipid and cholesterol homeostasis regulation'; members focus specifically on cholesterol/fatty acid/lipid biosynthesis regulation, distinguishing it from the sibling's transport/uptake focus.

The single child covers virus-host antiviral restriction, while the direct members concern SRP-dependent cotranslational ER protein targeting, an unrelated translational/secretory process; no honest umbrella joins antiviral immunity with ER protein targeting short of a vacuous term like 'cellular processes'.

name: Gametogenesis and reproductive development
rationale: Distinct from all siblings including 'Hormone-responsive reproductive development'; no parent to collide with as a root theme.

name: Telomere maintenance and capping
rationale: All members concern regulation of telomere length or protection of chromosome ends by shelterin and associated factors, including negative regulation of DNA metabolic processes as it applies to telomere/replication restraint and centromere maintenance in the Reactome member.

name: Cardiac ion channel regulation
rationale: Both children and all representative members concern control of ion channel activity, trafficking and gating that shapes cardiac membrane potential and action potentials, narrower than general excitability or ion transport.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression regulation
rationale: Union of the mitochondrial gene expression child with direct members covering regulation of mitochondrial RNA/DNA catabolism, mitoribosome assembly, mitochondrial rRNA processing and translation control - all regulatory layers over mitochondrial gene output, not the core process itself.

name: VEGF-mediated angiogenic sprouting
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'VEGF signalling in vascular and lymphatic development'; narrowed to the angiogenic sprouting process specifically, distinguishing from the signalling-focused sibling.

name: Gliogenesis and glial proliferation control
rationale: No sibling addresses glial proliferation or gliogenesis specifically; name is distinct from parent's broader proteinopathy/glial fate scope.

name: Gliogenesis and glial proliferation control
rationale: All four members concern regulation of glial cell generation (astrocyte, oligodendrocyte) or proliferation from neural progenitors, sharing overlapping regulators like Notch/HES and cytokine signalling.

name: Coagulation cascade regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Hemostasis' and parent's hemostasis/platelet terms; narrowed to the coagulation cascade specifically to distinguish it.

name: Extracellular matrix remodelling in vascular repair
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Extracellular matrix and connective tissue integrity' and 'Vascular injury response and wound healing'; narrowed to matrix remodelling specifically during vascular repair processes.

name: Nucleoside phosphate metabolic processes
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; members concern nucleoside/nucleotide metabolic and biosynthetic processes without transport, so renamed to reflect that specifically.

name: Damaged base recognition and excision
rationale: Repeated the parent term 'base excision repair'; new name specifies the sub-step without reusing parent's name.

name: Base excision repair initiation by DNA glycosylases
rationale: All five members describe the glycosylase-mediated recognition and excision of damaged bases (uracil, oxidised or alkylated bases, deaminated pyrimidines) that generates an AP site, the first step of base-excision repair.

name: Meiotic germ cell division
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Germ cell meiosis and fertilisation'; renamed to focus specifically on the meiotic division process, distinct from sibling 'Sperm-egg fertilisation'.

name: Macrophage cholesterol handling in foam cell formation
rationale: Name is already distinct from parents and sibling; it specifically identifies macrophage foam cell formation, not a general term.

name: Macrophage cholesterol handling and foam cell formation
rationale: All members concern cellular responses to sterols, lipids and lipoproteins that drive macrophage cholesterol uptake, efflux and foam cell differentiation in atherosclerosis.

name: Somatotropic axis growth regulation
rationale: All members involve hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal or growth hormone/IGF endocrine signalling that sets body growth rate and its positive or negative regulation.

name: Leukocyte and cell migration signalling
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; it uniquely covers chemotaxis/migration signaling, unlike differentiation, apoptosis, or cytokine-focused siblings.

name: Mitotic and meiotic division machinery
rationale: Covers the mitotic apparatus/segregation children plus centrosome and meiotic spindle-assembly members, tightening beyond a bare 'cell division' to the structural machinery of chromosome segregation in both division types.

name: PI3K and RAS/MAPK signalling
rationale: Repeated parent name 'FGFR signalling via PI3K and RAS/MAPK'; renamed to specify the two branches distinguishing it from the sibling phospholipase C pathway.

name: Lipid mediator signalling
rationale: Both children and the GPCR/leukotriene/prostaglandin examples concern lipid-derived mediators (eicosanoids, pro-resolving lipids) and their receptor-based signalling and biosynthesis; no direct members exist outside the children.

name: Chaperone-mediated protein quality control
rationale: Overlapped with parent's 'protein degradation' and could be confused with sibling 'Ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation'; specifying chaperone-mediated quality control distinguishes it as the non-proteasomal folding/quality-control pathway.

name: Kinase feedback inhibition control
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Regulation of protein phosphorylation and modification' which already covers kinase-mediated regulation; needs a more specific distinguishing mechanism.

name: Amino acid and biogenic solute transport and metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; focuses specifically on amino acid and biogenic solute transport, unlike siblings covering micronutrients, ions, lipids, or nucleotides.

name: Adipocyte triglyceride storage
rationale: Distinct from parent (which includes phospholipids) and from sibling (which covers lipolysis broadly); specifies adipocyte-specific triglyceride storage.

name: Taste perception and transduction
rationale: Combines the sensory transduction channel child with direct members specifically about taste (general and sour), broader than the channel-only child but not extended to other sensory modalities.

name: TGF-beta/SMAD tumour suppressor signalling and its loss in cancer
rationale: Four members directly concern TGF-beta receptor-SMAD signalling and its cancer-associated disruption (receptor complex, SMAD2/3 phosphorylation mutants, TGFBR2 kinase mutants), and two concern RUNX3, a TGF-beta/SMAD-linked transcription factor mediating growth arrest and apoptosis (BIM induction). Anoikis regulation shares the theme of anchorage/apoptotic control tied to tumour suppression and is included as the weakest link via shared BCL2-family apoptotic gatekeeping, though it does not itself involve TGF-beta or RUNX3 directly.

name: Androgen and estrogen receptor signalling
rationale: Repeats parent name closer to specific hierarchy; renamed to reflect the specific androgen/estrogen receptor focus of members, distinguishing from circadian sibling.

name: Nucleotide-sugar and amino sugar metabolism
rationale: The current name overlaps with sibling 'Glycan metabolism and Golgi processing', which also involves glycan/Golgi-related processes (GPI anchor, glycoprotein biosynthesis); the revised name is more specific to the nucleotide-sugar and amino sugar biosynthetic/catabolic focus of this theme's members.

name: Hypersensitivity and allergic effector responses
rationale: Covers the antibody-mediated hypersensitivity child plus direct members on mast cell, eosinophil, Th2 and IL-33 driven allergic-type effector biology, without repeating the child's antibody-specific framing.

name: Hormone-responsive transcriptional activation
rationale: Child covers positive regulation of DNA binding and RNA polymerase II transcription; direct members add thyroid hormone response and mitochondrial biogenesis, which is itself induced via thyroid-hormone-driven transcriptional programmes. The umbrella is transcriptional activation triggered by hormone signalling, broader than the child alone but not extending to unrelated transcriptional control.

name: Chaperone-mediated protein folding
rationale: All members concern chaperone-assisted folding or refolding of proteins, including the specialized post-chaperonin tubulin folding pathway.

name: Neuronal cytoskeletal remodeling in projection growth and branching
rationale: All four members regulate cytoskeletal processes (microtubule nucleation, filopodial actin dynamics) that drive neuron projection outgrowth, branching, and arborization.
Both children are identically named 'Gametogenesis and reproductive development' and there are no direct members, so the parent would simply restate the child rather than add anything.

name: RTK signalling to PI3K/AKT axis
rationale: Repeats parent 'RTK signalling via PI3K/AKT axis' and overlaps sibling 'Receptor tyrosine kinase to PI3K/AKT signalling'; needs specific downstream node distinction.

name: Nephron patterning and ureteric development
rationale: The current name also fits sibling 'Nephron and kidney tubule development', which shares kidney morphogenesis, cell differentiation, and nephron development; this theme's distinct members involve ureter/nephric duct formation and glomerulus/proximal-distal patterning.

name: Nephron segment patterning
rationale: No siblings and name is more specific than parent, focusing on segment patterning rather than overall morphogenesis.

name: Intracellular protein trafficking and degradation
rationale: Covers the child's vesicular/lysosomal trafficking plus the direct members' proteasome assembly and ubiquitin-independent degradation, unifying vesicular and proteasomal routes for moving and disposing of cellular proteins without naming either mechanism exclusively.

name: Hair cycle phases and epidermal delamination
rationale: Overlaps sibling 'Epidermal differentiation and cornification' which shares epithelial differentiation and epidermis development members; revised to emphasize the distinguishing anagen/molting/delamination phase content.

name: Androgen and estrogen receptor signalling
rationale: No members reference retinoic acid; all are androgen, estrogen, or progesterone receptor pathways, and this name is more specific and doesn't overlap with the mammary gland development sibling.

name: Neuronal projection outgrowth and regeneration
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers broader neurite/cell shape morphogenesis) and from sibling (which covers cytoskeletal shaping/process outgrowth generally); this theme specifically addresses neuronal projection outgrowth and regeneration.

name: Non-sulfur amino acid metabolism
rationale: Name duplicated the sibling theme exactly and overlapped with parent 'Sulfur amino acid metabolism'; narrowed to exclude sulfur amino acids, distinguishing it from both.

name: Complement activation and humoral regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader humoral effectors) and sibling (antimicrobial peptides); already specific to complement activation.

name: Complement cascade regulation
rationale: Repeats parent 'Complement activation and regulation' too closely; more specific to focus on complement pathway regulation, distinguishing from antimicrobial peptide sibling.

name: Coordinated mitochondrial-cytosolic translation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Protein translation' and paralleled 'Mitochondrial gene expression'; revised to emphasize the coordination between the two compartments' protein synthesis, distinguishing it from siblings.

name: IRF3/IRF7-mediated type I interferon induction
rationale: Covers the child (type I interferon response) plus the direct members, both TICAM1/TBK1/IKKε-driven IRF3/IRF7 activation steps upstream of interferon production, without broadening to all innate sensing.

name: Beta cell glucose sensing and insulin release
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Insulin biosynthesis and secretion' and 'Glucose and lipid metabolic regulation'; narrowed to the specific beta cell glucose-sensing mechanism distinguishing it from siblings like 'Insulin signalling to glucose uptake'.

name: rRNA processing and modification
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Nucleolar RNA modification and snoRNP assembly' which covers snRNA modification and related processes; narrowing to emphasize rRNA-specific processing distinguishes it while remaining true to members like rRNA processing and modification in nucleus/cytosol.

name: Amino acid and bile acid transport and catabolism
rationale: Name is unique in the hierarchy and its emphasis on amino acid transport does not match any sibling's members (e.g., bile acid sibling focuses on bile acid signaling, not amino acid transport).

name: Neurotransmitter release and receptor signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent's broader developmental scope and from siblings focused on morphogenesis/connectivity and structural synapse organization; this theme specifically covers neurotransmitter release and receptor signaling mechanisms.

name: Sister chromatid cohesion and chromosome condensation
rationale: Covers the child (cohesion maintenance) plus direct members on establishing cohesion and regulating chromosome condensation, both aspects of mitotic chromosome structure control; no broader term like 'chromosome segregation' is needed since spindle attachment biology is absent.

name: Coordinated replication-repair synthesis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'DNA repair synthesis and replication restart' and echoed parent terms; renamed to emphasize the coupled replication/repair synthesis mechanism distinguishing it from replication restart and polymerase-mediated repair alone.

name: Somatotropic axis and body growth control
rationale: Members at inclusion >=0.5 converge on growth hormone/IGF1 signalling, GDNF-RET neurotrophic signalling, and body-size regulation (growth rate, organism growth, negative regulation of growth). Weakly included members (btm neuronal specification 0.29, eating behavior 0.36, cellular response to leptin 0.30) are excluded as they concern appetite/feeding and neuronal identity rather than growth axis control.

name: p53-mediated stress response
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Stress and nutrient signalling with p53' without distinguishing itself; renamed to specify the p53-centric focus, differentiating from siblings 'Nutrient sensing' and 'mTOR/stress signalling'.

name: Endosomal TLR-driven IRF3/IRF7 activation
rationale: The child covers endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLR signalling, and the direct members (TICAM1-dependent and TBK1/IKKε-mediated IRF3/IRF7 activation) are the downstream signalling steps of that same TRIF-dependent axis; xenophagy regulation (0.36) is weakly included and not reflected in the name.

name: Poly(A) signal-dependent termination
rationale: Repeats parent 'mRNA 3' end formation' concept; narrowing to the polyadenylation-signal-coupled termination mechanism distinguishes it as a specific sub-process.

name: Mammary gland development and epithelial proliferation
rationale: All members concern hormone-driven growth of mammary epithelium: ductal outgrowth, branching, alveolar development and puberty onset, and their shared proliferative control.

name: Neurotrophin and p75/Trk signalling in neuronal injury and regeneration
rationale: Distinct from parent (adhesion in myelination) and sibling (junction organization in CNS myelination); this theme focuses on neurotrophin/p75/Trk signaling in injury and regeneration, a different mechanistic focus.

name: Hypoxia and HIF signalling
rationale: All members concern cellular oxygen sensing and the HIF pathway: HIF-alpha stabilization, prolyl hydroxylation, VHL-mediated degradation, and downstream hypoxic gene expression driving glycolysis and angiogenesis.

name: Nucleotide catabolism and salvage
rationale: Near-duplicate of sibling 'Nucleotide pool sanitization and catabolism' which shares the same core members (nucleotide catabolism, NUDT hydrolysis, NTP catabolism); revised to reflect this theme's distinct salvage/deoxyribonucleotide catabolism content (APRT salvage, dGMP, deoxyribonucleotide metabolism).

name: Nucleotide and phosphate metabolism
rationale: Both children concern nucleotide biosynthesis/metabolism and phosphate handling, and representative members (GTP biosynthesis, NADPH regeneration via phosphate pathways, phosphorus metabolism) fit this union without extending to unrelated biology.

name: DNA replication and repair synthesis
rationale: Covers origin licensing, elongation, and repair-associated synthesis steps that together constitute genome duplication and its repair-linked synthesis, without extending to unrelated repair pathways like excision or mismatch correction.

name: Interferon-stimulated gene antiviral defence
rationale: Overlaps heavily with siblings 'Viral life cycle and host antiviral defence' and 'Host-virus molecular interactions' which cover viral process/genome replication; the distinguishing feature of this theme is specifically ISG/interferon-driven antiviral mechanisms rather than general host-virus interaction.

name: Plasma lipoprotein remodeling and lipid absorption
rationale: Union covers lipoprotein particle remodeling (VLDL, HDL) and intestinal lipid/cholesterol absorption and transport, all centered on circulating lipid and lipoprotein handling.

name: Cytokine and interferon signalling
rationale: Covers the child's interferon-stimulated antiviral effectors plus the broader cytokine-mediated signalling and IFNA/IFNB regulation members; the weakly-included GO cytokine-signaling term (0.29) fits comfortably under this umbrella too.

name: Calcineurin-dependent cardiac hypertrophy signalling
rationale: Core members (calcineurin-mediated signalling and its negative regulation, muscle hypertrophy in response to stress, positive regulation of muscle adaptation, negative regulation of cardiac muscle tissue growth, positive regulation of cardiac muscle contraction) all converge on calcium/calcineurin-NFAT signalling driving or restraining cardiac/muscle hypertrophic growth. The weakly included IGF receptor signalling member (0.25) is excluded as it does not concern calcineurin or cardiac growth directly.

name: Glycosaminoglycan degradation and mucopolysaccharidoses
rationale: All members concern lysosomal stepwise breakdown of heparan/chondroitin/dermatan sulfate chains and the storage diseases caused by blocking single steps in that pathway.

name: Steroid hormone receptor transcriptional response
rationale: Not a duplicate; sibling concerns regulatory processes of signaling pathways (GO terms), while this theme covers hallmark transcriptional response gene sets, so the name does not fit the sibling.

name: Nucleotide biosynthesis and metabolism
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Nucleotide degradation and salvage' by including turnover; renamed to focus on biosynthesis and general metabolism, distinguishing it from parent's degradation/salvage focus.

name: Deoxyribonucleotide catabolism and salvage
rationale: Name overlapped with parent 'Nucleotide pool metabolism and salvage' and sibling 'Nucleotide pool homeostasis and salvage' which share similar pyrimidine deoxyribonucleotide members; the theme's actual focus is deoxyribonucleotide breakdown and salvage enzymes (NUDT, APRT), which is more specific and distinguishes it.

name: Myoblast proliferation, fusion and differentiation
rationale: The sibling 'Regulation of muscle growth and adaptation' shares the same top members (negative regulation of myotube differentiation, striated muscle cell proliferation, regeneration), so the original broad name fit both; the revision highlights the myoblast-specific proliferation/fusion/differentiation focus unique to this theme.

name: Transcriptional control of myeloid differentiation
rationale: The child covers leukocyte/myeloid differentiation broadly, while the direct members (RUNX1, RUNX2, NOTCH2) are specific transcription factors driving myeloid lineage differentiation programs, so the parent unites both under transcriptional regulation of myeloid/leukocyte fate.

name: Cardiac electrical excitability and coupling
rationale: Covers the sinoatrial node/conduction child plus direct members on membrane depolarization regulation and electrical coupling between cells, all centered on excitable-tissue electrophysiology.

name: Insulin regulation of glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis
rationale: All three concern insulin-responsive control of glucose transporter trafficking (negative and positive) and glycogen synthase activity via overlapping IRS/PI3K/AKT and GSK3 machinery.

name: Motile cilia assembly and beat regulation
rationale: No siblings and name is more specific than parent, focusing on motile cilia assembly and beat regulation rather than general ciliary regulation of embryonic patterning.

name: Motile cilia and axoneme assembly
rationale: All members concern building or regulating motile cilia/axonemes and the centriole amplification that underlies multiciliogenesis, distinct from primary cilium signalling.

name: Branched-chain amino acid catabolic disorders
rationale: No sibling collisions and distinct from parent, which covers broader amino acid and carbon metabolism, not specifically BCAA catabolic disorders.

name: Spindle checkpoint and abscission machinery
rationale: Nearly identical to parent name 'Spindle assembly and cytokinetic apparatus' and overlaps sibling 'Cell division and cytokinesis'; revised to highlight checkpoint and abscission specifics.

name: Chromosome segregation regulation
rationale: Repeated parent 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinesis apparatus' terms; narrowing to chromosome segregation distinguishes it from parent and from sibling 'Mitotic and meiotic division machinery'.

name: Cholesterol biosynthesis regulation
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than parent by naming cholesterol specifically.

name: Glucose and cAMP/PKA hormonal signalling
rationale: Members converge on glucose/carbohydrate sensing (carbohydrate signalling, carbon catabolite regulation), glucagon-cAMP-PKA signalling, and ketone/steroid responses that feed into the same cAMP-PKA-CREB axis; GLP1 (0.25) is a weakly included, more peripheral incretin-specific example.

name: Sister chromatid cohesion maintenance
rationale: All three members concern establishing, regulating, or reinforcing sister chromatid cohesion via cohesin, shugoshin/BUB1 protection, and SMC5/6-NSMCE2 pathways.

name: Lymphocyte development and activation
rationale: Distinct from parent (which spans lymphocytes and monocyte/dendritic cells) and from sibling (which is specific to B lymphocyte humoral identity); this theme covers broader lymphocyte development and activation processes.

name: Cellular stress and oxygen-level response
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; siblings focus on hormonal/endocrine signalling while this covers cellular stress and hypoxia response, no collision.

name: Receptor internalization, recycling and degradation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader trafficking/signalling term) and sibling (specific to RTK), and describes the internalization/recycling/degradation fates generically applicable across receptor types.

name: Receptor internalization, recycling and degradation
rationale: All four pathways govern the surface abundance of receptors via endocytic uptake, recycling versus lysosomal sorting, and ubiquitin-dependent catabolism, illustrated recurrently by LDL receptor/PCSK9 handling and synaptic receptor trafficking.

name: Cardiac morphogenesis and valve formation
rationale: Duplicate name already used elsewhere; revised to reflect the specific focus on cardiac chamber, valve, and outflow tract morphogenesis.

name: Amino acid metabolism for translation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Translation and protein biosynthesis' and sibling's protein modification focus; narrowed to metabolic support of translation.

name: Dendritic and neurite cytoskeletal remodeling
rationale: Distinct from both parents and all listed siblings; no repetition or overlap requiring narrowing.

name: Inflammatory caspase activation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Death receptor signalling and NF-kappaB regulation' on NF-kB content; renamed to focus on the distinct apoptotic/caspase mechanism specific to this theme.

name: Cardiac chamber and valve morphogenesis
rationale: Repeated parent 'Heart development' and overlapped with sibling's morphogenesis scope; narrowed to chamber and valve formation, distinct from conduction system development.

name: General mitotic cell cycle
rationale: Repeats parent's themes (E2F-driven cell cycle regulation; General mitotic cell cycle regulation) without adding specificity; renamed to reflect the broad mitotic cell cycle members without duplicating parent phrasing.

name: Cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; no collision.

name: Neutrophil and myeloid degranulation
rationale: All three pathways concern regulated granule exocytosis by myeloid effector cells (neutrophils/macrophages) as the mechanism of antimicrobial immunity, mediated by SNAREs, integrins and Fc receptor signalling.

name: Regulation of serine/threonine kinase signalling
rationale: All members concern control of protein phosphorylation, with the two more specific ones focused on serine/threonine kinase activity regulation and its negative arm, nested within the broader phosphorylation-regulation theme.

name: Small-molecule carbohydrate and glycerol metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; no other theme covers small-molecule carbohydrate/glycerol metabolism specifically.

Members mix intracellular transport regulation (protein trafficking to surface, ER, endosomes), translation silencing, an atypical Rho GTPase degradation pathway, and activity-dependent transcription factor regulation; no single description covers housekeeping regulators, transport control, translational repression, and NPAS4 gene regulation without becoming an uninformative catch-all.

name: Excitation-contraction coupling in muscle
rationale: Repeats parent's calcium cycling theme and overlaps sibling 'Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium reuptake and muscle relaxation' which also covers calcium cycling in sarcoplasmic reticulum.

name: Vascular and connective tissue repair remodelling
rationale: Covers the angiogenesis/vessel-repair child plus direct members on fibroblast migration, ECM organization and connective tissue replacement, all facets of tissue repair remodelling; broader than 'angiogenesis' alone but excludes unrelated matrix biology.

name: Viral genome replication and entry regulation
rationale: The generic name overlaps with sibling themes like 'Viral life cycle and host antiviral defence' and 'HIV replication and host restriction'; this theme specifically covers regulation of viral genome replication, entry, and HIV assembly/transcription, which better distinguishes it.

name: Steroid and hormone biosynthesis and regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically covers steroid/hormone biosynthesis and its regulation, not overlapping with axis regulation, insulin, growth/appetite, or stress response themes.

name: E-cadherin adhesion regulation and turnover
rationale: All three members concern CDH1/E-cadherin-based homotypic adhesion, including its transcriptional and post-translational regulation and degradation.

name: Imprinted locus epigenetic memory
rationale: Repeated both parents' combined scope without adding specificity; renamed to reflect the intersection of imprinting and cross-generational memory maintenance.

name: Purine and pyrimidine nucleotide biosynthesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader metabolism/salvage) and sibling (salvage/catabolism vs biosynthesis); no collision.

name: Ribose phosphate and nucleotide biosynthesis
rationale: Nearly duplicated the parent 'Nucleotide biosynthesis, salvage and metabolism'; members center on ribose phosphate metabolism and monophosphate biosynthesis, distinguishing it from the salvage-focused sibling.

name: GPCR-coupled adenylate cyclase and calmodulin signalling
rationale: The original name duplicated the parent's scope and would equally describe the sibling 'Cyclic nucleotide signalling', which shares members like cAMP biosynthesis and GPCR-coupled cyclic nucleotide signaling; the revised name highlights the receptor-triggered adenylate cyclase/calmodulin focus unique to this theme.

name: Axon-glia adhesion in myelination and neural regeneration
rationale: Distinct from all siblings, including Gliogenesis and glial proliferation control and Neuronal development and synaptic transmission; no collision.

name: Smooth muscle contraction and relaxation
rationale: All three members concern the calcium/myosin contractile machinery of smooth muscle and its regulatory relaxation pathways (NO-cGMP, cAMP, Rho-ROCK).

name: Regulation of angiogenesis and vessel repair
rationale: Core members (all at inclusion ≥0.9) concern positive or negative regulation of endothelial cell proliferation, vasculature development, and angiogenesis in wound/vascular repair; weakly included smooth muscle adaptation (0.32) and general inflammatory wound healing (0.47) are excluded as they extend beyond endothelial/vascular growth control.

name: Nephron and collecting duct morphogenesis
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent by including nephron morphogenesis alongside collecting duct development.

name: Th1, Th2, and Th17 subset differentiation and response
rationale: Name closely repeated the parent's wording without adding specificity; members focus on Th1/Th2/Th17 lineage commitment and responses, distinguishing it from the sibling's broader CD4 T cell activation/regulatory differentiation focus.

name: Paranodal axon-glial junction assembly
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Axon-glia adhesion in myelination and neural regeneration'; narrowed to the specific paranodal junction assembly process distinguishing it from that broader adhesion parent and the neurotrophin signalling sibling.

name: Nucleotide and phosphate group metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Nucleotide and cellular energy metabolism' and 'Nucleotide and phosphoinositide metabolism'; narrowed to focus specifically on phosphate group biochemistry rather than energy or phosphoinositide signaling.

name: rRNA and snoRNP maturation
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to reflect the rRNA processing and snoRNP assembly focus, distinguishing it from the sibling's mitochondrial gene expression emphasis.

name: Nucleotide and methyl-group metabolism disorders
rationale: Distinct from parent (adds methyl-group metabolism scope) and from sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism' which is not about disorders.

name: GTPase-driven cytoskeletal and vascular signalling
rationale: Rap1, G12/13, RND1 GTPase cycles and VEGFR2 pathways converge on Rho/Rap-family GTPase control of the actin cytoskeleton, adhesion and endothelial/vascular responses; thrombin-PAR signalling (0.25) is excluded as weakly included.

name: Chromatin factor recruitment and dynamics
rationale: No sibling collision and name is more specific than parent, focusing on chromatin factor recruitment rather than nuclear envelope dynamics.

name: mRNA processing and turnover
rationale: Distinguishes itself from parent by specifying processing/turnover mechanisms, and from siblings by focusing on mRNA specifically rather than general RNA or ribosome biogenesis.

name: Bilirubin and heme catabolism
rationale: Collided with 'Xenobiotic and small-molecule conjugation metabolism' and 'Metal and xenobiotic homeostasis'; narrowed to bilirubin/heme breakdown pathway specifically.

name: Homologous recombination repair
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'DNA repair pathways' and sibling 'Base excision repair'; narrowed to the recombination-specific repair mechanism distinguishing it from base excision and replication synthesis repair.

name: Endothelial shear stress mechanotransduction
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling, referring specifically to shear stress mechanotransduction rather than leukocyte adhesion regulation.

name: Endothelial mechanotransduction and shear stress response
rationale: All five pathways describe how endothelial cells (and, in the broader mechanical-stimuli entry, other mechanosensitive cells) convert fluid shear stress or mechanical force into signalling that governs vascular quiescence versus inflammation.

name: Protein quality control and aggregate clearance
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader folding/turnover) and sibling (proteolysis/maturation); focuses on quality control and aggregate clearance specifically.

name: Coagulation cascade initiation and hemostasis
rationale: Collides with an identical name used elsewhere; retitled to reflect the cascade initiation/amplification and hemostasis members, distinguishing it from the sibling focused on factor VIII defects.

name: rRNA transcription and processing
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and nuclear RNA metabolism', which also covers ribosome/rRNA maturation; this theme's members focus specifically on rRNA transcription (Pol I/III) and processing, distinguishing it from the sibling's export/decay focus and the parent's broader splicing/elongation scope.

name: Nucleotide excision and cross-link repair
rationale: Name duplicated an existing theme elsewhere; members specifically involve nucleotide-excision repair and interstrand cross-link repair, distinguishing from sibling themes on mismatch and double-strand break repair.

name: Cyclic nucleotide second messenger signalling
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no other theme covers cyclic nucleotide second messenger signalling specifically.

name: Mesoderm patterning and cell fate commitment
rationale: Both children concern embryonic axial/mesodermal patterning, and the representative members (cell fate determination, mesodermal cell fate commitment, somitogenesis) show the union spans segmentation patterning together with the lineage-commitment decisions that follow it.

name: Skeletal dysplasias from glycosaminoglycan defects
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Glycosaminoglycan metabolism and its disorders'; narrowed focus to skeletal disorder phenotypes specifically.

name: Upregulation of lipid biosynthesis
rationale: All three members concern positive regulation of fatty acid, lipid, and lipid biosynthetic processes, sharing transcriptional regulators (SREBP, PPARA, LXR) that drive lipogenic output.

name: Neurotransmitter release and transport
rationale: Covers both children (synaptic transmission/receptor assembly and neurotransmitter release) plus the direct member GABA secretion, uniting vesicular loading, reuptake, and calcium-triggered release of transmitters generally, without restating either child's specific scope.

name: Purine ribonucleoside salvage and catabolism
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Nucleotide pool homeostasis and salvage' which shares deoxyribonucleoside monophosphate catabolic process; members here focus on purine/ribonucleoside salvage-catabolism, distinguishing it from the pyrimidine deoxyribonucleotide focus of siblings.

name: Coordinated mitochondrial-nuclear gene expression
rationale: Distinguishes from parent's broader scope and sibling's ncRNA focus by specifying cross-compartment coordination of gene expression.

name: TAK1/NIK-mediated NF-kappaB and JNK activation
rationale: No siblings and name is already specific, distinguishing itself from parent by naming the mediators and downstream pathways (NF-kappaB and JNK).

name: Endogenous antigen presentation via MHC class I
rationale: Name is already specific (endogenous/MHC class I pathway) and distinct from the broader sibling and parent.

name: Amino acid catabolism
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Small-molecule carbohydrate and glycerol metabolism' and overlaps with xenobiotic conjugation sibling; narrowed to reflect amino acid-specific catabolic focus distinct from parent's broader micronutrient scope.

name: Telomere maintenance
rationale: Both children (protein-cap-based and recombination-based telomere maintenance) and representative members (mitotic recombination, its regulation, telomere recombination) converge on maintaining chromosome ends and stability; no direct members push beyond this scope.

name: Transcription and RNA processing machinery
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Chromatin, transcription and nuclear gene expression'; narrowed to distinguish from sibling 'Chromatin and DNA methylation regulation' by focusing on transcription/RNA processing components.

name: Cardiac action potential repolarization
rationale: All three concern control of ventricular/cardiac membrane repolarization and its plateau phase via delayed rectifier and L-type channel machinery, linked to QT interval regulation.

name: Glutamatergic synaptic signalling and neurotransmitter release
rationale: Covers the child (synaptic release/uptake) plus the direct members, all centered on glutamatergic transmission and trans-synaptic signalling regulation; the AUTS16 member (0.28) is weakly included and excluded from the core claim.

name: Glycosaminoglycan metabolism and related disorders
rationale: The current name is broader than the members, which focus specifically on GAG biosynthesis/degradation and associated diseases (not general ECM structural biology), and overlaps with the parent 'Proteoglycan and glycosaminoglycan metabolism'; the revised name is more specific and still distinct from the sibling's focus on glycoprotein/proteoglycan biosynthesis disorders.

name: Nuclear-encoded cytosolic and mitochondrial expression
rationale: Too similar to sibling and unclear differentiation from parent; revised to specify nuclear-encoded genes with dual localization products.

name: Nephron and kidney morphogenesis
rationale: All three describe the developmental programme of kidney/nephron induction, patterning and cell differentiation from ureteric bud and metanephric mesenchyme.

The union spans dozens of unrelated cellular processes (proteostasis, mitochondrial biology, membrane trafficking, apoptosis regulation, adipogenesis, RUNX/MITF transcriptional programs, blood group biochemistry, GPCR signalling) with no shared biology tighter than 'cellular regulatory processes', which is too vacuous to serve as a name.

name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium cycling
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Muscle contraction and ion homeostasis'; narrowed to the specific calcium-handling mechanism distinguishing this theme.

name: Microtubule-based organelle and cargo transport
rationale: Covers both children's organelle/vesicle transport along microtubules plus the direct member's dendritic transport of a receptor complex, a specific cargo carried by the same microtubule motor machinery.

name: Cardiac looping and chamber formation
rationale: Identical to sibling theme name 'Heart morphogenesis'; specifying looping and chamber formation distinguishes it from the duplicate sibling and from the parent's focus on ventricular wall growth and trabeculation.

name: Protein export and secretion pathways
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Insulin secretion and incretin regulation' due to shared insulin/hormone secretion members; narrowing to the export/localization aspect (protein localization to extracellular region, export from cell) distinguishes it.

name: Cortical cytoskeleton and cell polarity
rationale: All members involve actin/microtubule cortical machinery (septin rings, cortical microtubules, centrosome positioning) that establishes cell polarity axes (apicobasal, monopolar) or drives polarized cell migration (podocytes), converging on Rho-GTPase and cortex-anchoring proteins shared across the set.

name: Epithelial and stromal cell migration in wound healing
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from the parent, which focuses on adhesion/contractile machinery rather than migration.

name: Amino acid metabolism and one-carbon biosynthesis
rationale: Combines the amino acid catabolism child with methionine biosynthesis/salvage and folate-compound biosynthesis, all centered on amino acid and related one-carbon/methyl-group metabolism; broader than 'catabolism' alone to capture the biosynthetic direct members.

name: Post-Golgi carrier transport to the cell surface
rationale: Covers vesicle coat/tethering machinery, post-Golgi vesicle transport, Golgi-to-plasma-membrane delivery, and the VxPx ciliary cargo route, all of which move cargo from Golgi-derived carriers outward to plasma membrane or cilium; tighter than general secretory transport since it excludes ER-to-Golgi and retrograde/endosomal steps.

name: Vesicular trafficking mechanisms
rationale: Repeated the parent's scope (endosome-to-secretory pathway protein sorting); narrowing to the vesicular trafficking mechanisms distinguishes it from the parent's protein sorting focus.

name: T cell activation and effector regulation
rationale: No siblings exist and no duplicate indicated; keeping current name unchanged despite overlap with parent, since revision requires collision or sibling fit, neither applies.

name: mRNA 3'-end processing and spliceosome assembly
rationale: Sibling 'RNA polymerase transcription and co-transcriptional splicing' shares transcription termination members, so 'transcription termination' fits both; the distinguishing focus of this theme is 3'-end processing and spliceosome assembly.

name: CD4 T-helper differentiation and effector response
rationale: Both children and all members concern CD4 T cell activation, lineage commitment and subset-specific effector responses (Th1/Th2/Th17/Tfh/Treg); no direct members extend beyond this.

name: Platelet activation and adhesion signalling
rationale: Distinct from parent themes (coagulation cascade, integrin adhesion) and sibling (hemostasis); specifically about platelet activation and adhesion mechanisms.

name: BCL-2 family apoptosis regulation
rationale: Repeats parent 'Mitochondrial apoptosis and its regulation' and overlaps 'Regulation of mitochondrial membrane permeability and apoptosis'; specifying BCL-2 family control distinguishes it.

name: Amyloid-beta and tau pathology regulation
rationale: Distinct from parents (broader proteinopathy/glial fate and lipid metabolism themes) and siblings (gliogenesis, cholesterol transport); no collision.

name: Regulation of progenitor cell proliferation and commitment
rationale: All four members concern restraining or balancing the proliferation, survival, or fate commitment of progenitor/tissue cell populations (thymocytes, bone marrow cells, tissue cells generally, and fate-committing progenitors), rather than any single tissue or mechanism.

name: TAK1-dependent TLR/NF-kB and JNK activation
rationale: Four members (TLR10, TLR5, TAK1-dependent IKK/NF-kB, TAK1-mediated JNK activation) converge on MyD88-TRAF6-TAK1 signalling driving NF-kB and JNK activation downstream of innate immune receptors; the weakly included JNK cascade regulation member (0.28) overlaps this axis but is broader and largely excluded from the core theme.

name: Viral entry and protein targeting to the ER membrane
rationale: Unites virus-host interaction biology with SRP-dependent cotranslational targeting of nascent chains to the ER membrane; no broader term is needed since these are the only two biological threads present.

name: Toll and interleukin-1 driven inflammatory response
rationale: The generic phrase also fits siblings 'IL-1 family cytokine signalling and inflammatory chemotaxis' and 'Toll-like receptor and innate inflammatory signalling'; narrowing to the combined Toll/IL-1 axis distinguishes this theme's specific members (Toll signaling pathway, Interleukin-1 family/processing/IL-37) from those siblings.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint regulation
rationale: Nearly identical to siblings 'Cell cycle progression and division' and 'Cell cycle and mitotic machinery' which cover the same generic mitotic cycle terms; this theme's distinct members (G1/S checkpoint, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, Polo-like kinase) point to checkpoint regulation specifically.

name: Ion and osmotic homeostasis
rationale: Union covers ion transport homeostasis and water/osmotic balance responses, including apoptosis triggered by osmotic stress and salt/water sensing; a broader term like 'cell stress response' would be too vague, while restating either child alone would miss the other.

name: Protein phosphorylation
rationale: No sibling collision and name is more specific than parent, distinguishing itself clearly.

name: Membrane excitability and calcium signalling responses
rationale: The child covers calcium/calcineurin signalling regulation, while direct members add membrane depolarization control and stimulus responses (caffeine, organophosphorus) that act through calcium release and excitable-membrane channels; together these converge on excitability and calcium-linked signalling rather than any single receptor family.

name: Regulatory T cell differentiation and CD4 T cell activation
rationale: Overlaps sibling 'T-helper subset differentiation and response' which also covers T-helper differentiation; this theme is distinguished by its focus on activation and regulatory/Treg differentiation rather than T-helper subset commitment.

name: Eicosanoid receptor signalling and biosynthesis
rationale: Nearly repeats the parent 'Lipid mediator signalling'; members focus on prostaglandin/leukotriene GPCR pathways and eicosanoid biosynthesis, distinct from the sibling's SPM biosynthesis focus.

name: T cell receptor-driven activation
rationale: No sibling collisions and name is more specific than parent, distinguishing TCR-driven activation mechanism.

name: T cell receptor signalling and activation
rationale: All members converge on antigen-receptor-proximal signalling (LCK, ZAP70, SYK, CD45) and its costimulatory/coinhibitory tuning that drives T cell activation, proliferation and adhesive engagement; the gamma-delta T cell activation member (0.42) shares this same TCR-proximal signalling logic despite using an unconventional receptor.

name: Androgen receptor signaling regulation
rationale: All members concern regulation of androgen receptor signaling or its direct downstream transcriptional targets.

name: Cardiac conduction system development
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Heart morphogenesis and development' on the morphogenesis aspect; narrowing to conduction system development distinguishes it.

name: Notch pathway in organogenesis
rationale: Repeated the parent 'Notch signalling in organ development' without adding specificity.

name: Immune checkpoint regulation of lymphocyte activity
rationale: Distinct from parent and all listed siblings; specifically about checkpoint regulation, not overlapping with cytotoxicity, T-helper differentiation, or effector response themes.

name: HDL and triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle remodeling
rationale: The current name also fits the sibling theme, whose chylomicron assembly member is itself a triglyceride-rich lipoprotein; the revised name reflects the HDL remodeling/assembly focus unique to this theme's members.

name: Mitochondrial apoptotic signalling
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Intrinsic apoptotic signalling'; needs to indicate mechanism distinct from the sibling's regulatory focus.

name: Central carbon and lipid fuel metabolism
rationale: Name already differs from parent by excluding cofactor metabolism, and there are no siblings to conflict with.

name: Digestion and sugar absorption
rationale: Both children cover digestion/intestinal absorption and hexose/monosaccharide transport; with no distinct direct members, the parent is the union of digestive processing and sugar transport, broader than either child alone but not a generic 'metabolism' label.

name: JNK cascade activation
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and name is more specific than parent, distinguishing JNK cascade from NF-kB regulation.

name: Vitamin metabolism and transport
rationale: Covers retinoid metabolism/transport, vitamin absorption/transport, and related fat-soluble vitamin and cofactor handling (e.g. fatty acid alpha-oxidation, folate biosynthesis) without invoking a mechanism narrower than the whole set.

name: Cytokinetic ring contraction and abscission
rationale: Repeats parent 'Mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis' and overlaps siblings; narrowed to the specific contractile ring and abscission process distinguishing it from spindle checkpoint and mitotic machinery themes.

name: Photoreceptor and pigmentation biology
rationale: Union of photoreceptor structure/ciliary trafficking children with pigmentation-related direct members (eye pigmentation, pigment granule localization) and melanocyte pigmentation child; both photoreceptor and pigment-cell biology are covered without invoking a mechanism common to only one arm.

name: Cell cycle and E2F-driven proliferation
rationale: All three members describe the CDK/cyclin/RB-E2F machinery controlling replication licensing and mitotic progression.

name: Xenobiotic and small-molecule conjugation metabolism
rationale: Distinct from siblings; conjugation metabolism specifically separates it from other xenobiotic-related themes like bilirubin metabolism and xenobiotic homeostasis.

name: Bacterial ligand pattern recognition receptors
rationale: Overlapped with 'Innate pattern recognition and cytokine-driven inflammation' and 'Endosomal innate immune sensing and peptide transport'; narrowed to bacterial-specific pattern recognition receptors distinct from endosomal/viral sensing siblings.

name: Focal adhesion and cell-substrate junction regulation
rationale: Both parents already combine cell-matrix adhesion with lamellipodial themes, and the sibling also includes lamellipodium morphogenesis and actin nucleation regulation, making 'lamellipodial dynamics' equally descriptive of it; the distinguishing content of this theme is adhesion/junction regulation rather than protrusion dynamics.

With a single named child (non-canonical NF-kappaB signalling) alongside broader NF-kappaB regulation and NOD-like receptor signalling members not organised under it, there is no umbrella tighter than 'NF-kappaB and innate immune receptor signalling regulation', which is too broad and just restates the lone child plus extras.

name: Kidney and lung morphogenesis
rationale: Distinct from siblings; no other theme specifically covers kidney and lung organogenesis.

name: Renin-angiotensin system and fluid balance
rationale: Both children and all members concern the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis and its downstream control of blood pressure, blood volume, and ion/water homeostasis; no member extends beyond this hormonal fluid-pressure regulatory system.

name: PAR-mediated platelet activation and degranulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Hemostasis and coagulation', which covers hemostasis and coagulation factor defects broadly; the revised name specifies PAR/thrombin receptor signaling and degranulation, matching this theme's actual members.

name: Plasma membrane organization and lipid asymmetry
rationale: Covers the named child (membrane shaping and bilayer asymmetry) plus representative members on plasma membrane organization, phospholipid scrambling and raft-directed protein transport, all concerning the structure, lipid distribution and domain organization of the plasma membrane.

name: Receptor-mediated mitophagy
rationale: Too broad and overlapped with sibling 'Mitochondrial quality control by autophagy'; narrowed to specific receptor-mediated clearance mechanism distinguishing it from general quality control and biogenesis siblings.

Most members concern NADPH oxidase-driven superoxide production and its role in phagocyte antimicrobial killing, but the tissue-macrophage identity programme and the M. tuberculosis metabolic manipulation pathway share only a loose connection to macrophages/phagocytes, not the oxidative killing biology itself.

name: Phagocyte NADPH oxidase respiratory burst
rationale: Core members (btm macrophage identity, respiratory burst, neutrophil killing, superoxide regulation, RHO-GTPase oxidase activation, PMN phagocytolytic peroxidase chemistry) all concern NADPH oxidase-driven superoxide generation and its use in microbial killing by phagocytes. The weakly included 'Manipulation of host energy metabolism' (0.49) is excluded as it concerns pathogen rewiring of host glycolysis rather than oxidative killing.

name: DNA damage response checkpoints
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Mitotic chromosome segregation fidelity' and sibling 'Cell division and genome integrity' as a generic genome-stability label; renamed to specify DNA damage checkpoint mechanisms distinguishing it from segregation fidelity and division-integrity themes.

name: Cornified envelope formation and keratinization
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; focuses specifically on cornified envelope assembly and keratinization rather than collagen matrix or general appendage differentiation.

name: Growth factor and insulin receptor signalling to metabolism
rationale: Distinct from all sibling themes; no parent to collide with.

name: Meiotic recombination and nuclear division
rationale: Nearly duplicates parent 'Meiosis and gametogenesis' and overlaps siblings 'Reproductive development and gametogenesis' and 'Sex-specific gametogenic regulation'; the distinguishing content here is meiotic chromosome mechanics (recombination, telomere attachment, nuclear division regulation) rather than gametogenesis broadly.

name: Actin-driven membrane ruffling and macropinocytosis
rationale: Distinct from parents and sibling; specifically names membrane ruffling and macropinocytosis rather than general Rho GTPase signalling or pathogen entry.

name: Selective clearance of misfolded proteins by autophagy
rationale: Core members (aggrephagy, regulation of aggrephagy, chaperone-mediated autophagy in both GO and Reactome) all describe selective autophagic or lysosomal disposal of misfolded/aggregated proteins via chaperone recognition. Stress granule disassembly (0.58) shares the chaperone/VCP-mediated clearance machinery; response to heat (0.36) is weakly included and only partly fits, involving broader thermal stress responses beyond selective proteostasis.

name: Mitochondrial maintenance and quality control
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings, covering broader quality control processes not overlapping with protein import/cristae architecture or general autophagic clearance.

name: Regulation of phosphatase-mediated dephosphorylation
rationale: Overlaps parent 'Protein phosphorylation' and sibling 'Regulation of kinase-mediated phosphorylation'; narrowed to dephosphorylation/phosphatase regulation to distinguish from kinase-focused sibling.

name: T-helper 1/2 differentiation and response
rationale: Union covers commitment/activation of helper T cells generally plus specific Th1 and Th2 regulation, but not Th17/Treg/Tfh specifics beyond lineage commitment already named in the child.

name: Proteolytic maturation of secreted proteins
rationale: Core members (protein processing, insulin processing, regulation of proteolysis, peptide biosynthetic process) all describe proteolytic cleavage that converts precursor proteins/hormones into active mature forms. The thyroid hormone response members are included partly because they involve cathepsin proteolysis and glutathione peptide synthesis, so they partially overlap; the herbicide response member (0.29) is excluded as it concerns xenobiotic oxidative stress rather than proteolytic maturation.

name: Glycosaminoglycan degradation and related disorders
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis, degradation and related disorders' and sibling 'Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis and related disorders'; this theme's members are dominated by degradation pathways (HS-GAG, CS/DS degradation, MPS II/VII), distinguishing it from the biosynthesis-focused sibling.

name: Integrin-mediated cell adhesion
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically about integrin-mediated adhesion mechanisms, unlike endothelial-leukocyte or platelet-mediated adhesion siblings.

name: Somitogenesis and axial segmentation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Gastrulation movements and axis formation'; renaming to focus on somite formation and segmentation distinguishes it from parents and siblings focused on cardiac/mesoderm fate and neuroectoderm patterning.

name: SUMOylation and telomere-linked chromatin maintenance
rationale: The original name overlapped with sibling 'Chromatin organization and sister chromatid cohesion', which also deals with chromatin-associated genome stability via cohesion; this theme's distinguishing members involve SUMO conjugation and telomere maintenance via recombination, which the sibling lacks.

name: Retinoid metabolism and transport
rationale: All members concern vitamin A/retinoid (diterpenoid) synthesis, storage, catabolism, or transport, including the STRA6-mediated retinol uptake defect.

name: Neural tube and craniofacial morphogenesis
