rationale: Covers the child's neural patterning/fate specification plus the direct members on neural tube closure and neurocranium formation, without repeating the child's name.

name: Amino sugar catabolism
rationale: All members concern breakdown or phosphorylation of amino sugars (sialic acid, glucosamine, GlcNAc) and related carbohydrates feeding into central metabolism.

name: Chemical stress response and p53 signalling
rationale: The generic name also fit both siblings' stress-response members; members here specifically include chemical stress response and the p53 pathway, distinguishing it from the starvation/nutrient-sensing and UPR/misfolded-protein siblings.

name: Transcription termination and mRNA processing/decay
rationale: Both children concern coupling of transcription termination to 3' end formation and subsequent mRNA turnover; no direct members extend beyond this union.

name: HDL particle assembly and clearance
rationale: Repeats parent's scope broadly; sibling 'Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein assembly and transport' covers remodeling of lipoprotein particles which overlapped with the broad transport wording, so narrowing to HDL assembly/clearance/localization distinguishes it.

name: General chemotaxis and cell migration
rationale: Highly overlaps with siblings 'Leukocyte chemotaxis and recruitment' and 'Leukocyte migration and adhesion' which both describe leukocyte chemotaxis/migration; this theme's inclusion of generic cell chemotaxis and positive chemotaxis distinguishes it as broader, non-leukocyte-specific motility.

name: Type I interferon induction and signaling
rationale: Members include RIG-I pathway activation, not just TLR-driven; broader name avoids overlap with sibling 'Endosomal TLR-driven IRF3/IRF7 activation' which is specific to endosomal TLR receptors.

name: Photoreceptor differentiation and light perception
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent 'Photoreceptor development and maintenance' and sibling 'Photoreceptor ciliary trafficking and development', which shares three of the same members; the revised name emphasizes rod/cone differentiation and sensory perception, which distinguishes it.

name: Bile acid, alcohol and fat-soluble vitamin metabolism
rationale: No siblings and name is more specific than the parent, covering bile acids, alcohol, and fat-soluble vitamins distinctly.

name: Sex hormone-driven pubertal changes
rationale: Overlapped conceptually with parent 'Hormone-driven puberty and sexual maturation' and was too generic relative to siblings like 'Mammary gland development and hormone signalling'; narrowed to specify pubertal sex hormone effects.

name: Th17 lineage commitment and differentiation
rationale: Four of five members directly concern Th17 cell fate specification, differentiation and its regulation via IL-23/IL-6-JAK-STAT3 and RORC/BATF/IRF4; T-helper lineage commitment (1.00) generalises the same decision process across helper subsets. Th1 immune response (0.26) is excluded as a weakly included, off-topic member.

name: Cardiac septation and valve morphogenesis
rationale: Distinct from parent 'Heart morphogenesis' and sibling 'Cardiac morphogenesis' by specifying septation and valve development.

name: Cholinergic receptor signalling
rationale: Core members (inclusion 1.00) all concern acetylcholine receptor signalling, muscarinic G protein-coupled or nicotinic calcium-permeable, and cholinergic synaptic transmission; response to nicotine and opioid signalling (0.42, 0.32) are excluded as they extend beyond cholinergic receptor biology into broader nicotine/opioid effects.

name: Lymphocyte and monocyte/dendritic immune cell identity
rationale: Name distinctly covers lymphocyte and monocyte/dendritic identity/differentiation, not overlapping with other siblings which cover specific signaling pathways, effector functions, or distinct lineages like myeloid/megakaryocyte or osteoclast differentiation.

name: Interferon and JAK-STAT receptor signalling
rationale: Overlapped with several cytokine/innate inflammatory signalling siblings (e.g., Innate inflammatory cytokine signalling, Cytokine-driven innate inflammatory response); narrowed to the interferon/JAK-STAT receptor mechanism to distinguish it.

name: Epidermal and hair follicle development
rationale: No collision with any listed name, no siblings to conflate with, and it does not repeat either parent's name.

name: Extrinsic apoptotic signalling
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Apoptosis signalling' which covers intrinsic/BCL-2 pathway; own members (TRAIL, CASP8, extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway) are specifically extrinsic/death-receptor mediated.

name: Inflammasome and cytokine-driven innate inflammation
rationale: Covers IL-1 driven inflammatory response and cytosolic pattern recognition/inflammasome signalling, both converging on inflammasome activation and inflammatory cytokine release; broader than either child alone but excludes adaptive immunity and non-inflammatory pattern recognition outcomes.

name: mRNA transcription and splicing coupling
rationale: Both children cover transcription elongation/termination coupled with splicing/RNA processing machinery; the direct member RNA decapping extends this to mRNA processing/turnover, so the umbrella covers RNA polymerase transcription steps together with co- and post-transcriptional RNA processing, without repeating either child's name.

name: RTK signalling via PI3K/AKT axis
rationale: Collides closely with sibling 'Receptor tyrosine kinase signalling'; renamed to clarify the specific downstream axis, distinguishing it from both the generic sibling and the oncogenic-focused sibling.

name: Protein glycosylation and proteoglycan biosynthesis
rationale: Overlapped with parent's 'Glycan metabolism' and sibling's nucleotide-sugar metabolism theme; members are specifically about protein/lipid glycosylation and GAG/proteoglycan synthesis, which distinguishes it.

name: Kinetochore-spindle attachment and chromosome separation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinesis', which also covers cytokinesis and chromosome segregation; renamed to emphasize the kinetochore-microtubule attachment focus unique to this theme's members.

name: Base excision repair and oxidative DNA damage response
rationale: Distinct from parent (DNA damage repair) by specifying base excision repair/oxidative pathway, and distinct from sibling which focuses on UV response.

name: Intestinal and pancreatic epithelial differentiation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Endoderm-derived epithelial identity and organ differentiation' which shares the same HNF/epithelial maturation members; the distinguishing content here is intestinal stem cell/epithelial differentiation and exocrine pancreas development rather than general endoderm epithelial identity.

name: Coagulation cascade initiation and propagation
rationale: Members are entirely about coagulation cascade defects/regulation and VWF cleavage, not platelet function; 'Platelet function and hemostasis' also fits the sibling's members (which include F8 defects and HALLMARK_COAGULATION), so a more specific name distinguishing cascade dynamics is needed.

name: Ribosome biogenesis and nuclear RNA metabolism
rationale: Covers both children: rRNA processing/ribosome export and MYC-driven growth on one side, mRNA export and surveillance (e.g. NMD) on the other; both concern nuclear processing and export of RNA species destined for translation, with no direct members to broaden further.

name: Regulation of MAPK cascade signalling
rationale: Would also describe sibling 'Kinase-mediated phosphorylation signalling', whose members are nearly identical regulatory kinase terms; this theme's distinct focus is MAPK/JNK cascade regulation.

name: Cardiac action potential membrane potential regulation
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than parent 'Cardiac conduction system excitability', focusing on membrane potential regulation specifically.

name: Insulin-independent regulation of carbohydrate and lipid fuel switching
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Hormonal regulation of energy substrate metabolism' and parent's hormonal focus; narrowed to non-hormonal/metabolic fuel-switching mechanisms distinct from hormone-driven regulation.

name: Immune checkpoint restraint of T cell activity
rationale: All members concern inhibitory receptors, suppressive cytokines and other checkpoint mechanisms that dampen T cell activation, proliferation, adhesion and cytokine output, exploited by tumours for immune escape.

name: Intrinsic apoptotic signalling
rationale: Members focus on the intrinsic/mitochondrial pathway (BAX, BCL-2, ER stress-induced intrinsic pathway); the current name would also describe the sibling 'Extrinsic apoptotic signalling'.

name: Sinoatrial node development and cardiac conduction
rationale: No siblings present, and the name is already more specific than its parent, distinguishing itself by focusing on sinoatrial node development and cardiac conduction rather than general electrical excitability.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase signal transduction and attenuation
rationale: Covers the child's RTK/PI3K-AKT signalling plus IRS activation and signal attenuation, both steps in receptor tyrosine kinase signalling; broad phosphorylation (0.32) is below threshold and excluded.

name: Cardiac action potential dynamics
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Cardiac ion channel regulation' since both cover cardiac ion channel topics; narrowing to action potential dynamics distinguishes it from channel regulation focus.

name: Vesicle transport to organelles and the vacuole/lysosome
rationale: Both children concern vesicle-mediated transport, one general and one specifically targeting the vacuole/lysosome; representative direct-member pathways (post-Golgi transport, Golgi-to-vacuole transport, vesicle targeting) fall within this same union, so the umbrella covers vesicle-mediated intracellular transport broadly while including the vacuolar/lysosomal destination emphasised by several members.

name: TAP-mediated peptide loading for MHC-I
rationale: Overlapped with 'Endosomal innate immune sensing and peptide transport' and 'MHC-restricted antigen presentation and viral immune evasion'; narrowed to the specific TAP/peptide-loading mechanism distinguishing it from both.

name: Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing and antiviral interferon signalling
rationale: No siblings and name is distinct from parent, adding specific mechanism and downstream signaling.

name: Complement and antimicrobial peptide effectors
rationale: Too similar to 'Phagocyte antimicrobial effector mechanisms' and 'Antiviral innate immune response'; narrowed to specify complement/antimicrobial peptide effector molecules rather than broad innate effector responses.

name: Telomere maintenance
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Genome maintenance and chromosome dynamics'; narrowing to telomere-specific mechanisms distinguishes it.

name: Matrix vesicle-mediated hydroxyapatite deposition
rationale: Nearly duplicated sibling 'Skeletal and dental mineralized tissue development' and parent 'Skeletal tissue mineralization and development'; narrowed to the specific molecular mineral-deposition mechanism in bone and tooth matrix.

name: Regulation of translational activity
rationale: Repeated scope of parent 'Cytoplasmic translation initiation and ribosome assembly'; renamed to distinguish regulatory control aspect from initiation/assembly focus.

name: Cytoplasmic translation and its regulation
rationale: Core members cover translation, translational elongation, and positive/negative regulation of cytoplasmic translation, all centered on ribosome-based protein synthesis; the weaker members (stalled ribosome rescue, tRNA metabolism regulation) also bear on translational quality control and capacity.

name: Hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Hematopoietic and leukocyte differentiation' which covers differentiation; this theme is distinguished by focusing on stem cell maintenance and homeostatic regulation rather than lineage differentiation.

name: CD4 T cell activation and proliferation
rationale: Covers the child (helper subset differentiation) plus direct members on CD4 T cell activation and T cell proliferation; the weakly included 'positive regulation of cell activation' (0.37) is broader and not the basis for the name.

name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium cycling in muscle contraction
rationale: Nearly duplicates parent 'Muscle contraction and calcium regulation' and overlaps sibling 'Muscle contraction regulation' which shares the same muscle contraction members; the distinguishing feature here is sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium transport.

name: Ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling, specifying the ubiquitin-proteasome mechanism specifically rather than general protein quality control.
n/ a

name: Chromatin structure and repair
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Telomere and chromosome maintenance' and was too broad relative to parent's checkpoint focus; narrowed to chromatin-level repair and organization.

name: T-helper cell subset differentiation
rationale: The current name duplicates the parent's broad scope and could describe myeloid/lymphocyte siblings; members are specifically about T-helper lineage commitment and Th1/Th2/Treg differentiation, distinguishing it from 'T cell receptor signalling and differentiation' and 'Myeloid and megakaryocyte differentiation'.

name: Regulation of protein trafficking to the plasma membrane
rationale: All members concern secretory and vesicular trafficking pathways that control delivery, localization or polarized targeting of proteins to the plasma membrane.

name: MHC-restricted antigen presentation and viral immune evasion
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; no overlapping theme covers MHC-restricted presentation combined with viral immune evasion specifically.

name: Voltage-gated ion channel function
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Gap junction and electrical coupling' by repeating 'electrical coupling'; narrowed to ion channel gating function distinct from junctional coupling and from sibling calcium/muscle themes.

name: Nuclear and mitochondrial DNA repair
rationale: No collision with parent or siblings; name is already distinct.

name: Translesion DNA synthesis
rationale: No siblings and name is distinct from both parent themes, which refer to broader coordinated repair or gap-filling synthesis processes.

name: Translesion DNA synthesis and its termination
rationale: All three concern bypass of replication-blocking lesions by specialized polymerases and the mechanisms that end this error-prone synthesis and restore accurate replication.

name: Coagulation cascade regulation
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Platelet function and hemostasis' which shares the word hemostasis and even some members; renaming to focus on coagulation cascade activity distinguishes it.

name: Mitotic spindle checkpoint control
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to focus on checkpoint signaling and spindle attachment regulation, distinguishing it from the sibling's broader chromosome separation and cytokinesis focus.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint control
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Mitotic cell cycle and organelle partitioning'; overlaps generic cell cycle scope, needs distinction from sibling 'APC/C-mediated mitotic exit' by focusing on checkpoint regulation aspect.

name: Neurotransmitter reuptake and recycling
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Presynaptic neurotransmitter release and transport'; narrowed to focus on reuptake/recycling machinery distinct from release/transport.

name: Cross-bridge cycling regulation
rationale: Too broad relative to parent 'Calcium sensitivity of contractile filaments' and overlapped with sibling 'Calcium signaling regulation'; narrowed to the thin/thick filament regulatory mechanism distinct from calcium signaling itself.

name: MPTP-mediated calcium efflux in apoptosis
rationale: Overlapped substantially with parent 'Mitochondrial calcium and apoptosis regulation'; narrowed to focus specifically on the mitochondrial permeability transition pore mechanism, distinguishing it from sibling 'Mitochondrial apoptosis regulation' which covers broader regulatory aspects.

name: Mitochondrial membrane permeability and calcium transport
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Mitochondrial apoptosis and its calcium/redox regulation', which shares the hypoxia and calcium members; removing 'apoptosis' and 'redox' language and emphasizing membrane transport/permeability distinguishes it from that sibling.

name: Nuclear and mitochondrial RNA polymerase transcription
rationale: Core members cover elongation and termination by RNA polymerases I, II and III and by the mitochondrial transcription machinery (POLRMT/TFAM/MTERF1), all concerning production of rRNA, mRNA or mitochondrial transcripts by dedicated RNA polymerases. Weakly included members (mitochondrial RNA catabolism, Pol III abortive initiation, Pol III termination) touch related turnover/termination steps but are below the 0.5 threshold and excluded from the core claim.

name: Phosphatase regulation and inositol phosphate metabolism
rationale: Core members (regulation of phosphatase activity, dephosphorylation, positive regulation of dephosphorylation, phosphatidylinositol dephosphorylation) concern phosphatase enzymes and their control, while the weaker members (inositol phosphate metabolism, cytosolic and nuclear pyrophosphate synthesis, 0.70/0.56/0.53) extend into the soluble inositol phosphate/pyrophosphate network that interconverts with phosphoinositide turnover; both groups converge on phosphate addition/removal from inositol-containing molecules.

name: Viral replication, assembly and egress
rationale: Covers the child (viral hijacking of host translation) plus the direct members: genome replication/transcription/translation, nuclear export of viral ribonucleoproteins, and virion assembly and release, all centered on late-stage viral life-cycle steps that co-opt host machinery.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression and genome maintenance
rationale: Covers both children (tRNA aminoacylation and mitochondrial gene expression) plus the direct members concerning mitochondrial RNA turnover and DNA repair/metabolism, all centered on maintenance and expression of the mitochondrial genome.

name: Angiogenesis in wound healing
rationale: Repeated 'vascular remodelling' from both parent themes; angiogenesis specifically distinguishes wound-healing neovascularization from ECM- and hypoxia-driven remodelling processes.

name: Muscle adaptation to exercise stress
rationale: Overlaps parent 'Muscle growth and differentiation regulation' and siblings covering development/regeneration and growth; narrowing to adaptation/exercise response distinguishes it.

name: UPR signal attenuation mechanisms
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'ER stress and unfolded protein response'; narrowed to regulatory attenuation aspect distinct from the core ER stress/UPR pathway sibling.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression
rationale: All members concern transcription, RNA processing/turnover, or translation of the mitochondrial genome, including the broader cytosolic translation pathway that explicitly incorporates the mitochondrial system.

name: PI3K-AKT downstream signalling from RTKs
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Receptor tyrosine kinase signaling in growth factor pathways' which also covers FGFR ligand binding; this theme's members emphasize PI3K/AKT and IRS downstream signaling, which better distinguishes it and avoids repeating the parent's RTK framing.

name: Long-chain fatty acid and ether lipid metabolism
rationale: Adds ether lipid/wax biosynthesis and general fatty acid derivative metabolism to the child's long-chain/very-long-chain fatty acid metabolism, broadening it to cover related lipid derivatives without invoking unrelated lipid classes.

name: IL-1 family cytokine signalling and inflammatory chemotaxis
rationale: Covers IL-1 driven inflammatory response plus IL-33 signalling (a member of the IL-1 family) and granulocyte chemotaxis regulation triggered by such cytokines; narrower than general inflammation since all members centre on IL-1 family cytokines and their downstream leukocyte recruitment.

name: Beta cell ion channel signaling
rationale: Repeated broader scope of parent 'Beta cell glucose sensing and insulin release' rather than narrowing it; needs specificity distinguishing it from sibling 'Beta-cell insulin secretion and glucose homeostasis', e.g. focusing on channel-level mechanisms if that describes the members.

name: Chemokine-directed leukocyte migration
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Leukocyte trafficking to inflamed tissue' which covers similar movement processes; specifying the chemokine-driven mechanism distinguishes this theme.

name: eIF2α kinase signalling
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Integrated stress response and translational control'; narrowing to the eIF2α kinase arm distinguishes it while remaining true to members.

name: Deoxyribonucleotide pool synthesis
rationale: Nearly repeats parent and overlaps conceptually with sibling's catabolism scope; renamed to specify synthesis/biosynthesis of dNTP pools, distinguishing from sanitation and catabolism sibling.

name: Deoxyribonucleotide pool metabolism
rationale: All members concern synthesis, interconversion, and catabolism of deoxyribonucleoside mono/triphosphates that maintain balanced dNTP pools for DNA replication and repair, spanning both purine and pyrimidine precursors.

name: Mitochondrial protein import and organization
rationale: Covers the cristae/inner membrane child plus direct members on protein targeting, processing, import, fusion regulation and overall organization, all centered on building and maintaining mitochondrial structure and protein content.

name: Hypoxia and glycolytic metabolism
rationale: Child covers HIF/hypoxia signalling; direct members add glycolysis, pyruvate handling and nucleoside diphosphate turnover tied to glycolytic flux, plus oxygen transport/sensing that feeds hypoxia response, so the union spans oxygen-linked glycolytic metabolism rather than glycolysis or hypoxia alone.

name: Sensory perception of light and sound
rationale: Repeats the parent 'Sensory perception' exactly; narrowing to specific modalities distinguishes it from sibling 'Sensory perception of taste and mechanical stimuli'.

name: Receptor endocytic trafficking and signal regulation
rationale: Both children and their members concern the internalisation, sorting, recycling or degradation of cell-surface receptors and how this shapes downstream signalling duration; broader than either child alone but not extending to unrelated trafficking or signalling biology.

name: Germ layer specification and early lineage commitment
rationale: The child covers mesoderm patterning/fate, while direct members add endoderm development/differentiation and EMT plus CDH11 transcription tied to mesenchymal transition—together spanning early germ-layer (mesoderm/endoderm) specification and the fate-commitment/transition events that establish these lineages.

name: Sex-specific gametogenic regulation
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere; also overlapped with sibling 'Gametogenesis and meiotic division'. Members include oocyte differentiation, spermatogenesis, and regulation of reproductive process, distinguishing this as sex-specific regulatory aspects rather than the core meiotic division process.

name: Intestinal lipid and cholesterol absorption
rationale: The current name asserts chylomicron formation, which the members do not directly describe; renamed to reflect the actual digestion/absorption focus, distinct from the sibling's lipoprotein particle remodeling and transport theme.

name: Amino acid and bile acid membrane transport
rationale: Union covers L-amino acid (and GABA) transmembrane transport plus one bile acid transporter, so the smallest umbrella spanning both is transport of amino acids and bile acids across membranes.

name: Digestion and intestinal nutrient absorption
rationale: All members cover luminal digestion of dietary macronutrients and/or their transport across the intestinal epithelium (sugars, lipids, sterols).

name: Excitatory synapse structure and plasticity
rationale: Union covers glutamatergic synapse organization/signaling and structural/synaptic plasticity, with no direct members adding new scope beyond these two children.

name: Small GTPase signalling
rationale: All three children cover activation, effector signalling and regulation of small GTPases across the Ras/Rho/Rab/Arf families, with no direct members adding further scope; the umbrella is the signalling system itself without restating any child's specific focus.

name: Nucleolar RNA processing and ribosome biogenesis factors
rationale: Both children concern nucleolar/snoRNP-mediated rRNA and snRNA processing; mitochondrial ribosome assembly extends this to ribosome biogenesis broadly, and protein methylation (weakly included, 0.25) overlaps via methyltransferases acting on rRNA-processing and ribosomal components, so a ribosome-biogenesis-centered umbrella covers all with minimal broadening.

name: Fat-soluble vitamin transport and metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent (fat-soluble vitamins vs trace minerals) and there are no siblings to collide with.

name: Mitotic cell cycle and DNA replication initiation
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere; also two siblings ('Cell cycle progression and division machinery', 'Cell cycle and mitotic machinery') share near-identical wording. This theme's members emphasize DNA replication initiation and G1/S checkpoint signaling, which distinguishes it.

name: Hexose and monosaccharide transmembrane transport
rationale: The sibling 'Digestion and intestinal nutrient absorption' shares intestinal absorption/hexose absorption members, so the original name also described it; renaming to emphasize the transmembrane transport mechanism distinguishes this theme.

name: Histone deposition and nucleosome assembly
rationale: Repeated parent's 'genome maintenance' phrase; narrowing to nucleosome assembly/histone deposition distinguishes it from parent's broader mitotic genome maintenance scope and sibling's nuclear envelope focus.

name: Inhibitory regulation of NK and T cell cytotoxicity
rationale: Union covers checkpoint restraint of T cells plus NK receptor-based inhibitory control (negative regulation of NK activation, NK receptor repertoire) and PD-L1 trafficking that modulates this inhibition; broader than the single child but scoped to lymphocyte cytotoxic restraint rather than immunity generally.

name: Myofibril assembly and maturation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Sarcomere structure and contractile mechanics' and sibling 'Muscle contraction regulation'; narrowed to the assembly/maturation process distinct from contraction regulation.

name: Sarcomere assembly and contraction
rationale: All members concern building sarcomeric thin/thick filaments to defined length and geometry (myofibril assembly, thin filament assembly, myosin filament organization, pointed-end capping) and the force-generating actin-myosin sliding they enable (Striated Muscle Contraction).

name: Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis and disorders
rationale: Repeats parent's language and overlaps sibling 'Protein glycosylation and its disorders' which also covers glycosylation disorders; narrowing to glycosaminoglycan/proteoglycan metabolism distinguishes it, matching this theme's members like GAG biosynthesis, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan metabolism, and CHSY1.

name: Serine/threonine kinase signalling regulation
rationale: No siblings, and the name does not repeat either parent (which focus on dephosphorylation/phosphatase regulation and kinase feedback control), so it remains distinct.

name: Mitochondrial amino acid metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with parent's 'cofactor metabolism' scope; narrowed to the amino acid-specific component to avoid redundancy with parent name.

name: RNA polymerase transcription, splicing and termination
rationale: Both children cover polymerase transcription coupled to splicing and to termination/spliceosome assembly, and the single direct member, RNA polymerase I elongation, is itself transcription by a polymerase; the umbrella spans transcription elongation, splicing and termination without extending to unrelated RNA processes.

name: FGFR ligand binding and phospholipase/PI3K cascades
rationale: Repeated parent's 'FGFR and EGFR ligand-activated signaling cascades' too closely; also broad enough to overlap with RTK signal transduction sibling. Narrowed to reflect the specific FGFR-driven phospholipase C and phosphatidylinositol signaling members.

name: Interferon-mediated antiviral response
rationale: Overlaps with 'Interferon and cytokine receptor signalling' and 'Innate immune effector responses'; specifying interferon-mediated mechanism distinguishes it from general innate sensing and cytokine signalling siblings.

name: Cell-cell adhesion junctions
rationale: Both children (general cell-cell adhesion and cadherin-based adhesion) and representative members describe adherens, tight and desmosomal junction machinery holding cells together; there are no direct members adding further scope.

name: Mechanosensory and chemosensory transduction
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Sensory signal transduction' and sibling 'Sensory perception'; renamed to specify the mechanosensory/chemosensory receptor pathways distinct from phototransduction siblings.

name: Base excision repair and single-strand break repair
rationale: All members concern removal of damaged bases via AP-site intermediates or repair of the resulting single-strand nicks; the direct members add MUTYH/NEIL3/NTHL1 defect pathways and AP-site resolution routes plus general single-strand break repair, broadening beyond the child 'Base excision repair' to include strand-break repair specifically, without expanding to all DNA repair.

name: Hepatic lipoprotein processing
rationale: Overlapped with parent name 'lipoprotein metabolism'; narrowed to distinguish from sibling 'Intestinal digestion and absorption' by focusing on post-absorption hepatic/plasma processing.

name: Synaptic neurotransmitter release and uptake
rationale: All members concern presynaptic vesicular loading, calcium-triggered release, and transporter-mediated reuptake/clearance of neurotransmitters, including their positive and presynaptic regulation; the weakly included glutamate secretion member (0.26) fits this same release-regulation theme but was largely excluded from core weighting.

name: TNF/NF-kappaB signalling
rationale: Distinct from sibling 'Non-canonical NF-kB signaling' and not a repeat of the parent, which also includes NOD-like receptor signalling.

name: Non-canonical NF-kB and TNF signalling
rationale: Both children concern the non-canonical NF-kB branch (NIK-driven and TNF-linked), and direct members like TNF signalling and its negative regulation extend to the broader receptor-proximal control of this pathway; no direct members introduce unrelated biology.

name: Gastrulation and body axis formation
rationale: No sibling collisions and name is distinct from both parent themes, which focus on neuroectoderm patterning and axial segmentation respectively.

name: Gastrulation and body axis specification
rationale: All members concern early embryonic germ-layer formation, primitive streak EMT, and anterior-posterior/paraxial axis patterning, including the weaker axis elongation member (0.62), which shares the same posterior WNT-driven segmentation logic.

name: Proteoglycan turnover and remodeling
rationale: Overlapped both parent (ECM glycosaminoglycan metabolism) and sibling 'Glycoconjugate biosynthesis and extracellular matrix formation'; narrowed to proteoglycan turnover/remodeling specifically.

name: Adrenergic and serotonergic adenylate cyclase activation
rationale: The current name would also fit both siblings, which involve GPCR-cAMP pathways; the members here are specifically about adrenergic/serotonergic receptor-driven adenylate cyclase activation and cAMP production, distinguishing it from cholinergic/aminergic pathways and cAMP catabolism/dynamics.

name: Thrombin-mediated platelet activation signalling
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Cell adhesion and hemostasis' which also covers hemostasis broadly; this theme is specifically about thrombin/PAR/Rap1 signalling driving platelet activation and degranulation, which better distinguishes it.

name: Phototransduction cascade
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers broader phototransduction biology) and siblings (development, structural biogenesis, other sensory transduction); no collision.

name: Phototransduction and its regulation
rationale: All members concern the light-activated signaling cascade in photoreceptors, its recovery/inactivation machinery, or disease-causing defects in specific components of this cascade (calcium exchange, opsin function).

name: Genetic regulation of skeletal and dental development
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Skeletal tissue mineralization and development' and sibling 'Biomineralization of bone and tooth tissues'; narrowed to the regulatory/genetic aspect of development rather than the mineralization process itself.

name: ERBB2 amplification signalling
rationale: Repeats parent 'ERBB2 and RTK-driven oncogenic signalling'; narrowing to ERBB2 amplification-driven signalling distinguishes it from sibling themes about mutant/fusion kinases and FGFR signalling.

name: B cell identity and receptor signalling markers
rationale: All members are transcriptional/surface marker signatures defining B lymphocyte lineage identity, antigen receptor components, and their regulatory modulators used to identify B cells in expression data.

name: TNF signalling and death receptor apoptosis
rationale: Covers the child (caspase-8 activation downstream of death receptors) plus direct members on TNF-mediated signalling and its NF-kappaB regulation, unifying receptor-triggered inflammatory and apoptotic outputs without invoking mitochondrial apoptosis, which is not represented.

name: Phosphatase regulation and cellular signalling attenuation
rationale: Sibling 'Phosphate group metabolism in lipids and signalling' shares identical core members (regulation of phosphatase activity, dephosphorylation, phosphatidylinositol dephosphorylation), making the two indistinguishable; renamed to emphasize the regulatory/negative-feedback aspect (negative regulation of cell size, IGF receptor signaling, caveolin-mediated endocytosis) that separates this theme.

name: Osmotic and salt stress adaptation
rationale: Both children and all members concern cellular responses to tonicity and salt/water imbalance, spanning stress response, water homeostasis, and apoptosis triggered by osmotic failure; no direct members extend beyond this scope.

name: Drug-resistant kinase mutants
rationale: Members are specifically about drug-resistant RTK mutants (sunitinib/sorafenib/gilteritinib-resistant KIT, PDGFR, FLT3, ALK), not general constitutive activation; sibling covers downstream PI3K/FGFR signalling, distinct theme.

name: Calcium/cAMP-CREB signalling
rationale: All core members (inclusion ≥0.6) converge on calcium- and cAMP-driven activation of PKA/CaMK cascades leading to CREB phosphorylation and transcription; NGF-stimulated transcription shares the CREB-driven immediate-early gene output. Weakly included members (cAMP/PKA signal transduction 0.26, response to organophosphorus 0.48) fit the same axis but are excluded from strict coverage.

name: Cardiac and skeletal muscle growth regulation
rationale: The child covers developmental formation of cardiac/skeletal muscle, while the direct members add regulation of hypertrophy, adaptation, differentiation and contraction/growth of these same muscle types, so the parent spans development plus its regulatory adaptation without invoking unrelated tissue processes.

name: Axial body plan and organ primordium formation
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Embryonic tissue and organ patterning'; narrowed to axial body plan establishment and organ primordium formation to distinguish it.

name: Endosomal innate immune sensing and peptide transport
rationale: Distinct from the similar sibling 'Innate sensing and antigen presentation via peptide transport' due to specific endosomal localization, and distinct from other siblings covering different immune mechanisms.

name: Cardiac valve and chamber morphogenesis
rationale: The members contain no endothelial differentiation processes, and the sibling shares the same top exemplars, so a more specific name reflecting valve/chamber/septum morphogenesis is needed to distinguish it.

name: HIV and SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle
rationale: Original name duplicated the parent's theme and was broad enough to also describe both siblings ('Viral entry and coronavirus host interactions' and 'Viral entry, replication and host infection'); the actual members focus on HIV reverse transcription/assembly and SARS-CoV-2 infection/therapeutics, which is more specific and distinct.

name: Osteoclast differentiation and bone remodeling regulation
rationale: Distinct from all siblings, which cover other immune/differentiation or bone processes; not repeating either parent.

name: Negative regulation of osteoclast-mediated bone remodeling
rationale: All members at 0.5+ concern restraint or control of osteoclast differentiation, fusion, proliferation or downstream bone/tissue remodeling; the weakly included macrophage fusion member (0.28) is excluded.

name: Craniofacial and ocular organogenesis
rationale: Core members (extraocular muscle, optic nerve, embryonic eye morphogenesis, eyelid development, diaphragm development) all describe cranial/craniofacial and ocular structure formation; weaker members (response to gravity, post-embryonic morphogenesis, anatomical structure maturation, inclusion <0.5) are broader developmental-physiology themes not specific to this axis and are excluded from the name.

name: Mitophagy
rationale: All members describe selective autophagic clearance of mitochondria (mitophagy) and its regulation, including PINK1/parkin and receptor-mediated routes.

name: Regulation of muscle cell proliferation and differentiation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Skeletal muscle development and regeneration' which also covers muscle development/regeneration broadly; this theme's members specifically concern proliferation and differentiation regulation, distinguishing it from the structural/regenerative siblings.

name: Reproductive hormone signalling and gonadal development
rationale: Covers both children (gonadotropin/ovarian signalling and sex hormone/reproductive development) plus direct members on structural maturation and RUNX2, which relate to developmental maturation processes tied to hormonal/reproductive axes; broader than either child but tied to reproductive-developmental biology rather than generic development.

name: Spindle organization and localization
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinesis' which also involves chromosome segregation; own members lack organelle inheritance content, so narrow to spindle organization/localization themes distinct from cytokinesis focus.

name: Pancreatic and hepatic epithelial organogenesis
rationale: Nearly indistinguishable from siblings 'Endoderm organ development and epithelial specification' and 'Endoderm-derived organ morphogenesis and differentiation'; narrowing to the specific endoderm-derived epithelial organs (e.g., liver, pancreas) distinguishes it.

name: Muscle structure, contraction and excitability
rationale: Both children concern sarcomere assembly/contraction and contractile excitability, and the direct members (muscle cell homeostasis, caveolin-mediated endocytosis, negative regulation of cell size) extend this to muscle cell size/homeostatic regulation and membrane trafficking within muscle cells, so the umbrella covers muscle structural, contractile and homeostatic processes without broadening to unrelated cell biology.

name: Nuclear gene expression and protein biogenesis machinery
rationale: Union spans nuclear genome maintenance/transcription, RNA and protein nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, plus direct members on cotranslational membrane targeting and protein modification, all core cellular machinery for producing and localising gene products.

name: Pattern recognition receptor-triggered cytokine response
rationale: Too similar to siblings 'Cytokine-driven innate inflammatory response' and 'Innate inflammatory cytokine signalling'; narrowing to receptor-triggered cytokine output distinguishes it from generic innate inflammatory cytokine themes.

name: rRNA synthesis and modification
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Ribosomal RNA transcription and ribosome assembly' and sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis'; renamed to emphasize transcription and processing of rRNA distinct from ribosome assembly steps.

name: Interferon-stimulated antiviral effector genes
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Antiviral innate immune response' and near-duplicated 'Nucleic acid sensing and interferon-driven antiviral response'; narrowed to focus on the ISG effector output rather than sensing/signalling.

name: Non-coding RNA processing and turnover
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'mRNA processing and turnover'; narrowing to non-coding RNA distinguishes it.

name: Corticotropin and glucocorticoid axis regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Growth hormone and hormonal growth signalling' on growth-related members; renamed to emphasize the corticotropin/glucocorticoid-specific members (CYP21A2, corticotropin secretion, glucocorticoid biosynthesis) that distinguish it.

name: Cholesterol-derived metabolite metabolism
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; no other theme addresses cholesterol-derived metabolites like bile acids or steroids specifically.

name: Extracellular matrix, adhesion and platelet-associated proteolysis
rationale: Core members (cell adhesion, fibronectin matrix formation, platelet degranulation, regulation of peptidase activity, FXIIa/kallikrein regulation) all concern extracellular matrix assembly, adhesive/platelet biology, and its proteolytic control. The weakly-included SRF/cytoskeletal remodeling member (0.29) is excluded, as it centers on transcriptional control of contractile cytoskeleton rather than matrix or protease regulation.

name: Metabolic and neurotrophic growth factor signaling
rationale: The original name repeated the parent's 'growth hormone' and 'hormonal' terms; members here center on leptin, insulin-like growth factor, GDNF, and eating behavior, distinguishing it from the stress-axis-focused sibling.

name: Cortical actin and septin dynamics in cell division and migration
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no other theme addresses cortical actin/septin dynamics in division and migration.

name: Kinase-driven growth signalling and its regulation
rationale: Both children (phosphorylation/methylation signalling and Hippo/MAPK/ERK regulation) plus the direct members (MAP2K mutant signalling, growth-factor signalling regulators, and regulation of protein localization downstream of kinase signalling) converge on growth-factor-driven kinase cascades and their control of localization and output; broader terms like 'signal transduction' would be too vague.

name: Protein O-glycosylation
rationale: All members concern the biosynthesis, upregulation, or disease consequences of O-linked glycan attachment to proteins.

name: Muscle stem cell homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Skeletal muscle development and regeneration' by repeating 'regeneration'; renamed to focus on satellite cell/stem cell maintenance aspect, distinguishing from sibling's proliferation/differentiation focus.

name: Endoderm-derived organ differentiation and morphogenesis
rationale: Both children concern endoderm-derived epithelial/endocrine identity and differentiation, and the direct member 'post-embryonic animal morphogenesis' extends this to organism-level morphogenesis following that differentiation; the weakly-included TBA member (0.28) is not coherent with this axis and is excluded.

name: RNA processing and turnover
rationale: Name does not repeat its parent and has no siblings to collide with; it remains distinct.

name: Hormonal and cellular homeostatic signalling
rationale: Children cover endocrine hormone biosynthesis/regulation, HPA axis, insulin secretion, growth/appetite endocrinology, stress/oxygen sensing and cAMP signalling, while direct members add GPCR/cAMP-linked signalling, mTOR/TOR pathways, ion channel and membrane potential responses, and stress/pH/mechanical sensing, all converging on hormone- and second-messenger-driven regulation of cellular and physiological homeostasis.

name: Cortical actomyosin polarity establishment
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Cytoskeletal organization in cell division and polarity' and overlaps parent 'Cytoskeletal control of mitotic spindle and cell polarity'; narrowed to actomyosin-based polarity establishment mechanism.

name: Glycosylation and glycan biosynthesis disorders
rationale: Both children cover protein glycosylation and glycosaminoglycan/proteoglycan biosynthesis together with their associated congenital disorders; no direct members exist, so the parent is simply the union of the two, avoiding restating either child's narrower scope.

name: Lamellipodium and focal adhesion regulation
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Cell-matrix adhesion and actin-driven migration', which shares adhesion/migration wording and members; the own theme is distinguished by lamellipodium morphogenesis and focal adhesion/actin nucleation regulation.

name: Lipid mediator signalling and metabolism
rationale: Covers GPCR-mediated lipid/nucleotide mediator signalling plus direct members on N-acylethanolamine metabolism and lipid-linked receptor trafficking, broader than the child but still anchored to lipid mediator biology.

name: Mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis
rationale: No sibling collision, but name overlaps conceptually with parent's spindle orientation focus; sharpened to emphasize assembly and cytokinetic machinery distinct from orientation cues.

name: Bacterial detection and NOD-like receptor signalling
rationale: No siblings and does not repeat parent name; already distinct and specific.

name: NOD-like receptor sensing and antigen presentation
rationale: Overlaps with 'NOD-like and endosomal TLR signaling with peptide transport' and 'Cytosolic pattern recognition and antimicrobial defence' which also cover innate bacterial sensing; specifying NOD-like receptor focus better reflects the NOD1/NLR members while keeping antigen presentation distinct.

name: Glycoprotein and proteoglycan biosynthesis
rationale: Original name overlapped with sibling 'Congenital disorders of glycosylation' since both include 'Diseases of glycosylation'; new name emphasizes the biosynthetic assembly process distinct from the disorder-focused sibling.

name: Phosphoinositide and nucleotide signaling metabolism
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Nucleotide and phosphate metabolism' and 'Nucleotide and cellular energy metabolism'; emphasizing phosphoinositide signaling role distinguishes this theme.

name: Filopodial and lamellipodial projection dynamics
rationale: Overlapped conceptually with parent 'Actin-driven cell shape remodeling' and risked overlap with sibling 'Neuronal process outgrowth'; narrowed to specific projection types distinct from neuronal outgrowth.

The children span unrelated biology - steroid conjugation/excretion, Y-chromosome/sex-chromosome dosage genes, and androgen biosynthesis - with no shared theme narrower than a vacuous 'sex-related biology' label.

name: Glutamate-dependent postsynaptic remodeling
rationale: Name collided with another theme elsewhere; revised to emphasize glutamate signaling driving postsynaptic actin and spine changes, consistent with member processes.

name: Dendrite and neurite arborization control
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere; members emphasize dendrite/neurite morphogenesis, arborization, and cytoskeletal regulation (filopodium, microtubule nucleation), distinct from sibling's focus on postsynaptic specialization maintenance and long-term synaptic plasticity.

name: Regulation of mitochondrial intrinsic apoptosis
rationale: Child covers the core mitochondrial apoptosis pathway; direct members add positive regulators of that pathway (via DNA damage or p53) and the BAX activation/oligomerization step central to it, so the umbrella is regulation of the intrinsic mitochondrial apoptotic route rather than apoptosis broadly.

name: DNA repair and recombination
rationale: Covers the DNA repair child plus the direct members on regulating mitotic recombination and telomere maintenance via recombination, both recombination-based genome maintenance processes not restricted to canonical repair.

name: Smooth muscle tone and sexual reflexes
rationale: Covers the child (smooth muscle contraction/relaxation) plus direct members tied to erection, copulation, and relaxation regulation, which are smooth-muscle-dependent reproductive reflexes; response to genistein is only weakly included (0.34) and not reflected in the name.

name: rRNA processing and transcription termination
rationale: Repeated parent name verbatim; members focus on rRNA maturation and transcription elongation/termination, distinguishing it from the sibling theme covering mRNA decay and splice site recognition.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint regulation
rationale: Overlapped parent's 'Mitotic cell cycle' phrasing and sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation and cell cycle control', which shares APC/C members; renamed to emphasize checkpoint/regulatory aspect (E2F, G2M checkpoint, APC/C inhibition) distinguishing it from spindle-mediated division and chromosome segregation siblings.

name: MHC antigen processing and presentation
rationale: All members concern loading of peptide or lipid antigen onto MHC/CD1 molecules and its consequences for T cell recognition, including the broader immune response this display initiates.

name: Endogenous antigen processing and presentation
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; this theme's members focus on endogenous/peptide-MHC assembly, distinguishing it from the sibling which includes T cell receptor engagement.

name: Cytoplasmic translation initiation and ribosome assembly
rationale: Name is distinct from both parents (amino acid metabolism; mRNA/protein quality surveillance) and from its sibling (mRNA export/quality control), clearly describing translation initiation and ribosome assembly specifically.

name: Insulin secretion signal integration
rationale: Repeated parent 'Insulin and incretin secretion' too closely; renamed to reflect regulatory integration role distinguishing it from sibling parents on sensing and exocytosis.

name: Insulin and hormone secretion regulation
rationale: All members describe the calcium- and cAMP-coupled exocytic machinery and its regulatory inputs that control insulin release from beta cells, with one broader member extending the same regulatory logic to endocrine hormone secretion generally.

name: Mesoderm and cardiac fate specification
rationale: Distinct from parent (subdivision/patterning vs specification into cardiac fate) and sibling (germ layer/axial segmentation is a different process).

name: Mitotic cyclin-CDK regulation
rationale: The name overlaps with the parent 'Cyclin-CDK activity control' without indicating what distinguishes it; narrowed to specify mitotic-phase regulation of cyclin-CDK complexes.

name: Gene expression machinery: transcription, RNA processing and translation
rationale: The children together span the full gene-expression pipeline from transcription/RNA processing machinery biogenesis to translation, and the direct members (SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting) extend this into the coupling of translation with protein targeting to membranes, so the parent must cover the whole synthesis-to-targeting continuum rather than any single stage.

name: Plasma lipoprotein remodeling and clearance
rationale: Both children concern the metabolic processing of circulating lipoprotein particles: triglyceride-rich particle lipolysis/remodeling and HDL assembly/clearance, with no direct members adding further scope.

name: Skeletal ossification and growth plate development
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Skeletal mineralization and matrix glycosylation' and 'Skeletal, craniofacial and appendage morphogenesis'; narrowed to focus on ossification and growth plate processes distinct from matrix glycosylation and craniofacial morphogenesis.

name: Mitotic spindle assembly
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitotic and meiotic chromosome segregation' on chromosome segregation; narrowed to focus solely on spindle assembly, distinguishing it from the chromosome segregation sibling.

name: Gametogenesis and germline meiosis
rationale: Both children cover meiotic recombination and gametogenesis; representative members (gonad development, male meiosis I, oocyte differentiation) extend this to the broader reproductive developmental programme, so a slightly wider umbrella covering germline meiosis and gamete formation fits without invoking gonad specification or hormonal signalling as core themes.

name: Nucleolar rRNA processing and ribosome subunit maturation
rationale: All members concern nucleolar steps in ribosome biogenesis: rRNA transcription and processing, spacer cleavage, subunit export, and regulated nucleolar protein localization supporting these processes.

name: Trace mineral metabolism and transport
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Vitamin and cofactor transport and metabolism' and other metal/ion siblings; narrowed to trace minerals specifically.

name: Ribonucleoside and ribose phosphate metabolism
rationale: Sibling 'Nucleotide pool metabolism and salvage' also involves nucleotide metabolism/salvage broadly; this theme's members are specifically ribonucleoside/ribose-phosphate biosynthesis and catabolism, distinguishing it from the deoxyribonucleoside-focused sibling.

name: Gustatory and mechanosensory taste perception
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Sensory perception'; specifying taste and oral mechanosensation distinguishes it from general sensory perception and situates it under oro-gastric sensation.

name: Endothelial control of leukocyte adhesion
rationale: Distinct from parents (broader adhesion/tissue homeostasis and barrier/quiescence themes) and from siblings (smooth muscle, differentiation, hemostasis, integrin adhesion), specifically naming endothelial regulation of leukocyte adhesion.

name: Photoreceptor and pigmentation biology
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is already distinct from its parent, which covers broader sensory receptor mechanisms; this theme specifically addresses photoreceptor and pigmentation biology.

name: Copper ion homeostasis and detoxification
rationale: All members at inclusion ≥0.5 concern copper handling—import, chaperoning, export and sequestration—with a broader detoxification of inorganic compounds member also centered on metal buffering; the weakly included cadmium detoxification pathway (0.39) shares the same metallothionein/transporter machinery but is excluded from the core name.

name: Type I interferon and TLR-RIG-I signalling
rationale: Collides with sibling 'Interferon-mediated antiviral defence' which shares identical top members; renamed to specify the TLR3/RIG-I/type I IFN pathway focus distinguishing it from other interferon-related themes.

name: Nucleocytoplasmic RNA and protein trafficking
rationale: Repeated 'nuclear gene expression' from the parent name; narrowing to the trafficking-specific aspect distinguishes it from the parent and from the sibling's proliferation/transcription focus.

name: PDGF-driven mesangial and glomerular development
rationale: Both children concern mesangial/capillary tuft formation and PDGF receptor signalling in mesenchymal cells, and the representative members (filtration regulation, migration in kidney development, PDGFRA signalling) all tie PDGF-driven mesenchymal signalling to glomerular structure and function; no direct members extend beyond this union.

name: IL-1 and TNF-driven inflammatory signaling
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Innate inflammatory cytokine signalling' and 'Innate pattern recognition and cytokine-driven inflammation'; narrowing to specific cytokine pathway family distinguishes it.

name: Leukocyte trafficking to inflamed tissue
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; it specifically covers trafficking to inflamed tissue, not the general adhesion/recruitment parent nor the chemotaxis/migration sibling.

name: Steroid hormone and fatty acid hydroxylation pathways
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; refers specifically to CYP-mediated hydroxylation of steroids and fatty acids, unlike the other metabolic/signalling themes.

name: Mitotic spindle cytoskeletal organization
rationale: Repeated the parent's scope; narrowing to spindle-specific organization distinguishes it from sibling's focus on cortical polarity.

name: Nephron development and patterning
rationale: All members concern nephron formation, segmentation and patterning within kidney morphogenesis, broader than renal tract morphogenesis alone by including nephron-specific patterning and epithelial development.

name: PINK1-Parkin mitophagy pathway
rationale: Too close to parent 'Mitophagy pathways' and indistinguishable from sibling 'Receptor-mediated mitophagy'; narrowed to the ubiquitin-dependent PINK1-Parkin mechanism.

name: Mitotic checkpoint and chromosome segregation
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Cell cycle progression and division' and 'Cell cycle progression and division machinery', which also center on mitotic cell cycle; this name instead reflects the theme's distinctive checkpoint signaling and sister chromatid separation members.

name: Rho family GTPase cycles
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'GTPase signalling and vesicle trafficking' which also covers GTPase activity regulation; members here are specifically RHO/RAC/CDC42 GTPase cycles, which better distinguishes it.

name: Insulin and incretin secretion
rationale: Name is distinct from both siblings due to inclusion of incretin secretion, which neither sibling covers, and differs from the parent's broader systemic scope.

name: Histone modification and imprinting
rationale: Sibling 'Chromatin and epigenetic regulation' shares chromatin organization and epigenetic regulation members, so the original name overlapped; the revised name reflects the histone-modifying enzymes and imprinting-specific members unique to this theme.

name: Checkpoint-driven phase transitions
rationale: Distinguishes from parent's general checkpoint control theme and siblings by focusing on the transition mechanism itself rather than division (sibling) or specific G1/S checkpoint (sibling).

name: Cardiac conduction system function
rationale: Covers the single child on conduction system electrical propagation plus direct members on overall cardiac conduction and its regulation, without restating the child's specific propagation focus.

name: TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD signalling
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and no siblings exist to collide with.

name: TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD signalling
rationale: The single child covers regulation of TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD signalling; direct members add the core SMAD signal transduction itself (including positive regulation) and the general TGF-beta signalling hallmark, so the parent broadens from regulation-only to the whole SMAD signalling axis without extending to other pathways.

name: Nucleotide biosynthesis regulation and phosphate transport
rationale: Overlaps sibling 'Nucleotide and pyridine cofactor metabolism' which also involves nucleotide metabolism broadly; revised to emphasize regulation of biosynthesis and transmembrane transport unique to this theme's members.

name: Biogenesis and modification of gene expression machinery
rationale: Covers ribosome/gene expression machinery biogenesis, protein hydroxylation and translational modification, and cotranslational targeting to membrane, all centered on producing and modifying the components of gene expression machinery without invoking a specific downstream pathway.

name: Viral entry and ER protein targeting
rationale: Too vague and overlaps conceptually with parent 'Viral entry and protein targeting to the ER membrane'; renamed to specify the actual mechanism distinguishing it from immune-signalling siblings.

name: Growth cone filopodial guidance
rationale: Sharpened to reflect the parent's filopodial/lamellipodial focus, distinguishing it as the guidance-specific application rather than general axon guidance.

name: Lymphocyte activation and cytotoxic immune regulation
rationale: Covers the child's broad monocyte/T/B/NK immunoregulation plus the direct members: NK-cell enrichment and IFN-gamma production regulation, both tied to lymphocyte activation and cytotoxic effector control.

name: Mitochondrial nitrogen and carbon metabolite handling
rationale: No siblings exist and no duplication indicated; kept name as-is since revision grounds are not met, but name nearly repeats parent verbatim without added specificity. Revising to reflect specific processes: amino acid/cofactor catabolism and shuttle reactions.

name: Nucleotide biosynthesis and ATP homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with 'Nucleotide and phosphate metabolism' and 'Nucleotide and phosphoinositide metabolism' siblings; narrowed to biosynthesis and ATP energy charge regulation to distinguish it.

name: Fertilization and reproductive process regulation
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Meiosis and gametogenesis', which shares male meiosis I, oocyte differentiation, and reproduction in multicellular organism; renamed to emphasize fertilization and regulatory members distinguishing it from that sibling.

name: cAMP catabolism and receptor-linked signaling
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Adenylate cyclase regulation and cAMP signalling' which shares cAMP biosynthetic process and response to caffeine; this theme is distinguished by cAMP catabolic process, serotonin/adrenergic receptor pathways, and muscle relaxation regulation.

name: SRF-driven smooth muscle phenotypic regulation
rationale: The original name also fits the sibling 'Myofibroblast contractility and matrix remodeling', which shares the same top SRF-target members; the theme's distinguishing focus is smooth muscle differentiation, migration, and proliferation control rather than general contractile programs.

name: Hypoxia-driven vascular remodelling
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Vascular injury response and wound healing'; narrowing to hypoxia-driven remodelling distinguishes it.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation
rationale: All children concern the mechanics and fidelity of segregating chromosomes during mitosis; broader terms like cell division or genome stability would exceed what the children share.

name: Glycosylase-mediated base excision
rationale: Repeated the parent name exactly; specifying the glycosylase-mediated mechanism distinguishes this theme from the broader base excision repair and oxidative DNA damage response parent.

name: Cristae architecture and inner mitochondrial membrane organization
rationale: All three members concern MICOS-, OPA1- and cardiolipin-dependent shaping and maintenance of cristae and the inner mitochondrial membrane.

name: Monoamine signalling in behaviour and locomotion
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than its parent by focusing on monoamine signalling in behaviour and locomotion.

name: Sensory transduction across modalities
rationale: All members concern the transduction step of sensory perception—vision, olfaction, taste, mechanotransduction/hearing and somatosensation—converting stimuli into neural signals; the weakly included Sensory processing of sound (0.28) is the hearing-specific subset of this same theme.

name: Endoderm epithelial cell fate specification
rationale: Overlaps heavily with siblings 'Endoderm-derived epithelial organ development', 'Endoderm-derived organ morphogenesis and differentiation', and 'Endoderm lineage specification and derivative development'; narrowed to focus on cell fate/specification aspect rather than organ development/morphogenesis.

name: G1/S transition and cell cycle protein turnover
rationale: Union covers the child's ubiquitin-proteasome control of cell cycle and p53 turnover plus direct members on G1 phase and the G1/S checkpoint, so it spans regulated proteolysis timing the G1-to-S commitment.

name: Nitrogen excretion and urea cycle
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Amino acid and sulfur compound metabolism' on amino acid scope; narrowed to nitrogen disposal pathways specific to this theme's members.

name: Nucleotide transport and pyridine metabolism
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere and identical to parent; revised to reflect transmembrane transport and pyridine/NAD catabolism members distinguishing it from sibling's biosynthesis focus.

The members span host defense against pathogens (neutrophil killing, phagocytic oxidants, symbiont response), pathogen nutrient acquisition from the host (iron and metal assimilation, energy metabolism manipulation), and unrelated small-molecule handling (lactone metabolism, ascorbic acid response, iron import), which share no single biological process tighter than 'host-microbe interactions and metabolism'.

name: Mitochondrial ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing
rationale: Core members (mitochondrial ribosome assembly, rRNA processing in the mitochondrion, both 1.00) concern building the mitoribosome from its rRNA; broader members (Metabolism of proteins, protein methylation, mitochondrial translation, rRNA processing) touch this but extend well beyond it, so the name reflects the tight, fully-covered core rather than the wider protein-metabolism umbrella.

name: Recombination-based telomere and chromosome maintenance
rationale: The child covers homologous recombination and telomere maintenance; direct members add negative regulation of DNA metabolic process, chromosome maintenance, and inhibition of DNA recombination at telomeres, all regulatory controls on the same recombination/telomere machinery. The umbrella covers both the mechanism and its regulation without broadening to general DNA repair.

name: Nuclear receptor signalling and circadian gene expression
rationale: Covers steroid hormone receptor signalling (and its regulation) plus circadian clock gene expression, the two children, with no direct members to broaden further.

name: Adaptive immune memory and monocyte regulation
rationale: Repeats parent's phrasing and overlaps heavily with sibling 'B and dendritic cell adaptive immune responses', which shares the same core B-cell enrichment members; distinguishing this theme's memory/monocyte-regulation content separates it.

name: Monoamine metabolism and transport
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers conjugation metabolism broadly) and sibling (xenobiotic biotransformation/conjugation/transport); this theme specifically concerns monoamine metabolism and transport, a different substrate class.

name: Adipocyte differentiation and lipid storage
rationale: All members describe adipogenesis and the lipid-droplet storage machinery it establishes, centred on PPARG-driven differentiation and downstream triglyceride/cholesterol handling.

name: Base excision and mitochondrial DNA repair synthesis
rationale: Union covers the child (general DNA replication/repair synthesis) plus direct members specifically on base excision repair patch resolution (POLB-dependent, AP-site resolution pathways) and mitochondrial DNA repair/metabolism (mtDNA repair, its regulation, DNA strand elongation), so the parent must span both repair-synthesis in general and the mitochondrial/BER-specific subset the direct members add.

name: Epithelial organ morphogenesis
rationale: Covers branching morphogenesis plus ectodermal differentiation, tube formation, and respiratory system development, all involving shaping of epithelial organs from progenitor cells into structured tissues.

name: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remodeling and clearance
rationale: Distinct from parent 'LDL and VLDL particle remodeling' (broader lipoprotein class covering triglyceride-rich particles like chylomicrons and their remnants) and from sibling 'Intestinal lipid and cholesterol absorption', which covers a different process entirely.

name: B lymphocyte identity and adaptive humoral immunity
rationale: Name distinguishes B lymphocyte identity/humoral immunity from parent's broader scope and from sibling's focus on lymphocyte development/activation.

name: Glycoconjugate and carbohydrate metabolism
rationale: Children and members converge on carbohydrate handling and its conjugation to proteins/lipids across ECM, transport, Golgi/lysosomal processing, and post-translational modification, plus a transporter defect affecting related solute handling.

name: Vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion
rationale: Core members (vesicle organization, organelle fusion, vesicle uncoating, endosome organization regulation, all >=0.89) share vesicle biogenesis, uncoating and fusion machinery; inositol phosphate metabolism (0.63) and synaptic vesicle recycling (0.28) are weaker, more specialized members that nonetheless feed into this same membrane traffic cycle.

name: Glycerophospholipid biosynthesis
rationale: Distinct from parents (glycerolipid/sphingolipid biosynthesis, phospholipid/lipid droplet metabolism) and sibling (phospholipid/lipid droplet homeostasis), clearly specifying glycerophospholipid biosynthesis.

name: Glycerophospholipid biosynthesis and remodelling
rationale: All members concern synthesis, interconversion or remodelling of glycerophospholipids, including specific branches for phosphatidic acid and cardiolipin.

name: Mammary gland development
rationale: Overlapped with parent's hormone signalling scope and sibling 'Steroid hormone response'; narrowed to the tissue-specific developmental process distinct from general hormone signaling.

name: Wound healing and fibrotic remodelling
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader injury response/repair) and sibling (coagulation factor disorders); already specific to fibrotic/wound remodeling processes.

name: Drug-resistant receptor tyrosine kinase mutants
rationale: Covers FLT3, KIT, PDGFR and ALK mutants that all confer resistance to targeted kinase inhibitors, generalising beyond the single-kinase children/members without invoking unrelated biology.

name: Galactose metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Glycan and glycolipid biosynthesis and degradation' which already covers glycan metabolism; narrowing to galactose distinguishes this theme.

name: AU-rich element mediated mRNA stability
rationale: Overlaps closely with sibling 'mRNA decay and turnover' since both concern mRNA lifetime; narrowing to the specific stabilization mechanism distinguishes it from decay-focused sibling.

name: Vascular remodeling and wound repair
rationale: Combines the contractile/wound-healing remodeling child with direct members on endothelial proliferation control and wound angiogenesis, all tissue-repair and vascular-tone processes; broader terms like general angiogenesis or proliferation are avoided since only wound-associated and negative-regulatory aspects are represented.

name: Endothelial barrier and quiescence maintenance
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Vascular wall remodelling' and parent's remodeling focus; renamed to emphasize homeostatic endothelial function rather than structural remodeling.

name: Actin-mediated pathogen entry and phagosome subversion
rationale: Distinct from all siblings; no collision with parent (none) or listed siblings.

name: Mitochondrial amino acid catabolism and cofactor lipoylation
rationale: Covers both children (mitochondrial amino/organic acid catabolism and its BCAA/alpha-keto acid disorders) plus the direct member protein lipoylation, which supplies the lipoyl cofactor these same catabolic dehydrogenase complexes require; narrower terms like just 'amino acid catabolism' would omit the lipoylation member.

name: Triglyceride synthesis and packaging
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Lipoprotein particle metabolism and transport'; narrowing to triglyceride synthesis/packaging distinguishes it from the sibling's focus on particle metabolism and transport.

name: Cytoplasmic translation
rationale: Both children (initiation machinery and protein synthesis) plus representative members span initiation, elongation, and the initiation complex, all within cytoplasmic translation; no direct members extend beyond this scope.

name: Cardiac septation and valve morphogenesis
rationale: Core members (outflow tract, mitral and pulmonary valve, atrioventricular valve, and ventricular septum development/morphogenesis) all describe building the septa and valves that separate cardiac chambers and vessels. Atrial septum primum morphogenesis (0.48) and regulation of heart morphogenesis (0.38) fit less tightly but remain consistent with this developmental theme.

name: Nucleoside phosphate interconversion
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; members involve nucleoside mono/di/triphosphate metabolism, distinguishing it from the generic duplicate.

name: Glycan metabolism and Golgi-lysosomal trafficking
rationale: Both children concern glycan/sugar metabolism and Golgi-lysosomal processing; the direct member, blood group biosynthesis, is itself a glycan-modification pathway occurring in this same compartment system, so it fits under the broader umbrella without extending beyond glycan/Golgi-lysosomal biology.

name: Pancreatic and intestinal epithelial differentiation
rationale: Sibling 'Endoderm-derived epithelial and endocrine differentiation' shares the same top members (hepatocyte nuclear factors, epithelial cell maturation, leukocyte migration), making the original name indistinguishable; this theme's distinct members concern pancreatic bud/endocrine progenitor regulation and intestinal stem cell homeostasis.

name: Nucleocytoplasmic transport and viral exploitation of export machinery
rationale: Distinct from parent (which is broader trafficking) and from sibling (chromatin/transcription); specifically covers viral exploitation of nuclear export machinery.

name: Sensory organ physiology
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Sensory perception'; renamed to emphasize organ-level physiological function distinct from perceptual processing.

name: Xenobiotic conjugation reactions
rationale: Repeated parent's 'biotransformation and conjugation' phrasing nearly verbatim; narrowing to conjugation reactions distinguishes it from the parent and from the sibling's biotransformation/transport focus.

The union mixes an unnamed heterogeneous gene list, a duplication-defined nuclear-pore-adjacent locus family, and an unrelated estrogen-receptor regulation term, with one child theme unnameable from samples alone; no honest umbrella narrower than 'miscellaneous biology' covers them.

name: Toll-like receptor triggered inflammation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Pattern recognition receptor-triggered cytokine response' and sibling 'Macrophage cytokine-driven inflammatory activation'; narrowed to the specific receptor class distinguishing this theme.

name: Mitophagy pathways
rationale: Under parent 'Mitochondrial quality control and maintenance', sibling 'Mitochondrial dynamics and turnover' covers fission/fusion; renaming to 'Mitophagy pathways' specifies selective degradation of mitochondria rather than organelles generally, matching parent scope.

name: Heart looping and chamber formation
rationale: Repeated the parent 'Heart morphogenesis' and overlapped with sibling 'Cardiac septation and valve morphogenesis'; renamed to specify the distinct developmental processes this theme covers.

name: Dendritic cell chemotaxis and signaling
rationale: The current name is broad enough to also describe the sibling 'Chemokine-driven leukocyte recruitment', which shares overlapping members like positive regulation of leukocyte chemotaxis and mononuclear cell migration. This theme's distinct focus includes dendritic cell chemotaxis, survival, and PLC/PKC signal transduction.

name: Gap junction and electrical coupling
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings, which focus on contraction/sarcomere biology, while this theme addresses gap junction and electrical coupling.

name: Host cell subversion by viral proteins
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and name is more specific than the parent 'Host-virus molecular conflict', clearly distinguishing this theme.

name: Neuronal and synaptic structural plasticity
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent name 'Neuronal signalling and synaptic connectivity'; members focus on structural remodeling of dendrites, spines, filopodia and microtubules rather than transmission itself, distinguishing it from the sibling's neurotransmitter release/receptor theme.

name: Calcineurin-NFAT feedback regulation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Calcineurin-NFAT hypertrophic signaling' and overlapped with sibling 'Regulation of muscle contraction'; narrowed to the specific calcium-dependent feedback mechanism distinguishing this theme.

name: Immune system signalling and cellular defence
rationale: Covers the union of innate and adaptive immune signalling, leukocyte differentiation/trafficking, and host-pathogen defence children, plus direct members like monocyte modules, leukocyte apoptosis regulation, and chemotactic/inflammatory production pathways; broader than any single child but excludes non-immune biology.

name: Phospholipid and lipid droplet metabolism
rationale: Union covers glycerophospholipid/phosphoinositide biosynthesis and remodeling plus lipid droplet triglyceride storage and homeostasis, all centered on phospholipid and neutral lipid handling without extending to unrelated lipid classes.

name: APC/C-mediated chromosome separation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Mitotic checkpoint and chromosome segregation' and sibling 'Cell cycle and mitotic division'; the members center on APC/C-driven degradation enabling sister chromatid/chromosome separation, which distinguishes it from both.

name: JAK-STAT-mediated interferon response
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; members center on JAK-STAT signaling and interferon-stimulated antiviral genes, distinguishing it from the other cytokine/interferon-related siblings.

name: Canonical Wnt transcriptional activation
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Beta-catenin destruction complex in Wnt signaling' under parent Wnt pathway components; narrowed to the nuclear/transcriptional arm of the pathway, distinguishing it from the destruction complex sibling.

name: Proteasome assembly and regulatory complexes
