rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Proteasomal protein degradation' by both covering proteasome function; renamed to focus specifically on proteasome assembly/regulatory subunit aspects, distinct from the degradation process itself.

name: ERAD pathway and deubiquitination regulation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Proteasomal and ERAD-mediated degradation' and overlapped with sibling 'Proteasomal protein degradation and assembly'; new name reflects the ERAD pathway regulation and deubiquitinase members distinguishing this theme.

name: Golgi to plasma membrane protein trafficking
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name differs from parent by specifying protein trafficking specifically to the plasma membrane, distinct from the parent's broader scope including cilium trafficking.

name: Cadherin adhesion loss driving EMT
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Cadherin-based adhesion dynamics'; revised to specify the EMT-related loss-of-adhesion process distinguishing it.

name: Amino acid and GABA transport
rationale: Both children concern transmembrane movement of amino acids, with GABA transport a specialized instance; no direct members extend the scope further.

name: MHC antigen processing and presentation
rationale: All members concern loading and display of peptide or lipid antigen on MHC class I, class Ib, or class II molecules for T/NK cell recognition, including the accessory chaperone and cell-surface components in the weakly included 'enriched in antigen presentation' module.

name: Adenylate cyclase-coupled aminergic and cholinergic GPCR signalling
rationale: The original name overlapped with siblings 'Cyclic nucleotide signalling' and 'Cholinergic receptor signalling', both of which it would also describe; the members specifically involve adenylate cyclase-activating adrenergic, serotonergic, and cholinergic GPCRs, which distinguishes it.

name: Ubiquitin chain conjugation and removal
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling, describing chain conjugation/removal mechanics rather than degradation broadly or ligase activation/chromatin turnover.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint and arrest signaling
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Mitotic cell cycle progression' which shares nearly identical members; renamed to emphasize checkpoint/arrest signaling (E2F, G2M checkpoint, TP53 arrest) distinguishing it from mitotic progression and G1/S turnover siblings.

name: Urea cycle and mitochondrial shuttle transport
rationale: Name is unique within the hierarchy and does not describe the sibling theme, which focuses on carbon shuttling and amino acid catabolism rather than urea cycle and shuttle transport specifically.

name: Regulation of small GTPase signalling
rationale: Core members (1.00-0.95 inclusion) cover activation, inhibition and signal transduction of small GTPases (Ras, Rho, Rab, Arf families); the weaker members on RHO effectors and RAB geranylgeranylation (0.50, 0.33) still concern GTPase regulation and downstream effector coupling, fitting the broader theme.

name: Nucleotide and nucleoside biosynthesis and catabolism
rationale: Own members are entirely nucleotide/nucleoside pathways, not central carbon metabolism (that overlaps siblings like glycolysis and mitochondrial carbon metabolism); renaming to reflect actual scope avoids implying overlap with those siblings.

name: Myofibroblast contractility and matrix remodeling
rationale: Core members (SRF/myocardin contractile gene program, cytoskeletal remodeling, fibroblast migration, fibronectin matrix formation) converge on myofibroblast-type contractile and matrix-forming activity; weakly included members (regulation of ECM organization, 0.34; regulation of connective tissue replacement, 0.48) extend this into broader fibrosis regulation but are consistent with the same contractile/matrix theme.

name: Heart morphogenesis
rationale: Union covers whole-organ cardiac shaping (chambers, septa, valves, outflow tract) plus pericardium development, all developmental morphogenesis of the heart and its surrounding sac, broader than either child but not extending beyond cardiac development.

name: Fatty acid oxidation and ketogenesis
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically names fatty acid oxidation paired with ketogenesis, unlike the sibling's broader carbon metabolism and ketone handling scope.

name: Tight and adherens junction assembly
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Cell junction assembly and signaling' and sibling 'Cadherin-mediated adhesion and EMT'; narrowed to specific junction types distinct from EMT-focused sibling.

name: Metallothionein-mediated detoxification response
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Metal ion homeostasis and xenobiotic response' and overlapped with parent's detoxification focus; narrowed to the metallothionein-based mechanism distinguishing this theme's members.

name: Metal ion detoxification and acquisition
rationale: Core members (iron import, cadmium detoxification, metal assimilation from host, response to symbiont) center on transition metal handling—uptake, buffering, and export of iron, cadmium, zinc and manganese. Weakly included members (response to herbicide 0.41, response to L-ascorbic acid 0.50, lactone metabolism 0.96) overlap through shared oxidative-stress and detoxification enzymes but are not primarily metal-focused; herbicide response is excluded as too marginal.

name: Meiotic chromosome segregation and cohesion
rationale: Sibling 'Mitotic cell division and chromosome segregation' already covers the mitotic case; this theme's members emphasize meiotic spindle assembly, meiotic cytokinesis, and sister chromatid cohesion, so naming it for meiosis and cohesion separates it.

name: APC/C-mediated mitotic checkpoint regulation
rationale: Would also describe sibling 'Cell cycle control and division' which shares the same core mitotic cell cycle members; this theme is distinguished by APC/C inhibition, ubiquitin ligase activity, and checkpoint gene sets (E2F targets, G2M checkpoint).

name: Heart morphogenesis and chamber formation
rationale: Covers both children (septation/valve and chamber/septum morphogenesis) plus direct members on heart growth and cardiocyte differentiation, all aspects of building the heart's structure from progenitors, broader than either child but excluding unrelated cardiac processes.

name: General muscle contraction and ion homeostasis
rationale: A sibling is literally named 'Muscle contraction' with nearly identical members (muscle system process, muscle contraction, regulation of muscle contraction), so the original name duplicated it; added 'general' to distinguish this broader grouping including ion homeostasis from the calcium-cycling specific siblings.

name: Ureteric bud and collecting duct development
rationale: Name duplicated a sibling of the same name and was broader than the parent 'Renal tubule and ureter morphogenesis'; narrowed to the collecting system aspect, distinct from 'Nephron development and patterning'.

name: Vascular smooth muscle and endothelial remodelling
rationale: Covers the SRF-driven contractile/cytoskeletal transcriptional program and the vascular wall remodelling/leukocyte trafficking child, both centered on vessel wall structural and cellular dynamics; no direct members extend beyond this.

name: Antimicrobial defence and metal ion restriction
rationale: Combines the peptide-mediated humoral defence child with direct members centred on host control of metal ions (iron import, host metal assimilation, and at lower inclusion cadmium detoxification), both being facets of innate nutritional/chemical defence against microbes.

name: Vesicular trafficking and lysosomal degradation
rationale: Overlapped heavily with multiple sibling trafficking themes (Vesicular membrane trafficking, Golgi-derived vesicle transport, Endomembrane vesicular trafficking and secretion); specifying lysosomal degradation distinguishes the protein turnover aspect from pure trafficking siblings.

name: Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Mitochondrial apoptosis and its regulation' and sibling 'Mitochondrial apoptosis regulation'; narrowed to the specific membrane permeabilization process.

name: Sulfur and aromatic amino acid metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with sibling themes 'Amino acid catabolism and cofactor metabolism' and 'Amino acid and bile acid transport and catabolism' which also describe amino acid catabolism broadly; this theme's members specifically concern sulfur-containing, aromatic, and non-proteinogenic amino acids plus vitamin B6.

name: Complement regulatory mechanisms
rationale: Nearly repeats parent name 'Complement activation and humoral regulation'; narrowing to regulatory mechanisms distinguishes it from the broader parent scope.

name: Alternative complement pathway activation
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere in the hierarchy; renamed to reflect the alternative pathway focus present in the members while remaining true of all of them.

name: Smooth and cardiac muscle remodelling
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Cardiac and skeletal muscle growth and proliferation' and 'Skeletal muscle development and regeneration'; narrowing to smooth/cardiac muscle distinguishes it from those skeletal-focused themes.

name: Phospholipid biosynthesis and phosphoinositide dephosphorylation
rationale: The original name overlapped with sibling 'Glycerolipid and phospholipid metabolism' and 'Phosphatase regulation and inositol phosphate metabolism'; the revised name specifies biosynthesis and phosphoinositide dephosphorylation, matching this theme's actual members (CL/PA/glycerophospholipid synthesis, phosphatidylinositol dephosphorylation) without fitting those siblings.

name: Ion homeostasis and transport
rationale: Covers the sodium/potassium child and adds phosphate ion homeostasis, sodium-phosphate cotransport, and related ATPase complex assembly/disease members; broad enough to unite sodium, potassium and phosphate handling without collapsing into generic 'transport'.

name: SREBP-mediated sterol sensing response
rationale: Repeated the parent (Cellular cholesterol homeostasis) and overlapped conceptually with the sterol regulatory scope; narrowed to the specific SREBP sensing mechanism, distinguishing it from the macrophage foam cell sibling.

The children cover inositol phosphate and phosphoinositide signalling/metabolism, but the direct members (a heterogeneous housekeeping gene set and negative regulation of IGF receptor signalling) share no common biology with each other or with the children beyond a generic 'signalling' label, so no tight umbrella exists.

name: Vasopressin-mediated water reabsorption
rationale: Repeated parent's osmotic balance concept too closely; narrowed to vasopressin/ADH-driven mechanism, distinguishing it from the aquaporin/glycerol channel sibling.

name: Synaptic transmission and plasticity
rationale: The single child covers excitatory synapse structure/plasticity; direct members add GABAergic and kainate-receptor transmission, so the parent must span both excitatory and inhibitory synaptic signalling and its plasticity, without restating either.

name: Neurotransmitter receptor signalling in behaviour
rationale: The original name's broad reference to drugs and behaviour also fits the sibling 'Behavioral responses to drugs and reward' (locomotion, exploration, behavior); the members here center on specific receptor/ligand signalling (nicotinic, opioid) rather than general drug-response behaviors, so a receptor-signalling focus separates it.

Members span unrelated immune biology—TF-motif and monocyte gene modules, cytokine/NF-kB signalling, IL-8 regulation, nitrogen-species response and RHO/NADPH oxidase activation—with no single mechanism or pathway shared by all.

name: Sphingolipid and fatty acid derivative metabolism
rationale: The child covers fatty acid chain modification/derivatives, while direct members add sphingolipid (sphingomyelin) biosynthesis and ether lipid metabolism, so the parent must span both fatty acid derivative and sphingolipid/ether lipid metabolic routes.

name: Integrated stress response and eIF2α-mediated translational control
rationale: Core members converge on stress sensing that triggers eIF2α phosphorylation and downstream ATF4/CHOP translational reprogramming (cellular response to stress, regulation of translation in response to stress, PERK regulation of gene expression, HRI response to heme deficiency, Reactome cellular stress responses). The weakly included negative regulation of kinase activity (0.79) and mTORC1 signalling (0.44) members are excluded as they concern kinase feedback and anabolic growth rather than the stress-translation axis itself.

name: Mitochondrial calcium and apoptosis regulation
rationale: Both children concern mitochondrial membrane control of calcium flux and apoptotic signalling, with no direct members extending beyond that scope.

name: Peroxisome biogenesis and protein import
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers fatty acid metabolism broadly) and sibling (chain modification), focusing specifically on peroxisome biogenesis and protein import machinery.

name: Peroxisomal protein import and biogenesis
rationale: All members concern peroxisome biogenesis via protein import machinery (matrix and membrane protein import, receptor recycling), with the hallmark set broadly covering peroxisomal function tied to this same import system.

name: Pancreatic beta cell identity and insulin secretion
rationale: All members concern beta cell development, survival, proliferation or the incretin/GLP-1 signalling that drives insulin secretion; carbohydrate homeostasis (0.40) is broader but still centred on beta cell/insulin function, so it is included.

name: Mitotic spindle and cytokinesis apparatus
rationale: Too broad relative to siblings focused on specific mechanisms (licensing, ubiquitination, genome maintenance); narrowed to spindle/cytokinesis machinery specifically.

name: DNA repair pathways
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'DNA damage response' and parent's 'response' term; narrowed to focus on repair mechanisms specifically.

name: Neural tube patterning outcomes
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Hedgehog signalling in neural tube patterning'; renamed to emphasize downstream morphogenetic effects distinct from the signalling mechanism itself.

name: Hypothalamic-pituitary hormone secretion
rationale: Both children involve regulation of hormone secretion along hypothalamic-pituitary endocrine axes (gonadotropin and adrenal/HPA), narrower than general endocrine signalling.

name: Neural crest and organ-specific cell fate commitment
rationale: Repeated the parent name; members include neural crest, heart, and endothelin-related fate commitment distinct from sibling's axis/mesoderm patterning focus.

name: Dendrite and postsynaptic cytoskeletal remodeling
rationale: The child covers neuronal cytoskeletal remodeling in projection growth/branching broadly, while direct members specifically add dendrite morphogenesis/extension regulation and postsynaptic actin organization, so the parent generalizes to dendritic and postsynaptic structural remodeling without invoking axon-specific or non-neuronal cytoskeletal biology.

name: Metal ion-induced oxidative stress response
rationale: Overlapped with 'Metal and porphyrin homeostasis' and 'Metal and xenobiotic homeostasis'; narrowed to the specific oxidative stress signaling triggered by metal ions rather than general homeostasis.

name: ER stress cross-talk with GCN2
rationale: No sibling collision, but name overlaps parent's scope; narrowed to specify the connection between ER stress/UPR and GCN2-mediated amino acid stress signaling, distinguishing it as the intersection rather than an independent pathway.

name: Nucleolar RNA modification and snoRNP assembly
rationale: All core members (snoRNP assembly, rRNA modification, snRNA modification, guanine-N7 methylation) concern chaperoned assembly or chemical modification of noncoding RNAs (rRNA, snRNA, tRNA) that underlies ribosome and spliceosome maturation; the weakly included tRNA pseudouridine synthesis and negative regulation of tRNA metabolism members also fit under this broader RNA-modification umbrella.

name: Innate myeloid immune receptor signalling
rationale: Name is already distinct from parent and siblings; no other theme specifically covers myeloid immune receptor signalling.

name: Nucleotide metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Nucleoside and analogue metabolism' by repeating 'nucleoside'; narrowing to nucleotide-specific metabolism distinguishes it.

name: Nucleotide-sugar and glycoconjugate biosynthesis
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; members are specifically about nucleotide-sugar intermediates and protein/lipid glycosylation, not transport disorders, distinguishing it from sibling metabolic themes like Digestion and sugar absorption.

name: Mitotic chromosome condensation and cohesion
rationale: No siblings present and the name is more specific than the parent, distinguishing mitotic condensation/cohesion mechanics from general chromatin organization.

name: Chaperone-assisted protein and tubulin folding
rationale: Distinct from parent (folding vs turnover/degradation) and sibling (degradation focus); specific to chaperone-mediated folding of proteins and tubulin.

name: Neutrophil and phagocyte antimicrobial killing
rationale: The child covers antimicrobial defence and metal restriction broadly, while the direct members add neutrophil/PMN-specific bactericidal activity and phagocyte manipulation by pathogens; the umbrella centers on phagocyte-mediated antimicrobial killing, excluding the weak 0.26 metabolism-manipulation member from defining the name.

name: Cell adhesion and contractile machinery in tissue repair
rationale: Union covers epithelial/stromal migration in wound healing plus SRF-driven contractile programs, cell-cell/cell-matrix adhesion, and platelet degranulation, all sharing adhesion and contractile machinery deployed in tissue repair and hemostasis contexts.

name: Glycerolipid and sphingolipid biosynthesis
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; no other sibling specifically addresses glycerolipid/sphingolipid biosynthesis.

name: GTP and nucleoside triphosphate metabolism
rationale: Name duplicated an existing theme elsewhere; revised to reflect the specific focus on GTP/NTP biosynthesis and transport found in its members.

name: Epidermal and appendage differentiation
rationale: Both children (ectodermal/epidermal differentiation; keratinization and collagen matrix assembly) and the representative members (ectodermal cell differentiation, molting cycle, epithelial cell differentiation) converge on skin and appendage epithelial commitment, cornification and structural matrix assembly, with no direct members pushing beyond this scope.

name: Monocyte and myeloid inflammatory activation
rationale: Core members (both TBA monocyte-chemokine modules, IL15/IL23/TNF activation, TNFa-NFkB signalling) converge on monocyte/myeloid recruitment and cytokine-driven inflammatory activation with feedback control. Weaker members (motif-defined TF cluster at 0.43, dendritic cell response at 0.25, IL-8 negative regulation at 0.54) touch related inflammatory signalling but are not required to fit the core theme.

name: Synaptic architecture and plasticity
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Neuronal development and synaptic transmission' and sibling scope; narrowed to structural organization and plasticity mechanisms distinct from connectivity formation and neurotransmitter signalling.

name: Cytokine signalling
rationale: All members concern cytokine (interleukin, interferon, CSF, TNF) production or receptor signalling and its downstream immune effects.

name: Chromosome segregation checkpoint control
rationale: Original name was broader than parent 'Mitotic chromosome segregation fidelity' and overlapped with sibling 'Genome stability maintenance'; narrowed to checkpoint control mechanisms specific to segregation fidelity.

name: Metal and porphyrin homeostasis
rationale: Distinct from siblings 'Metal ion homeostasis and cellular stress response' and 'Metal and xenobiotic homeostasis' due to inclusion of porphyrin-specific metabolism; not a repeat of parent.

name: Lipoprotein remodeling and transfer
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Lipoprotein particle assembly and clearance' and sibling 'Lipoprotein particle metabolism'; renamed to focus on remodeling/transfer processes distinct from assembly/clearance and general metabolism.

name: Regulated proteolysis and protein maturation
rationale: Name is distinct from parent 'Protein folding and turnover' and sibling 'Protein quality control and aggregate clearance', clearly denoting proteolytic maturation processes.

name: Nuclear genome regulation and cell division
rationale: Covers all five children spanning gametogenesis, cell cycle/genome maintenance, transcription/gene expression, chromatin modification and nuclear transport, plus direct members on TP53 regulation and suppression of viral transcription, which are nuclear regulatory processes affecting gene expression and genome integrity.

name: Hematopoietic lineage commitment and maturation
rationale: Covers the myeloid/megakaryocyte child plus erythroid differentiation, stem cell homeostasis, erythropoietin signalling, and general structure maturation; the outlying inner cell mass differentiation member is weakly included (0.25) and left as a minor exception.

name: Nephric duct and ureter development
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Nephron and kidney development' which shares nearly identical members (kidney morphogenesis, cell differentiation, nephron development); this theme is distinguished by its duct/ureter/patterning specific members.

name: Hypoxia and glycolytic metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; hypoxia response combined with glycolysis differentiates it from purely metabolic siblings like glycolysis/redox cofactor metabolism.

name: Cholesterol transport and uptake regulation
rationale: Both children (HDL handling, macrophage cholesterol/foam cell biology) plus the direct members (VLDLR internalisation, NR1H2/3-mediated limits on cholesterol uptake, and regulation of lipid/cholesterol metabolic process) all concern regulating cholesterol transport, uptake, and clearance across lipoprotein and cellular systems, tighter than generic lipid metabolism.

name: Endocrine regulation of growth and appetite
rationale: Distinct from siblings like HPA axis regulation, insulin biosynthesis, and endocrine and metabolic homeostasis; specifically covers growth and appetite hormonal regulation, no collision.

name: Sarcomere structure and contractile mechanics
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Muscle contraction and growth regulation' on contraction; narrowed to sarcomere structural mechanics to distinguish from growth regulation and gap junction siblings.

name: Chemokine-mediated lymphocyte and monocyte chemotaxis
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Leukocyte chemotaxis and migration' which also covers general leukocyte migration/chemotaxis; this theme is distinguished by chemokine receptor signaling and specific lymphocyte/mononuclear cell regulation.

name: Neurotrophin signalling and axon regeneration
rationale: All members concern neurotrophin (NGF/BDNF) production, receptor signalling (TrkB, p75NTR complexes and downstream survival/death pathways), or the axon/neuron projection regrowth these signals support; NGF-stimulated transcription (0.38) is a weaker fit but still falls under neurotrophin signalling downstream effects.

name: Spindle and cortical cytoskeletal organization for cell division
rationale: Union covers spindle assembly/positioning and cortical/septin cytoskeleton polarity that together set division axis and cleavage; broader than either child alone but restricted to cytoskeletal control of mitotic geometry and polarity, not general cytoskeleton biology.

name: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and derived disorders
rationale: Covers the child (long-chain fatty acid and ether lipid metabolism) plus direct members: alpha-oxidation, omega-hydroxylase P450 pathway, and CYP4F22/SLCO2A1 defects, all peroxisomal/microsomal fatty acid oxidation routes and their associated disease states; 'miscellaneous substrates' is a residual catch-all included for completeness.

name: Plasma membrane amino acid transport
rationale: Name collides with another theme elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to reflect the plasma membrane transmembrane transport focus of its members, distinguishing it from the sibling's GABA/glutamate-inclusive theme.

name: Gastrulation and embryonic axis patterning
rationale: All members concern early embryonic patterning: germ layer formation via gastrulation and EMT, axis specification (A/P, midbrain-hindbrain, forebrain), and neural plate/mesoderm formation, unified by shared Nodal/Wnt/FGF/BMP signalling and organizer logic; cell fate determination (0.28) is the most general but still fits the developmental patterning theme.

name: Stress and nutrient signalling with p53
rationale: Union covers cellular stress response, mTOR/nutrient sensing, and the p53 pathway, all converging on damage/stress sensing and growth arrest decisions; broader terms like 'signalling' alone would omit the p53-specific damage-response element.

name: Sensory transduction and mechanosensation
rationale: Covers both children—broad sensory transduction across modalities and auditory/vestibular mechanotransduction—plus direct GO terms like general sensory perception and response to mechanical stimulus, without repeating either child's name.

name: ERBB2-EGFR receptor signaling
rationale: All members concern ERBB2/EGFR heterodimer signaling, its kinase-domain mutant forms, downstream effectors like PLC-gamma, and resistance to HER2-targeted therapy arising from that signaling.

name: Mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy
rationale: Repeated 'biogenesis' from parent and overlapped with sibling's 'maintenance/turnover'; narrowed to specify mitophagy as the turnover mechanism, distinct from sibling's quality control/repair focus.

name: RNA turnover and small RNA-mediated silencing
rationale: Union covers mRNA decay/quality control and the biogenesis-to-silencing pathway of microRNAs/other small ncRNAs, without invoking chromatin or transcriptional mechanisms not present.

name: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
rationale: All four members describe the mitochondrial respiratory chain and ATP synthase machinery driving oxidative phosphorylation, including their assembly and supporting factors.

name: Neuronal process outgrowth and guidance
rationale: Both children cover axon guidance and growth cone-driven neurite/growth outgrowth control; the umbrella spans the shared cytoskeletal and guidance-cue signalling without adding unrelated biology.

name: FGFR and EGFR ligand-activated signaling cascades
rationale: The current name broadly describes RTK signaling, which also fits the sibling theme's members (PI3K/AKT, PIP-mediated signaling, FGFR2c activation); the own theme is specifically about FGFR/EGFR ligand binding and downstream PLC-gamma cascades.

name: Tube and organ morphogenesis
rationale: Covers branching morphogenesis of epithelial organs plus tube development, respiratory system development, and the broader anatomical structure formation, all centered on shaping tubular/epithelial organ structures during development.

name: Membrane-bound organelle vesicle transport
rationale: Too similar to several siblings covering vesicular trafficking (Golgi-derived vesicle transport, Protein sorting/secretion/endosomal trafficking, Post-Golgi trafficking, Endomembrane vesicular trafficking and secretion); narrowed to organelle-to-organelle vesicle transport distinct from Golgi/endosome/synaptic-specific siblings.

name: Pancreatic endocrine and epithelial development
rationale: All members concern pancreatic (and related endodermal epithelial) lineage specification, maturation, proliferation and survival, centered on transcription factor programs (PDX1, NEUROG3, HNF factors, NKX6-1) governing beta cell and acinar/ductal identity.

name: Lipid droplet dynamics and regulation
rationale: Only one child theme, covering lipid droplet formation, turnover, and regulatory control of lipid storage, so the parent stays at the same scope as its sole child.

name: Kidney and urinary tract development
rationale: Covers nephron/renal tract morphogenesis plus collecting duct, metanephric tubule and nephron epithelium development, the broader union of kidney organogenesis processes.

name: Antibody-mediated hypersensitivity signalling and its regulation
rationale: All members concern Fc receptor/IgE-IgG signalling driving hypersensitivity reactions (type IV, Fc, Fc-epsilon) and the inhibitory mechanisms that restrain them (negative regulation of acute inflammatory response and degranulation).

name: Bcl-2 family regulation of MOMP
rationale: Repeated parent 'Intrinsic apoptotic signalling' in scope; narrowed to the specific regulatory mechanism (Bcl-2 family control of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization) to distinguish from parent and sibling.

name: Gastrulation movements and axis formation
rationale: Overlapped with parent's 'germ layer patterning' and sibling 'germ layer and mesoderm patterning'; renamed to emphasize gastrulation morphogenetic movements and body axis establishment, distinct from germ layer fate patterning.

name: Antiviral ISG effector mechanisms
rationale: Nearly identical to parent theme name 'Interferon-stimulated gene antiviral defence'; revised to emphasize the specific ISG effector proteins (ISG15, antimicrobial IFN-stimulated genes) distinguishing it from the parent's broader scope.

name: Hormonal regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism
rationale: Overlapped broadly with several siblings covering energy metabolism (glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration, hypoxia and glycolytic metabolism); narrowed to the specific hormonal regulatory mechanism distinguishing this theme.

name: Xenobiotic biotransformation and conjugation
rationale: Repeated the parent name verbatim, giving no distinguishing information despite having no siblings; revised to reflect the phase I/II metabolism and conjugation focus of its members.

name: Erythrocyte membrane protein organization
rationale: Name collides with another theme elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to reflect the specific members concerning membrane scrambling, ER organization, and erythrocyte membrane protein defects (RHAG, SLC4A1), distinguishing it from siblings.

name: Replication and innate defence evasion mechanisms
rationale: Repeated parent phrase 'virus-host interactions'; narrowed to the replication/innate-defence focus distinguishing it from the SARS-CoV-2 entry sibling.

name: Cytoplasmic translation elongation and rescue
rationale: The current name focuses on initiation, but the sibling 'Cytoplasmic protein synthesis' shares the same initiation-related members; this theme also includes elongation, ribosome rescue, and regulation of translation, which better distinguishes it.

name: NF-kB and NOD-like receptor signalling
rationale: No siblings and name differs from parent; distinguishes signalling pathways upstream of caspase activation.

name: Chemosensory and mechanosensory receptor signaling
rationale: Repeated the parent name exactly; renamed to specify non-photoreceptor sensory modalities, distinguishing it from the sibling 'Photoreceptor biology'.

name: B lymphocyte identity and adaptive immunity
rationale: All three children converge on B cell lineage markers, receptor signalling and humoral/adaptive immune function; dendritic cell markers appear only as context for B cell activation, not as a separate axis, so this stays tighter than 'adaptive immunity' broadly.

name: Ribosomal subunit assembly
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Ribosomal RNA transcription and ribosome assembly' and sibling 'rRNA transcription and processing'; narrowed to the assembly step distinct from transcription/processing.

name: Base excision repair of abasic sites and strand breaks
rationale: All members concern base excision repair machinery resolving abasic sites, single-strand breaks, or NEIL3-mediated crosslink unhooking that feeds into this same repair route.

name: Cholinergic and aminergic GPCR-cAMP pathways
rationale: The current name's cAMP focus overlaps with sibling 'Adenylate cyclase regulation and cAMP signalling', whose members (cAMP biosynthetic process, cyclic nucleotide GPCR pathway, response to caffeine) are also covered by this name; the revision emphasizes the cholinergic/aminergic receptor specificity unique to this theme.

name: dNTP sanitization via hydrolase catabolism
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Deoxyribonucleotide pool metabolism' and parent's salvage scope; narrowed to emphasize the hydrolytic sanitization/catabolic breakdown mechanism distinct from salvage/synthesis pathways.

name: Humoral immune response regulation
rationale: All members center on B cell antibody production, class switching, affinity maturation, and its positive/negative regulatory circuits (T cell help, complement, inhibitory receptors); IL-21 production and IgA switching are narrower slices of this same axis.

name: Intestinal lipid absorption and lipoprotein assembly
rationale: Unites the child theme (chylomicron/VLDL assembly and lipoprotein transport) with direct members on intestinal cholesterol and lipid absorption, covering both the enterocyte uptake step and the particle assembly/transport step without broadening to general lipid metabolism.

name: mRNA and protein quality surveillance
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Ribosome biogenesis and mRNA metabolism' and repeats 'Ribosome biogenesis' from parent; renamed to focus on the surveillance/quality-control aspect distinguishing it.

name: Regulation of fatty acid and lipid metabolic processes
rationale: The sterol/cholesterol emphasis overlaps with the sibling theme centered on cholesterol homeostasis and biosynthesis; this theme's distinct members are broader fatty acid and general lipid regulation.

name: DNA replication initiation and elongation
rationale: The child covers licensing/synthesis broadly, while direct members add specific initiation steps (origin firing) and strand elongation, so the parent must span both initiation and elongation phases of replication without invoking licensing-specific machinery as the sole frame.

name: Sphingolipid and glycosphingolipid metabolism
rationale: Distinguishes from parent's broad glycoprotein biosynthesis focus and sibling's glycosaminoglycan/skeletal focus by specifying the actual glycolipid class processed in Golgi and lysosome.

name: Ferroptosis regulation and protein repair
rationale: Shares its core members (response to oxygen radical, cell redox homeostasis, cellular oxidant detoxification) with sibling 'Mitochondrial energy metabolism and oxidative stress', so the oxidative-damage framing fits that sibling too; ferroptosis and protein repair are the distinguishing elements unique to this theme.

name: Meiotic progression and gonadal maturation
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'Germ cell meiosis and fertilisation' on the meiosis term; narrowed to emphasize gonadal/reproductive maturation distinct from fertilisation events.

name: Potassium channel regulation and cardiac repolarization phases
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Cardiac excitability and electrical conduction', which shares cardiac membrane repolarization regulation; narrowed to focus on potassium transport and specific repolarization/depolarization phases distinct from general conduction.

name: Macrophage activation and TLR2-mediated cytokine regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Innate pattern recognition and inflammatory signalling', which also covers inflammatory response and macrophage activation; this theme is distinguished by its focus on macrophage cytokine production and TLR2-specific regulation.

name: Glycerol metabolism and transport
rationale: Name is distinct from parent (which covers carbohydrates broadly) and sibling (hexose/monosaccharide transport), clearly specifying glycerol-specific metabolism and transport.

name: Gonadotropin signalling and ovarian follicle response
rationale: All members concern gonadotropin (FSH/LH) secretion or the cellular response to it, driving follicle maturation and ovulation; activin receptor signalling (0.44) ties into the same FSH-regulatory feedback loop.

name: Proteoglycan and glycoprotein biosynthesis
rationale: Overlapped with parent's ECM/glycosaminoglycan focus and sibling 'Glycosaminoglycan and extracellular matrix biology'; narrowed to the specific biosynthetic glycoconjugate pathways covered.

name: Metal ion transport regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Metal and xenobiotic detoxification response' and parent 'Heavy metal and drug detoxification'; narrowing to ion transport/homeostasis distinguishes it from detoxification-focused siblings.

name: Mitochondrial fission fusion and mitophagy
rationale: Repeated the parent name almost verbatim; specifying fission/fusion and mitophagy distinguishes it from the parent and from the sibling's broader homeostasis focus.

name: Mitotic chromosome structure maintenance
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings, focusing on structural maintenance rather than segregation mechanics.

name: Serotonin and monoamine metabolism
rationale: The child theme covers degradation/clearance of monoamine neurotransmitters broadly, while the direct members add serotonin-specific metabolism, uptake and clearance; together they form the union of monoamine (including serotonin) turnover pathways.

name: Growth cone actin dynamics
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Dendritic and neurite cytoskeletal remodeling' and closely echoed parent 'Neurite outgrowth and collapse signaling'; narrowed to growth cone actin dynamics to distinguish focus.

name: Innate nucleic acid receptor activation
rationale: Overlapped with parent name (nucleic acid sensing/interferon) and with sibling covering interferon-driven antiviral effectors; renamed to focus on receptor-level sensing step distinct from downstream interferon effector response.

name: Regulation of protein stability and localisation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; focuses on post-translational protein stability/localisation rather than genome maintenance, chromatin, or p53 pathways.

name: Ubiquitin-tagged substrate degradation
rationale: Nearly repeated the parent 'Ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation' and overlapped with sibling 'Proteasome function and regulation'; narrowed to the substrate-tagging and turnover process rather than proteasome machinery itself.

name: Pyruvate metabolism
rationale: Repeated 'central carbon metabolite metabolism' from parent; narrowing to pyruvate metabolism distinguishes it.

name: Spliceosome assembly and 3' end formation
rationale: Distinct from parent themes and its sibling covering transcription initiation/elongation; no collision.

name: Type I interferon signalling pathway regulation
rationale: The name overlaps with siblings 'Cytokine and interferon signalling' and 'Host-virus interactions and antiviral interferon regulation', which are equally about interferon-mediated antiviral defence; narrowing to the specific type I interferon pathway regulation members (production, TLR3/RIG-I signaling regulation) distinguishes this theme.

name: Nitrogen assimilation pathways
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Amino acid metabolism' and blurred into parent's nitrogen focus; renamed to specify nitrogen assimilation distinct from urea cycle excretion and amino acid catabolism.

name: Craniofacial, ocular and axial structure development
rationale: Union covers the craniofacial/cranial nerve child plus direct members on extraocular muscle, optic nerve, diaphragm, and general post-embryonic morphogenesis; all concern regional anatomical structure formation beyond the embryonic stage, broader than the craniofacial child alone but not stretching to all morphogenesis.

name: T and B lymphocyte receptor signalling and development
rationale: The current name overlaps too closely with sibling 'T cell differentiation and regulatory signalling', which also covers T cell activation/proliferation; this theme uniquely combines T cell receptor/costimulation signalling with B cell development and proliferation, which the new name captures.

name: Stress-induced translational control and proteostasis
rationale: Both children concern eIF2α-driven translational attenuation under proteotoxic and integrated stress; direct members (cellular stress response, protein misfolding response, stress translation regulation) reinforce the same axis, so the umbrella covers translational and proteostatic stress responses without broadening to all cellular stress biology.

name: Photoreceptor outer segment renewal
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Photoreceptor structural biogenesis'; renaming to focus on maintenance/renewal of outer segments distinguishes it from structural biogenesis and phototransduction siblings.

name: ATP homeostasis and energy metabolism
rationale: Repeated parent 'Nucleotide biosynthesis and ATP homeostasis' and overlapped with sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism and transport'; renamed to emphasize energy/ATP homeostasis aspect distinct from nucleotide metabolism siblings.

name: Phospholipid and neutral lipid storage regulation
rationale: Members centre on triglyceride/lipid droplet storage and mobilisation (storage, lipophagy x2) and on regulation of phospholipid biosynthesis/metabolism (phosphatidylcholine, phospholipid biosynthesis/metabolism regulation), plus surfactant lipid loading via ABCA3, which ties phospholipid supply to lamellar body/droplet biogenesis. The weakly included triglyceride metabolic process (0.28) is excluded as too broad.

name: Adrenergic and calcitonin receptor signalling with secretion inhibition
rationale: Overlapped heavily with sibling 'cAMP signalling and secretion regulation' which shares identical top members; revised to reflect this theme's distinct adrenergic/calcitonin receptor and negative secretion regulation content.

name: Homologous recombination and interstrand crosslink repair
rationale: The generic name 'DNA repair' overlaps with sibling 'DNA damage repair'; members here specifically involve HRR/BRCA-PALB2 pathways and ICL resolution, distinguishing it from the excision-repair-focused sibling.

name: Transcription termination and mRNA 3'-end processing
rationale: Not a duplicate and distinct from siblings: RNA Pol II pause/elongation sibling covers elongation not termination, and the mRNA 3'-end processing and decay sibling centers on catabolic/decay processes, unlike this theme's termination and histone pre-mRNA processing focus.

name: Body plan and craniofacial organogenesis
rationale: Core high-inclusion members (skeletal system morphogenesis, appendage development, face development, eyelid development, embryonic eye morphogenesis) share axial/appendage patterning via Hox and craniofacial neural crest-driven organogenesis; weaker members (facial nerve morphogenesis 0.29, thyroid gland development 0.33, digestive system development 0.26) touch related patterning factors but are only loosely tied and are excluded from the core claim.

name: Myofibril assembly and contractile apparatus organization
rationale: The current name overlaps with sibling 'Muscle development and regeneration' and 'Striated muscle structural development'; the members are specifically about sarcomere/myofilament assembly and contraction, which distinguishes it from the broader developmental siblings.

name: Toll-like receptor and RIG-I sensing pathways
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling names/members describing type I interferon induction and signaling; this theme is distinguished by its TLR and RIG-I sensing components rather than interferon production itself.

name: Dendritic and synaptic structural plasticity
rationale: Covers all three children, which describe regulation, postsynaptic organization, and structural plasticity of dendrites/synapses, plus the direct member on dendritic transport of neurotransmitter receptor complexes supporting that same structural remodeling; tighter than general neuronal signalling.

name: Isoprenoid and sterol lipid metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent (which also covers peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism) and from sibling (peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism and biogenesis); already specific to isoprenoid/sterol lipids.

name: TNF-mediated signaling pathway
rationale: Repeats parent's combination of TNF and non-canonical NF-kB themes; own members are specifically TNF signaling and NIK-driven noncanonical NF-kB activation, while sibling covers TLR-driven IKK/NF-kB activation, so narrowing to TNF-mediated signaling avoids overlap and parent repetition.

name: HPA axis and adrenal steroidogenesis regulation
rationale: Members converge on the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis: control of corticotropin secretion, glucocorticoid biosynthesis regulation (including CYP11B1/CYP21A2 steroidogenic defects), and growth signalling driven by the same neuroendocrine axis (GH/IGF1, ghrelin). Weakly included multicellular organism growth (0.28) and CYP11B1 defect (0.26) fit loosely but are consistent with this theme.

name: rRNA processing and transcription termination
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'RNA processing and translation' which shares identical top members; also echoes parent's broad scope. Narrowed to the actual themes present: rRNA maturation, transcription termination, and mRNA decay/splicing, distinguishing it from the translation-focused sibling.

name: Growth factor and insulin receptor signal transduction
rationale: Both children concern receptor-driven phosphorylation cascades (insulin/glucose signalling; RTK signalling), and the direct member protein autophosphorylation is a core step shared by these receptor kinases, so an umbrella covering receptor-triggered phosphorylation signalling fits without over-generalising to all phosphorylation.

name: Cholesterol and lipid response and regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Regulation of sterol and lipid metabolism' which also covers cholesterol biosynthesis regulation; this theme uniquely includes response-to-sterol/lipid processes alongside broader lipid regulation.

name: Postsynaptic structural organization and plasticity
rationale: Covers the child (glutamatergic synaptic plasticity) plus direct members on maintaining postsynaptic specialization, receptor trapping/localization, and actin organization beneath the postsynaptic density; broader than the child alone but restricted to postsynaptic structure and its regulation, excluding presynaptic or unrelated processes.

name: Glycan and glycolipid biosynthesis and degradation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader galactose metabolism scope) and from sibling (glycan/galactose metabolism without glycolipids); no collision detected.

name: Cardiac action potential repolarization
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifically refers to repolarization phase, not general electrophysiology or excitability.

name: Somitogenesis and paraxial mesoderm segmentation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Gastrulation and embryonic axis patterning', which also covers gastrulation and axis patterning; the revised name emphasizes the somite/paraxial mesoderm segmentation focus unique to this theme's members.

name: Angiotensin II receptor signaling
rationale: Overlaps with both parent themes (blood pressure regulation, renin-angiotensin system); narrowing to the specific receptor-mediated signaling cascade distinguishes it from siblings focused on contraction and ion/water balance.

name: Angiotensin signalling and blood pressure control
rationale: Covers the renin-angiotensin child plus direct members on angiotensin signaling/response and systemic blood pressure regulation, without invoking mechanisms like ACE2 or aldosterone not general to all members.

name: Leukocyte effector immunity and degranulation
rationale: No siblings present and name is distinct from both parents, describing leukocyte effector immunity and degranulation rather than receptor signalling or phagocyte function specifically.

name: Canonical Wnt destruction complex regulation
rationale: Nearly duplicates parent 'Wnt/beta-catenin destruction complex signalling'; revised to emphasize regulation of the destruction complex components, distinguishing from sibling 'Wnt and Hedgehog signalling' which lacks destruction complex members.

name: Viral protein synthesis, assembly and release
rationale: Members focus on translation, genome replication, assembly and virion release, not entry; 'entry' overlaps with the sibling 'Viral entry and coronavirus host interactions', and 'host infection' overlaps with 'Viral infection and host defence'.

name: T-helper cell differentiation and activation
rationale: Repeats parent's core meaning; renamed to reflect actual members which span multiple T-helper subsets rather than being CD4-specific.

name: GABA and neuroactive amino acid metabolism
rationale: Name largely repeated the parent phrase; narrowing to specify GABA and neuroactive amino acids distinguishes it as a specific subset of the broader biogenic solute transport/metabolism parent category.

name: Cardiovascular structure formation and morphogenesis
rationale: Both children concern shaping cardiac and vascular tissue during development, and the direct members (tube development; anatomical structure formation involved in morphogenesis) generalise this to structure-building morphogenetic processes that underlie the cardiac/vascular specifics without invoking other organ systems.

name: Cardiac conduction system electrical propagation
rationale: All members concern impulse propagation between conduction system cell types (atrial, AV node, His bundle, Purkinje) or the ion channel/junctional machinery that sets action potential shape and heart rate along this pathway.

name: Glycan, glycolipid and galactose metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parents (sphingolipid/glycosphingolipid, glycosaminoglycan disorders) and siblings (glycoprotein/glycosaminoglycan, polyol/pentose); no collision detected.

name: TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD signalling regulation
rationale: All three concern TGF-beta superfamily receptor serine/threonine kinase signalling and its SMAD-centred regulation, including the antagonists and inhibitory SMADs that tune it.

name: TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD signalling regulation
rationale: All three concern the TGF-beta superfamily receptor serine/threonine kinase system and its SMAD signal transduction, with strong emphasis on the negative regulators and antagonists that tune signal strength and duration.

With a single child theme (cytokine signalling) alongside monocyte-marker modules that are not truly generalized by it, any umbrella term either collapses to the child's own name or becomes a vacuous 'immune cell biology' label.

name: Beta cell differentiation and maturation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Pancreatic beta cell identity and insulin secretion'; narrowed to developmental differentiation/maturation processes distinct from identity/secretion function.

name: Beta-cell glucose sensing and mass regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Pancreatic beta cell identity and insulin secretion' and repeated parent's 'glucose homeostasis'; narrowed to glucose sensing and cell mass regulation, distinct from insulin secretion topics.

name: Sensory stimulus transduction channels
rationale: All members involve ion channels or receptors that convert mechanical, thermal, acid, or other stimuli into electrical signals underlying sensory perception, including pain, touch, and pH sensing.

name: Ion channel-mediated pH and mechanical sensing
rationale: Broad 'Sensory transduction channels' would also describe the sibling 'Sensory transduction across modalities'; the members are specifically about ion channels and pH/mechanical stimulus detection, which separates it from the broader cross-modality sibling.

name: Ribonucleotide and deoxyribonucleotide interconversion
rationale: Name already in use elsewhere; members center on ribonucleoside/deoxyribonucleoside mono-, di-, triphosphate metabolism and catabolism, distinguishing it from the sibling's broader nucleotide/phosphate biosynthesis.

name: Mitochondrial amino acid and carbon metabolism
rationale: Name adds carbon metabolism scope beyond parent's amino acid metabolism, distinguishing it; no siblings to collide with.

name: Type I interferon induction and signaling regulation
rationale: The original name overlapped with sibling 'Cytosolic pathogen sensing and antimicrobial response', which shares type I interferon production and its negative regulation; also TLR3 signaling in this theme isn't strictly cytosolic sensing, so the name is revised to emphasize interferon induction and downstream signaling regulation.

name: Smooth muscle cell phenotypic plasticity
rationale: All members concern the switch between contractile and synthetic/proliferative/migratory smooth muscle states, its regulation, and vascular remodelling consequences; 'smooth muscle adaptation' (0.43) fits the same phenotype-switching theme.

name: Glycogen metabolism and storage disorders
rationale: Covers the child (inherited glycogen storage diseases) plus direct members on energy reserve/glucan metabolism and glycogenolysis, all centred on glycogen synthesis and breakdown.

name: Mechanical and pH sensory transduction
rationale: Not a duplicate, but 'Sensory transduction' is broad enough to also describe the sibling 'Taste perception and transduction' (taste is a sensory perception/transduction process); narrowing to mechanical and pH stimuli distinguishes it from taste-specific perception.

name: Specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator biosynthesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (receptor signal transduction) and sibling (prostaglandin/eicosanoid signalling); specifically refers to resolvin/protectin/lipoxin biosynthesis.

name: Specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator biosynthesis
rationale: All five pathways describe synthesis of omega-3/arachidonic acid-derived pro-resolving mediators (resolvins, protectins, maresins, lipoxins) from various fatty acid substrates including DHA, EPA and DPAn-3, sharing the same lipoxygenase/COX chemistry and resolution function.

name: Developmental signalling pathways
rationale: Covers both children (Notch, Wnt and Hedgehog signalling) plus the inner ear differentiation member, which depends on these same developmental signalling cascades; broader than any single pathway but not extended to unrelated cell biology.

name: Triglyceride storage and lipolysis
rationale: All members concern synthesis, storage, mobilisation or lysosomal breakdown of triglyceride/lipid droplets in adipocytes and related metabolic tissues, including insulin-driven glucose uptake feeding this same fat-storage economy.

name: Synaptic transmission via neurotransmitter release and receptor signalling
rationale: Both children and all representative members concern presynaptic neurotransmitter release/transport and postsynaptic receptor trafficking/signalling, together spanning the full synaptic transmission cycle without extending to other neuronal processes.

name: Mitophagy and pexophagy
rationale: All members describe selective autophagic clearance of mitochondria or peroxisomes and its regulation via ubiquitin-dependent receptor tagging.

name: CCR7-dependent dendritic cell trafficking and survival
rationale: All three pathways converge on the CCL19/CCL21-CCR7 axis controlling dendritic cell chemotaxis to lymph nodes, the downstream phospholipase C/PKC signalling it engages, and the survival signalling that keeps migrating dendritic cells alive.

name: Cyclin-CDK activity control
rationale: Repeated broader parent scope of 'phase transitions'/'checkpoint surveillance'; renamed to specify the regulatory mechanism (cyclin-CDK complexes) distinguishing it from parents.

name: Hormonal cAMP/PKA control of energy metabolism
rationale: No sibling collisions and name is more specific than parent, describing the hormonal cAMP/PKA mechanism distinctly.

name: B cell identity and humoral immune response
rationale: The child covers B lymphocyte development and humoral immunity broadly; the direct members add B cell gene-expression signatures and positive regulation of humoral response, all centering on B cell identity/function and humoral immunity, so the parent extends only slightly beyond the child to capture these expression modules and regulatory member.

name: Post-recombination gap-filling synthesis
rationale: Too close to sibling 'Coordinated replication-repair synthesis' and parent themes; narrowed to specify the gap-filling/restart synthesis step following strand invasion.

name: Cranial and pharyngeal organ development
rationale: All members are morphogenesis programmes for organs derived from pharyngeal arches, cranial placodes or the gut tube head-region, including cranial nerves, inner ear structures, thyroid, face and digestive system, sharing conserved patterning cues rather than a single organ system.

name: Cranial and pharyngeal organ morphogenesis
rationale: All strong members (facial nerve, thyroid, semicircular canal x2, face development, and vestibulocochlear nerve at 0.62) concern development of cranial/pharyngeal-arch-derived structures—nerves, ear, thyroid, face—patterned by shared hindbrain/pharyngeal cues. Digestive system development (0.38) is excluded as it falls below threshold and does not share this cranial/pharyngeal focus.

name: Global genome NER pathway
rationale: Repeats parent name 'Nucleotide excision repair'; narrowed to a specific NER subpathway distinguishing it from the broader DNA damage repair pathways sibling.

name: Global genome and TC-NER pathway
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to reflect the GG-NER dual incision mechanism while remaining distinct from the broader 'DNA damage repair' sibling.

name: Vitamin and coenzyme cofactor metabolism
rationale: Overlapped closely with sibling 'Micronutrient metabolism and transport'; narrowed to vitamins and coenzyme-type cofactors specifically to distinguish it.

name: General mitotic cell cycle regulation
rationale: Overlaps siblings 'G1/S and G2/M checkpoint control' and 'Cell cycle phase transitions and checkpoints', which both cover checkpoints and progression more specifically; this theme's members are broader, generic cell cycle terms rather than specific checkpoint transitions.

name: Gap junction and electrical coupling
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no collision with parent (root) or siblings.

name: Amino sugar and sialic acid catabolism
rationale: Most members (N-acetylneuraminate catabolism, amino sugar catabolic process, glucosamine-containing compound catabolic process, sialic acid metabolism) converge on breakdown/salvage of amino sugars and sialic acid feeding glycolysis. Lysosome and N-glycan elongation members overlap only partially with this theme via shared enzymes (hydrolases, sialyltransferases), and carbohydrate phosphorylation is included at borderline strength as an entry step; these are noted as weaker fits.

name: Photoreceptor structural biogenesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (phototransduction signaling) and sibling (phototransduction cascade); this theme covers structural biogenesis, a different aspect.

name: Behavioral neural circuits
rationale: Both children concern neural circuitry underlying behavior (general behavior circuits and locomotor/exploratory ones); no direct members exist to add scope beyond this union.

name: Phase I/II drug metabolism enzymes
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Xenobiotic metabolism and transport' which shares Drug ADME and general xenobiotic metabolism; this theme's members specifically describe conjugation and oxidation enzyme reactions (methylation, acetylation, CYP, FMO, TPMT), distinguishing it by enzymatic mechanism rather than general metabolism/transport.

name: HIV replication and host restriction
rationale: Combines the child theme of viral replication/assembly/egress with direct members on HIV-specific steps (reverse transcription, Vpr functions, virion assembly) and host suppression of viral transcription/processes; captures both the viral replication cycle and host countermeasures without over-generalizing to all viruses.

name: Muscle growth and hypertrophy regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Muscle contraction and sarcomere biology' on the contraction aspect; narrowed to the growth/hypertrophy regulation focus of this theme.

name: Apical polarity and microvillus morphogenesis
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no overlap with apical/microvillus morphogenesis terms.

name: Xenobiotic and steroid metabolism and conjugation
rationale: The child covers xenobiotic and steroid metabolism broadly; the direct members add glycine-conjugation reactions and alcohol catabolism, both detoxification/excretion chemistry of xenobiotics and endogenous metabolites, so 'conjugation' extends the umbrella just enough beyond the child's scope.

name: Chamber septation and valve formation
rationale: Name was broader than its parent 'Cardiac looping and chamber formation', which is not allowed; narrowed to a specific downstream process consistent with that parent.

name: Forebrain and cerebellar neurodevelopment
rationale: All core members (telencephalon, hippocampus, cerebellar granular layer development, CNS neuron differentiation) describe patterning, progenitor specification, migration and circuit assembly in forebrain and cerebellar regions; the weakly included subpallium development (0.41) fits within forebrain patterning as well.

name: Glycolysis and redox cofactor metabolism
rationale: All members involve glycolytic enzymes and/or the NAD(P)H redox cofactors that couple to glucose flux, oxygen sensing and energy metabolism, spanning glycolysis itself, its regulators, and cofactor regeneration/catabolism, with oxygen transport included via its tie to hypoxia and glycolytic switching.

name: APC/C-mediated mitotic exit
rationale: Distinct from both parents (SAC regulation, mitotic organelle partitioning) and siblings (general division, spindle/kinetochore checkpoint) as it specifically names the APC/C-driven exit from mitosis.

name: APC/C-mediated mitotic exit and cell cycle proteolysis
rationale: All five members concern regulation and activity of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome and its ubiquitin-dependent degradation of mitotic substrates (cyclins, securin) via CDC20/FZR1 and UBE2C/UBE2S, controlling mitotic exit and checkpoint restraint.

name: TNF-NF-kB signalling and death receptor regulation
rationale: The child covers TNF/NF-kB signalling; direct members add regulation of MAPK activity and death-receptor-linked apoptosis pathways (Fas, activation-induced cell death) that intersect with this same signalling network, so the umbrella extends to death-receptor and MAPK crosstalk without broadening into unrelated signalling.

name: Kidney and nephron morphogenesis
rationale: All three children (nephron/tubule development, nephron/kidney development, nephron/collecting duct morphogenesis) concern the developmental building of kidney structures; with no direct members, the parent is simply the union of these developmental programmes.

name: GPCR second-messenger signalling and behavioural response
rationale: Covers the child's neuromodulatory GPCR pathways plus the direct members involving cAMP-coupled serotonin receptor signalling, amine responses and locomotor behaviour, all downstream of GPCR-mediated signal transduction.

name: Insulin biosynthesis and secretion
rationale: Distinct from parent and all siblings; no other theme covers insulin production and release specifically.

name: Photoreceptor cell development and homeostasis
rationale: Collides with an identically named theme elsewhere; revised to emphasize cell-type development and homeostasis, distinct from the phototransduction sibling.

name: Growth hormone and stress-axis hormonal signalling
rationale: Both children cover hormonal control of growth and stress axes (GH/IGF1, HPA); the FOXO member links metabolic/stress-responsive transcription downstream of these same hormonal axes, so no broader term than 'hormonal signalling of growth and stress' is needed.

name: Viral replication and assembly
rationale: Too close to parent's broad scope and overlaps with sibling 'Host-virus molecular conflict'; narrowing to replication/assembly stages of the viral life cycle distinguishes it.

name: Sphingolipid and complex fatty acid metabolism
rationale: Union covers the child's long-chain/ether lipid metabolism plus sphingomyelin biosynthesis and sphingolipid metabolism; the ARCI5 member (0.33) reflects defective ceramide/lipid processing and fits under this umbrella without broadening it further.

name: Glomerular capillary development and filtration
rationale: Distinct from all sibling themes; no collision with parent (root) or siblings.

name: Amino acid biosynthesis and degradation
rationale: Repeated both parents' combined scope (transport + metabolism) and overlapped with sibling 'Amino acid and GABA membrane transport'; narrowed to the metabolic (non-transport) aspect.

name: Golgi-derived vesicle transport
rationale: Child covers post-Golgi trafficking to endosomes/lysosomes while direct members add Golgi-to-plasma-membrane transport and COPII/general vesicle targeting from the Golgi/ER, so the unifying scope is vesicle transport originating at the Golgi to its various destinations.

name: Branching morphogenesis of epithelial organs
rationale: Four members at full inclusion describe bud elongation, terminal-unit bifurcation, proliferation driving salivary branching, and regulation of epithelial morphogenesis, all centered on reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal branching. The weakly included ectodermal cell differentiation (0.39) is excluded as it concerns broader epidermal fate specification rather than branching.

name: Purine and nucleoside salvage and catabolism
rationale: Name specifies purine/nucleoside salvage and catabolism, distinct from parent's broader biosynthesis-focused scope and siblings covering biosynthesis or general metabolism.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation fidelity
rationale: Both children govern distinct mechanisms ensuring accurate chromosome segregation during mitosis—kinetochore-microtubule attachment and chromosome condensation—without repeating either child's specific mechanism.

name: Cell cycle progression and DNA repair
rationale: The 'germline division' portion doesn't match its own members (no meiosis/gametogenesis genes) and instead overlaps with the sibling 'Gametogenesis and reproductive development'; narrowed to reflect actual members: cell division, mitotic cycle, DNA repair, recombination.

name: Bile acid and fat-soluble vitamin metabolism
rationale: Distinct from parent (excludes alcohol metabolism) and from sibling (excludes alcohol, includes vitamins), so no collision.

name: Peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism and biogenesis
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling; parent covers peroxisomal plus isoprenoid lipid metabolism broadly, sibling covers isoprenoid/sterol lipids, while this theme specifically addresses peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism and organelle biogenesis.

name: Purine catabolism
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Purine and nucleoside salvage and catabolism' and overlapped with sibling 'Purine and nucleoside salvage'; narrowing to the catabolic (breakdown) aspect distinguishes it from the salvage-focused sibling.

name: Post-translational modification and localization control
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no parent to collide with.

name: Cytoskeletal control of mitotic spindle and cell polarity
rationale: No parent to collide with, and distinct from siblings like Cortical actin and septin dynamics in cell division and migration and Small GTPase cycle regulation, since it specifically covers cytoskeletal regulation of spindle formation and cell polarity.

name: tRNA and rRNA modification and processing
rationale: The current name claims a mitochondrial scope that the members (rRNA/tRNA/snRNA processing and modification) do not support, and it overlaps with the sibling 'Mitochondrial gene expression and genome maintenance' which is the true mitochondrial theme.

name: Mitochondrial apoptosis and its regulation
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than the parent by naming the mitochondrial pathway.

name: Muscle contraction and calcium regulation
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere; revised to reflect the combination of muscle contraction processes with calcium ion homeostasis found in its members, distinguishing it from siblings focused on calcineurin signalling.

name: Nucleotide and mismatch excision repair
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; members center on nucleotide-excision, mismatch, and cross-link repair pathways, distinguishing from general DNA repair.

name: Beta-catenin destruction complex in Wnt signaling
rationale: Distinct from parent 'Wnt pathway components' (more specific complex) and sibling 'Wnt/beta-catenin signaling' (a pathway, not a complex); no collision.

name: Humoral innate defence effectors
rationale: Name is distinct from both parents and siblings; no collision.

name: Translation elongation and quality control
rationale: Original name duplicated the parent's scope and also described the sibling's initiation-focused members; the revised name emphasizes elongation, aminoacylation, and ribosome rescue steps that distinguish it from the initiation-machinery sibling.

name: Lymphocyte activation and differentiation
rationale: All members describe T or B cell receptor signalling, costimulation, developmental differentiation, or the resulting activation/memory/death programmes that shape adaptive lymphocyte responses.

name: Chylomicron and VLDL particle metabolism
rationale: Near-duplicate of sibling 'Triglyceride and lipoprotein metabolism', which also covers HDL clearance; this theme's members are specifically chylomicron and VLDL assembly/remodeling/clearance, which distinguishes it.

name: Regulation of transcription factor DNA binding activity
rationale: No parent to repeat, and no sibling names overlap with transcription factor DNA binding regulation.

name: Antigen presentation and T cell recognition
rationale: No siblings present and the name is more specific than the parent, adding T cell recognition aspect.

name: Pre-rRNA processing and modification
rationale: Repeated scope with parent 'Ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing' and overlapped with sibling covering transcription/assembly; narrowed to processing/modification steps specifically.

name: RNA polymerase I and III rRNA transcription
rationale: Parent 'rRNA synthesis and modification' is broad; specifying the polymerase-mediated transcription step distinguishes this theme from other rRNA processing/modification aspects.

name: Nuclear transport and mitotic division
rationale: Covers the nuclear pore/envelope child plus direct members on cell division, organelle inheritance, and SUMOylation of nuclear/mitotic regulators; broader than the single child but still specific to nuclear-envelope-linked mitotic processes rather than generic 'cell processes'.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase and downstream signalling
rationale: Both children concern RTK activation and its growth-factor signalling outputs; representative members (phosphorylation, ERBB2-EGFR, PI3K/AKT) are downstream kinase cascades of the same RTK-driven system, so the union is RTK signalling plus its immediate effector pathways rather than kinase signalling in general.

name: mRNA metabolism
rationale: Repeated 'Ribosome biogenesis' from the parent; the distinguishing content is mRNA metabolism, which also separates it from the sibling's surveillance focus.

name: Dolichol-linked glycosylation defects
rationale: All members concern synthesis or use of dolichol/dolichyl-phosphate-linked intermediates required for N-glycosylation and related pathways, or the congenital disorders of glycosylation caused by their loss.

name: Glutamate-driven regulation of dendritic spine plasticity
rationale: Repeats parent theme almost verbatim and overlaps both siblings' generic structural plasticity framing; own members are distinguished by glutamate/NMDA receptor signaling driving dendritic spine and postsynaptic actin remodeling.

name: Cytosolic protein translation
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Mitochondrial and cytosolic protein synthesis' and parent's scope; renamed to specify cytosolic-only translation, distinguishing from mitochondrial-specific sibling.

name: Positive regulation of lipid biosynthesis
rationale: Name does not repeat either parent and there are no siblings to collide with; it clearly denotes biosynthesis regulation distinct from sterol sensing and fasting-induced lipolysis/ketogenesis.

name: Innate inflammatory cytokine receptor pathways
rationale: Overlapped heavily with siblings 'Cytokine-driven innate inflammatory response' and 'Innate pattern recognition and cytokine-driven inflammation'; narrowed to focus on receptor-level cytokine signaling specifically.

name: p53-mediated apoptosis pathways
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'p53-driven senescence and apoptotic pathways' by repeating both apoptosis and stress response concepts; narrowed to focus on apoptotic function only, distinguishing it from sibling 'Cellular senescence'.

name: Branched-chain amino acid catabolism and lipoylation disorders
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Amino acid metabolism and catabolism' which covers general amino acid catabolic processes; this theme's members are specifically about branched-chain amino acid (MSUD, 3-MCC deficiency) and protein lipoylation defects, which is more specific and distinguishes it.

name: Hydrogen peroxide handling in thyroid and antioxidant defence
rationale: Most members converge on hydrogen peroxide/oxidant chemistry linked to thyroid hormone synthesis (thyroxine biosynthesis, DUOX maturation, deiodinases via selenocysteine/selenide metabolism) and antioxidant/detoxification responses (ascorbate, lactone, symbiont response). The weakly included modified amino acid catabolic process (0.33) is excluded as it does not fit this redox/thyroid axis.

name: Apical cell-cell junction organization
rationale: No siblings and name is more specific than parent, clearly distinguishing apical junction organization from general junction assembly regulatory proteins.

name: Cell-cell junction assembly and organization
rationale: All members describe the formation and maintenance of epithelial/endothelial junctional complexes (tight, adherens, desmosomal) that establish polarity and barrier function.

name: Cell-matrix adhesion and epidermal migration
rationale: Unites the child's cell-matrix adhesion/lamellipodial dynamics with the direct members, all concerning keratinocyte spreading and migration during wound healing, which depend on regulated cell-matrix adhesion.

name: Bile acid receptor-mediated homeostasis
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Bile acid and alcohol biosynthesis' and 'Bile acid and fat-soluble vitamin metabolism'; narrowing to receptor-mediated regulatory feedback distinguishes it from the biosynthesis-focused parent.

name: Bile acid synthesis and signalling
rationale: All core members (1.00) concern bile acid metabolism, secretion, receptor signalling, or transcriptional control of bile acid homeostasis; the two weaker members (Endogenous sterols 0.64, Metabolism of steroids 0.54) are broader sterol/steroid pathways included largely for their bile acid synthesis and FXR feedback content.

name: Lipoprotein assembly and remodeling
rationale: No bile acid metabolism among own members despite name mentioning it; also 'dietary lipid' overlaps broadly with sibling 'Whole-body lipid and energy homeostasis' which also deals with lipoprotein particles.

name: Mitochondrial quality control
rationale: Covers both children: mitophagy (clearance of damaged mitochondria) and mitochondrial dynamics/protein import (fission-fusion and biogenesis machinery that maintains a functional organelle pool); no direct members extend this scope.

name: Cell-cell junction organization and assembly
rationale: Duplicated parent 'Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesion' concept and members don't specifically reference cadherin mechanism, unlike sibling which is explicitly about CDH1/E-cadherin regulation.

name: Gametogenesis and gonadal development
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Meiotic progression and gonadal maturation' and sibling 'Meiotic chromosome and spindle dynamics' via shared meiotic terminology; renamed to emphasize gonadal/gamete developmental scope distinct from meiotic mechanics and ovulatory signalling.

name: Synaptic vesicle recycling and neurotransmitter release
rationale: Overlapped with several sibling vesicle-trafficking themes (Vesicular membrane trafficking, Golgi-derived vesicle transport, Endomembrane vesicular trafficking and secretion); narrowed to the synaptic-specific recycling and release process distinguishing it from generic vesicle trafficking siblings.

name: Steroid hormone receptor transcriptional regulation
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent, which concerns pubertal changes broadly while this theme addresses receptor transcriptional mechanisms specifically.

name: Steroid hormone receptor signalling regulation
rationale: All members concern transcriptional control of nuclear steroid hormone receptors (general, androgen-specific, or estrogen-specific) via coactivator/corepressor complexes.

name: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remodeling and lipolysis
rationale: Covers the child (chylomicron/TRL remodeling and clearance) plus direct members on VLDL/TRL particle remodeling regulation and the LPL/LIPC lipase machinery driving it, and extends to plasma lipoprotein remodeling generally (weak, 0.43) without invoking specific downstream fates like cholesterol transport.

name: Chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation in skeletogenesis
rationale: Covers the child's endochondral cartilage-to-bone programme plus the direct members: RUNX2 regulation and cartilage morphogenesis (both integral to chondrocyte/hypertrophy control) and osteoblast differentiation regulation, extending the theme beyond cartilage alone to the coupled bone-forming lineage.

name: Plasma cell antibody secretion
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'B cell antibody diversification and humoral response' and parent's humoral immunity term; narrowed to plasma cell effector function distinct from diversification/development siblings.

name: Glycoprotein and proteoglycan glycosylation
rationale: Repeats parent's nucleotide-sugar/amino sugar theme; more specifically this theme covers protein glycosylation and glycoconjugate synthesis, distinct from carbohydrate metabolism disorder siblings.

name: Spindle midzone and contractile ring assembly
rationale: Nearly identical to sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinetic machinery'; renamed to emphasize the specific midzone/contractile ring assembly processes distinguishing it.

name: B lymphocyte developmental stages
