rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'B cell antibody diversification and humoral response' on antibody diversification; narrowed to the developmental progression aspect unique to this theme.

name: Endothelial regulation of leukocyte trafficking
rationale: Covers both children: adhesion-molecule/extravasation control governing leukocyte-endothelial adhesion, and shear-stress-driven endothelial programmes that also set the vessel's anti-adhesive tone; no direct members extend beyond this endothelial-leukocyte interface.

name: TAK1-dependent MAPK and NF-kB activation
rationale: All members involve TRAF6/TAK1-driven signalling from innate immune receptors or growth factor pathways that activates MAPK cascades (ERK, JNK, p38) and/or NF-kB.

name: Isoprenoid and complex lipid biosynthesis
rationale: Union covers sterol (cholesterol) and isoprenoid (geranylgeranyl diphosphate, DHDDS/dolichol) synthesis plus sphingolipid/complex fatty acid metabolism and related fatty acid oxidation (alpha-oxidation, inclusion 0.33 kept as it fits the fatty-acid arm); 'lipid metabolism' alone would be too broad, but this phrase captures both the isoprenoid and complex-lipid biosynthetic threads uniting children and direct members.

name: NOD-like and endosomal TLR signaling with peptide transport
rationale: Combines the endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLR child with NOD1/NLRP signaling regulation and the peptide/dipeptide transporters (SLC15 family) that deliver ligands to these innate sensors; a broader term like 'innate immune signalling' would lose the specific transport component.

name: ER stress and unfolded protein response
rationale: Repeated the parent name exactly, giving no distinguishing information; however, since there are no siblings and no stated collision, minimal specificity change needed—retaining focus on IRE1/PERK regulation would help, but as no collision or sibling overlap exists, keep unchanged.

name: p53-mediated cell cycle checkpoint control
rationale: Core members (G1/S checkpoint signaling, G1 phase, Mitotic G1 phase/G1/S transition, TP53 degradation regulation, COP1 autodegradation, Cdc25A degradation, TP53 G2 arrest transcription) all converge on p53 stabilization and CDK/cyclin checkpoint regulation governing G1/S and G2/M transitions. Weakly included generic cell cycle regulation terms (mitotic cell cycle regulation, G2M checkpoint hallmark, GTSE1 role) are broader or peripheral but consistent with this axis.

name: Intestinal protein and carbohydrate digestion
rationale: Repeated both parent themes' scope; narrowing to protein and carbohydrate digestion distinguishes it from the lipid-focused parent and the sugar transport parent, as well as the hexose transport sibling.

name: Xenobiotic biotransformation, conjugation and transport
rationale: Name is distinct from parent themes and sibling; covers phase I/II xenobiotic metabolism plus transport, not repeated or confusable.

name: CD4 T cell priming and costimulation
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'T-helper 1/2 differentiation and response' and 'T cell activation and differentiation'; narrowing to priming/costimulatory events distinguishes it from lineage-specific differentiation covered by those siblings.

name: Calcium-calcineurin signalling in muscle hypertrophy
rationale: Both children concern calcineurin/calcium-driven signalling underlying cardiac or muscle hypertrophic adaptation, and the representative members (stress hypertrophy, muscle adaptation, IGF-1R regulation) all feed into that same calcium/calcineurin-linked hypertrophic growth axis; no direct members push the scope beyond muscle growth regulation.

name: NF-kB and JNK signal regulation
rationale: Children cover activation and negative regulation of NF-kappaB pathway components alongside positive regulation of the JNK cascade, both being stress/inflammatory signal transduction cascades regulated by shared upstream receptors and adaptors; a narrower term would exclude one branch.

name: Lipid and energy substrate homeostasis
rationale: The child covers lipid/cholesterol regulation broadly; direct members add triglyceride storage and nutrient storage regulation, extending the umbrella beyond lipids to general fuel/nutrient homeostasis while still centered on lipid/energy substrates.

name: Epithelial growth and morphogenesis regulation
rationale: All three concern regulatory control of epithelial cell behaviour—maturation, proliferation, and shape change—during development and tissue renewal.

name: Mesoderm subdivision and patterning
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Germ layer patterning' and sibling 'Gastrulation and germ layer patterning'; narrowed to focus specifically on mesoderm subdivision, distinguishing it from the broader germ layer processes.

name: MTOR pathway in starvation response
rationale: Nearly identical to parent name 'TOR/mTOR nutrient signaling in starvation response', giving no added specificity; retains core content (mTOR/TOR signaling and starvation response) true to members.

name: Glycosaminoglycan metabolic disorders
rationale: Name was broader than parent's specific ECM glycosaminoglycan focus and overlapped with siblings' scope; narrowed to disorders arising from glycosaminoglycan metabolism specifically.

name: Mitochondrial dynamics and quality control
rationale: Covers both children's fusion/fission/homeostasis and quality-control machinery plus the direct member organelle fusion, without narrowing to either child's specific scope.

name: Incretin and ion channel regulation of insulin secretion
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Regulated hormone secretion and beta cell function' which also covers insulin secretion broadly; this name is narrowed to the incretin/GLP1 and ABCC8 channel mechanisms actually present in the members, distinguishing it from the broader hormone-secretion/beta-cell-function sibling.

name: Interferon antiviral response
rationale: Name is distinct from parent, specifying interferon-mediated mechanism within the broader antiviral innate immune response; no siblings to conflict with.

name: Regulation of protein ubiquitination and turnover
rationale: Name is distinct from both parents (which focus on checkpoint regulation and broader protein stability/localisation) and siblings (replication licensing, genome maintenance, division machinery), with clear specificity to ubiquitination-mediated turnover.

name: TGF-beta family receptor signalling
rationale: Distinct from all listed siblings; no collision with parent since root has none.

name: Cellular cholesterol homeostasis
rationale: Both children concern how cells sense and manage cholesterol/sterol levels—via macrophage foam cell handling or general sterol response and biosynthesis regulation—with no direct members extending beyond this.

name: Non-canonical NF-kB signaling
rationale: Non-canonical NF-kB signaling is distinct from parent and sibling; it specifically refers to the NIK/IKKα-RelB/p52 pathway, unlike canonical TNF/NF-kappaB signalling.

name: Macrophage TLR-driven inflammatory activation and its negative regulation
rationale: No siblings and the name already integrates both parent concepts with added specificity (negative regulation), so it remains distinct.

name: Macrophage activation and TLR signalling regulation
rationale: All members concern macrophage/microglial activation and the TLR2/LPS signalling pathways (and their negative regulators) that drive innate inflammatory responses.

name: Incretin and channel regulation of beta cell secretion
rationale: Sibling 'Insulin biosynthesis and secretion' shares identical core members (insulin secretion, regulation of hormone/insulin secretion), making the current name indistinguishable; this theme's distinct content is incretin signaling and ion channel defects (GLP1, ABCC8), which the revised name captures.

name: Nuclear mRNP export and quality control
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'mRNA and protein quality surveillance'; narrowed to nuclear export/quality checkpoint of ribonucleoprotein particles, distinguishing it from ribosome biogenesis and rRNA processing siblings.

name: Nuclear mRNA export
rationale: All three pathways concern nucleocytoplasmic export machinery centered on mRNA, including nuclear pore/NXF1-NXT1-mediated transcript export and its regulation; the third broadens to nuclear export generally but is dominated by the same mRNA export factors.

name: Rho GTPase-mediated stress fiber formation
rationale: Overlaps with parent 'Rho GTPase cytoskeletal signalling' and sibling's actin focus; narrowed to a specific actin remodelling output (stress fibers) distinct from membrane ruffling/macropinocytosis sibling.

name: Dolichol-linked glycosylation and GPI anchor biosynthesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader glycan/glycolipid biosynthesis and degradation) and sibling (glycan metabolism and lysosomal catabolism); already specific to dolichol-linked glycosylation and GPI anchor biosynthesis.

name: Protein hydroxylation and histidine/EEF2 modification
rationale: Four members (1.00,1.00,1.00) concern amino-acid side-chain hydroxylation or diphthamide/histidine modification of EEF2 and actin, all installed by dedicated post-translational modifying enzymes acting on translation-related and structural proteins; the weakly included Protein methylation member (0.53) is broader and covers many non-histone substrates beyond this scope, but shares the theme of enzymatic side-chain modification tuning protein/translation function, so it is loosely covered by the general framing.

name: Neural tube patterning and neuronal fate specification
rationale: Both children and representative members (cell fate determination, dorsal spinal cord development, motor neuron differentiation) concern regional patterning of the developing CNS and the transcriptional commitment of neural progenitors to specific fates, a broader frame than either child alone but still specific to neural tube/CNS regionalisation and neurogenesis.

name: Regulation of presynaptic neurotransmitter secretion
rationale: The current name overlaps heavily with sibling 'Synaptic neurotransmitter release and signalling', which shares the same core members (neurotransmitter transport, uptake regulation); this revision emphasizes the regulatory/modulatory aspect (glutamate secretion regulation, uptake regulation, presynaptic modulation) that distinguishes this theme.

name: Heme and porphyrin metabolism with manganese transport
rationale: The copper-ion homeostasis members are shared verbatim with sibling 'Trace metal ion transport and homeostasis', so the name must instead emphasize the heme/porphyrin and manganese-specific members that distinguish this theme.

name: Axon and dendrite outgrowth
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than both parents by naming the actual structures (axons/dendrites) undergoing outgrowth.

name: Regulation of neuron projection extension
rationale: Repeats parent's core meaning (neurite outgrowth and extension); revised to be more specific to the actual members, which focus on projection/axon extension and cell growth extent.

name: Neurotransmitter uptake and short-term synaptic plasticity
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Presynaptic neurotransmitter release and its regulation', which shares the same core transport/secretion members; this theme's distinct members involve uptake regulation and short-term potentiation.

name: FGFR-mediated PLC-gamma signalling
rationale: Distinguishes from sibling 'FGFR signalling' and parent's PI3K/RAS-MAPK branches by specifying the PLC-gamma arm of FGFR pathway activity.

name: Oxidative and chemical stress response with ferroptosis regulation
rationale: Covers the child's antioxidant defence, the broader chemical stress response, and the ferroptosis/anti-ferroptosis members, all united by redox/iron-driven cell stress and death regulation.

name: Immune cell activation and tolerance regulation
rationale: The child covers inhibitory regulation of NK/T cytotoxicity, while direct members add broader monocyte/B/T immunoregulation, NK activation control, and allograft rejection—together spanning the balance between lymphocyte/myeloid activation and restraint that governs tolerance versus rejection.

name: Osmotic and mechanical stress response
rationale: Covers the child (ion/osmotic homeostasis), plus direct members on mechanical stimulus response and sodium-coupled phosphate transport, unifying osmotic/ionic and mechanosensory adaptation without repeating the child name.

name: Neutrophil population control and inflammatory resolution
rationale: All members concern the size and turnover of the neutrophil/myeloid compartment: homeostasis, apoptosis regulation (positive and negative), and restraint of IL-8-driven recruitment, with the neutrophil-enriched signature (0.46, weakest) reflecting the same cell-intrinsic machinery for recruitment and clearance.

name: Phosphorylation-driven inflammatory signalling
rationale: Covers the non-canonical NF-kB/TNF child, the protein phosphorylation regulation child (serine/threonine kinase cascades), and the direct cytokine-mediated signaling member, all converging on kinase-driven inflammatory and cytokine signal transduction; broader terms like 'signal transduction' alone would lose the phosphorylation/inflammatory specificity shared across all members.

name: Sialic acid catabolism
rationale: Repeated the parent's 'glycan catabolism' scope; narrowing to sialic acid specifically distinguishes it from the parent's broader glycan scope and from the sibling nucleotide sugar metabolism theme.

name: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein assembly and transport
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and name is more specific than parent by specifying triglyceride-rich lipoprotein assembly and transport rather than general dietary lipid absorption.

name: Cytosolic pattern recognition and inflammasome-driven inflammation
rationale: All members concern cytosolic detection of microbial/danger signals (PRR signaling, AIM2 inflammasome regulation, IL-18 maturation) or the lytic/antimicrobial effector output of that response (cytolysis). The weakly included 'positive regulation of response to external stimulus' (0.48) is broader but its listed components overlap the same PRR-inflammasome axis.

name: Meiotic chromosome segregation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation' on mitotic content; narrowing to meiotic-specific segregation distinguishes it.

name: Aromatic and sulfur amino acid catabolism
rationale: The name 'Amino acid catabolism' is broad enough to also describe the sibling 'Aromatic and non-proteinogenic amino acid catabolism'; the members show this theme uniquely combines aromatic amino acid and sulfur compound metabolism.

name: Phosphoinositide and phosphatase signalling
rationale: No parent to repeat; distinct from the sibling 'Inositol phosphate metabolism and signalling' since it covers phosphoinositide lipid and phosphatase signalling rather than inositol phosphate metabolism.

name: cAMP effector signalling
rationale: Parent 'cAMP metabolism enzymes' concerns synthesis/degradation enzymes; renamed to clarify this theme covers downstream signalling effectors rather than metabolic enzymes.

name: Ubiquitin-mediated protein quality control
rationale: Repeats parent's scope ('ERAD and neddylation-mediated quality control'); revised name better reflects the dominant ubiquitination-related members while remaining true to the whole set, no siblings to check.

name: Extracellular matrix remodelling in vessels
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Vascular remodeling in wound healing' and sibling 'Vascular wall and endothelial homeostasis'; specifying ECM remodelling distinguishes it from homeostasis-focused sibling.

name: Mineralization of bone and teeth
rationale: Core members (0.94-1.00) cover regulation of bone, tooth, cementum and odontoblast mineralization/differentiation. Phosphate homeostasis and the two phosphate-transporter pathways (0.29-0.57) support this by supplying the ion balance needed for mineralization but are weakly included and excluded from the name's specificity claim.

name: Lipid metabolism in neurodegeneration and atherosclerosis
rationale: Name is already distinct from parent and all listed siblings, which cover different metabolic domains (ion transport, nucleotides, vitamins, etc.).

name: VEGF signalling in lymphatic development
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'VEGF-driven vascular growth' on the vascular aspect; narrowed to the lymphatic-specific focus.

name: VEGF signalling and lymphatic vessel development
rationale: All members concern VEGF ligand-receptor signalling in endothelial cells and its role in specifying lymphatic vessel growth, spanning ligand binding, neuropilin co-receptor tuning, and downstream lymphangiogenic development.

name: Serotonergic modulation of behavior circuits
rationale: Name overlapped conceptually with parent's monoamine focus and didn't distinguish from dopaminergic siblings; narrowing to serotonergic signaling separates it clearly.

name: TLR3/TLR4-mediated IRF3 activation
rationale: Distinguishes from sibling 'Type I interferon production and signalling' by specifying the TLR-specific upstream sensing mechanism rather than downstream IFN effects, and narrows from broad antiviral/antibacterial framing to the specific TLR3/TLR4-IRF3 axis.

name: Fasting energy metabolism
rationale: Covers both children (fatty acid oxidation/ketone body metabolism and fasting fuel metabolism) plus direct members like glycerol, acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate handling and ketone regulation, all converging on fuel mobilization and interconversion during fasting; broader terms like general metabolism would be unwarranted.

name: Non-sulfur amino acid metabolism
rationale: Identical to sibling 'Amino acid metabolism' and overlapping with 'Nitrogen and amino acid metabolism'; specifying non-sulfur distinguishes it from the sulfur amino acid parent and siblings.

name: ERBB2/EGFR and TGF-beta signalling in cancer
rationale: Covers both children—ERBB2-EGFR receptor signalling and TGF-beta/SMAD tumour suppressor signalling with its loss in cancer—with no direct members to extend beyond them.

name: Photoreceptor development and maintenance
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'Photoreceptor and sensory receptor biology' which shares retina homeostasis and photoreceptor cell morphogenesis members; needs to be distinguished by emphasizing developmental/maintenance processes specific to this theme's members.

name: IgE and Fc receptor-mediated allergic effector responses
rationale: Name is specific and distinct from parent, no siblings to collide with.

name: Immune cell adhesion and tissue homeostasis
rationale: Union covers leukocyte-endothelial and platelet/integrin adhesion, immune cell differentiation and inflammatory signalling, plus direct members on wound healing, cell fate/number homeostasis and hematopoietic stem cell maintenance, tying cell adhesion processes to tissue-level cellular homeostasis.

name: Apical microvillus assembly and polarized epithelial trafficking
rationale: All members concern building or regulating the apical brush border (microvillus assembly, its positive/general regulation) and the polarized sorting of proteins to apical or basolateral membrane domains (raft targeting, basolateral secretion, apical surface proteome), converging on epithelial apical-basal polarity and surface architecture.

name: Synaptic transmission and plasticity
rationale: No siblings, and the name is distinct from the parent (mechanism of vesicle fusion/exocytosis vs. the broader synaptic transmission/plasticity process it enables).

name: Vesicle coat and tethering machinery for secretory transport
rationale: Core members (vesicle targeting, protein secretion, COPII transport at 1.00) all concern coat, tether and SNARE machinery moving cargo through the early secretory pathway (ER-Golgi-surface); COPI retrograde traffic and endosomal transport, both below 0.5, are excluded as they describe reverse or endosomal routes rather than the shared secretory-export machinery.

name: Ribosome biogenesis and translation
rationale: Repeats parent theme wording ('gene expression machinery'); more specific to ribosome/rRNA/tRNA processing and translation, distinguishing it from the sibling's protein hydroxylation/EEF2 modification focus.

name: De novo nucleotide biosynthesis
rationale: Repeated the parent name and overlapped with sibling's salvage/catabolism scope; renamed to specify de novo synthesis pathways.

name: Intracellular carbohydrate transport and metabolism
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Carbohydrate and glycoconjugate metabolism in the extracellular matrix'; narrowed to intracellular/cellular processes to distinguish from extracellular matrix focus.

name: Postsynaptic receptor and structural maintenance
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'Dendritic spine and synapse structural plasticity'; distinguishing feature is postsynaptic receptor localization and NMDA-related maintenance rather than general dendritic/filopodium morphogenesis.

name: Xenobiotic and drug biotransformation
rationale: All three concern the metabolic conversion (phase I/II) and transport of drugs and foreign compounds for clearance.

name: Ephrin and Roundabout guidance signaling
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Axon guidance and neurite outgrowth control', which shares axon guidance and cell projection regulation themes; renaming to specific receptor pathways (ephrin, Roundabout) distinguishes it.

name: Heart chamber and atrial development
rationale: Overlapped both parent 'Heart morphogenesis and chamber formation' and sibling 'Cardiac septation and valve morphogenesis' via shared septum/morphogenesis language; members emphasize whole-heart and chamber/atrial development distinct from the sibling's valve/septation focus.

name: DNA replication and repair synthesis
rationale: Covers translesion synthesis (child) plus initiation, flap removal, and repair-associated synthesis (direct members), all steps of copying or restoring DNA during replication/repair; narrower terms like 'translesion synthesis' would exclude initiation and flap processing.

name: Platelet-fibrin clot formation
rationale: Repeated the parent 'Coagulation cascade regulation' scope and overlapped with sibling 'Thrombin generation and signalling'; narrowed to focus on clot formation processes distinct from thrombin signalling.

name: PLK1-regulated spindle and centrosome dynamics
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; revised to reflect PLK1 regulation and centrosome-related members distinguishing it from siblings focused on kinetochore attachment and cytokinesis.

name: Regulation of protease activity
rationale: Repeats parent's 'regulated proteolysis' concept; renamed to specify regulation targets protease activity rather than duplicating parent scope, though no siblings force differentiation.

name: Chromosome segregation and cytokinesis
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cell division', which also covers chromosome segregation/spindle-kinetochore attachment; renaming to emphasize chromosome separation and cytokinesis distinguishes it from spindle organization/assembly focus of the sibling.

name: Sister chromatid cohesion and chromatin organization
rationale: Combines the child's chromosome condensation/cohesion focus with direct members on cohesion establishment/maintenance and broader chromatin organization and protein-chromatin localization, requiring a slightly wider umbrella than the child alone.

name: Coagulation cascade and hemostasis
rationale: Its own members are dominated by coagulation factors and hemostasis pathways, not cell adhesion; 'cell adhesion' duplicates the sibling theme 'Platelet-associated cell adhesion signalling', which explicitly covers cell adhesion regulation.

name: Receptor endocytic trafficking and signal attenuation
rationale: Distinct from siblings; specifically about receptor internalization for signal termination, unlike general vesicular/Golgi/endosomal trafficking siblings.

name: Proteasomal and ERAD-mediated degradation
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent name 'Protein quality control and turnover'; members are specifically proteasome/ERAD-related, distinguishing it from the folding/chaperone sibling.

name: Regional brain patterning outcomes
rationale: Repeated the parent's 'patterning outcomes' phrasing without distinguishing scope; renamed to specify brain regional identity as the distinguishing focus.

name: Mitochondrial redox and ROS balance
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitochondrial respiratory chain and its regulation'; narrowed to focus on redox/ROS balance rather than respiratory chain machinery itself.

name: Nuclear-encoded mitochondrial gene expression genes
rationale: Overlaps parent name and sibling; needs to distinguish nuclear-encoded components regulating mitochondrial gene expression machinery from the sibling's focus on mitochondrial-encoded gene expression and tRNA maturation.

name: Coagulation factor activation cascade
rationale: Too close to parent 'Coagulation factor activation'; needs specificity showing it covers the sequential cascade of factor activation steps rather than a single activation event.

name: Cardiac and tubular organ morphogenesis
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Cardiovascular and tubular organ morphogenesis'; narrowed to focus on cardiac chamber and tube-organ developmental processes rather than general morphogenesis.

name: DNA double-strand break and mismatch repair
rationale: Covers homologous recombination repair of double-strand breaks, mismatch repair and its defective variants (MSH2, BRCA1), the two main repair processes represented; broader terms like 'DNA repair' would be unnecessarily vague.

name: Spindle assembly checkpoint regulation
rationale: Repeated parent 'Chromosome segregation in mitosis' and overlapped with sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation and cell cycle control'; narrowed to the checkpoint mechanism controlling segregation fidelity.

name: Complement activation and regulation
rationale: Distinct enough from siblings but the theme is really about complement cascade, so specifying that gives more precision without overlapping 'Neutrophil and phagocyte antimicrobial killing' which shares the antibacterial humoral response members.

name: Phosphate group metabolism in lipids and signalling
rationale: Union covers phosphoinositide/phosphatase regulation, phospholipid metabolism, and the broader direct member 'phosphorus metabolic process', all centered on addition/removal of phosphate groups in lipid and signalling contexts; broader terms like general nucleotide phosphorylation are excluded since children focus on lipid/phosphatase biology.

name: Hexose and monosaccharide transport
rationale: Distinct from parents and siblings; siblings cover digestion, glycerol, polyol/pentose, and dietary sugar/glycogen metabolism while this theme specifically covers hexose/monosaccharide transport.

name: Hexose transporter function and disorders
rationale: Repeated parent name 'Hexose and monosaccharide transmembrane transport'; revised to emphasize transporter-specific function and disease relevance without duplicating parent phrasing.

name: Macrophage activation and cytokine production
rationale: Unites the child theme of macrophage activation/TLR regulation with direct members on macrophage and myeloid cytokine output, without broadening to inflammation generally.

name: Histone and DNA marks in imprinting
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Epigenetic regulation of chromatin and imprinting'; narrowed to specify the actual molecular marks (histone/DNA modifications) rather than general regulation.

name: Skeletal muscle development and regeneration
rationale: All members concern proliferation, differentiation, fusion, or regenerative maintenance of skeletal (and related striated) muscle cells, with no direct members outside these processes.

name: RTK family signaling: ERBB, FGFR, ALK, IGF1R
rationale: The name overlapped heavily with the parent 'Growth factor receptor signalling and oncogenic mutants'; the specific receptor tyrosine kinase families present in the members distinguish it from the parent and from the sibling's phosphorylation-regulation focus.

name: B cell receptor and differentiation
rationale: Overlaps with parent's focus on plasma cell antibody secretion; renamed to specify B cell receptor signaling and differentiation stages, distinguishing it from downstream antibody secretion by plasma cells.

name: Arachidonic acid eicosanoid biosynthesis
rationale: Nearly repeats parent 'Prostaglandin and eicosanoid signalling'; renamed to emphasize biosynthesis of arachidonic acid-derived eicosanoids, distinguishing it from parent's signalling scope.

name: Craniofacial and ocular organogenesis
rationale: No siblings present, and the name is more specific than the parent (craniofacial/ocular vs. skeletal/craniofacial/appendage), so it is already distinct.

name: Bile acid metabolism and vitamin D regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Steroid hormone and sterol metabolism', which already covers steroid hormone/sterol metabolism; narrowing to bile acid and vitamin D distinguishes this theme, consistent with its bile acid signaling and CYP27B1/CYP24A1 members.

name: Non-interferon cytokine receptor signalling
rationale: Repeated the parent scope; parent covers interferon and JAK-STAT signaling, so this needs to clarify it is the broader cytokine receptor family distinct from interferon-specific signaling.

name: Epidermal and hair cycle differentiation
rationale: Too closely echoed the parent name 'Epidermal and appendage differentiation'; the members include molting/anagen hair cycle phases and keratinization distinct from the sibling's collagen matrix assembly theme.

name: mRNA stability and turnover
rationale: Covers the child (deadenylation/decapping decay) plus direct members on 3'-UTR-mediated mRNA stabilization and miRNA-mediated catabolism, all converging on control of mRNA half-life rather than a specific decay mechanism.

name: Platelet activation and coagulation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader category) and sibling (specific factor deficiencies); this theme covers platelet function and clotting cascade activation, not a repeat of either.

name: Trace metal ion homeostasis
rationale: Covers copper homeostasis/detoxification (child) plus manganese transport and response, and host metal ion assimilation; all concern regulation and acquisition of transition metal ions, broader than copper alone but not general 'metabolism'.

name: Lymphocyte chemotaxis and migration regulation
rationale: All three pathways concern chemokine-driven control of lymphocyte and T cell movement, adhesion, and trafficking through tissues and lymphoid organs.

name: Vesicular trafficking and lysosomal degradation
rationale: Covers the child (endomembrane trafficking/lysosomal degradation) plus the direct members: membrane docking, extracellular vesicle biogenesis, and prevention of phagosome-lysosome fusion all concern vesicle-mediated transport and its regulation of degradative fusion.

name: Reproductive developmental processes
rationale: Repeats the parent name 'Gametogenesis and germline meiosis'; the members emphasize broader reproductive developmental and regulatory processes rather than meiotic recombination, distinguishing it from the sibling.

name: Mitochondrial fission and fusion
rationale: Overlapped with parent's scope and 'turnover' duplicated sibling Mitophagy pathways; narrowed to the fission/fusion dynamics distinct from mitophagy.

name: Adipocyte differentiation and fat mass regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent and all siblings; no collision with adipocyte/fat mass focus.

name: Hexose transport and glycogen storage disorders
rationale: Overlaps parent's scope broadly; members center on hexose/glucose transport and glycogen storage disease rather than general carbohydrate metabolism, distinguishing it from the galactose/pentose sibling.

name: B cell differentiation and receptor diversification
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent name's 'B cell...humoral immune response' phrasing; members focus on developmental stages and receptor diversification/isotype switching, which better distinguishes it from the parent's broader identity/response framing.

name: Cell division and meiotic cytokinesis
rationale: Highly overlaps with sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation and cytokinesis' and 'Mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation', which share chromosome segregation and cytokinesis themes; the distinguishing members here are cell division, Rho GTPase cycle, and meiotic-specific processes.

name: Forebrain and cerebellar neuronal differentiation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Regional patterning and differentiation of the developing CNS', which also covers dorsal spinal cord and motor neuron patterning; revised to specify the forebrain/cerebellar structures and neuron differentiation unique to this theme's members.

name: DNA damage response pathways
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'DNA repair and chromosome segregation' and sibling 'Telomere and chromosome maintenance'; narrowed to focus on damage-response signaling distinct from telomere maintenance and segregation mechanics.

name: Cardiac and skeletal muscle cell development
rationale: Sibling's members (heart morphogenesis, outflow tract morphogenesis, valve development) also fall under 'Heart development'; this theme is actually about muscle/cardiac cell differentiation, which the new name specifies.

name: Nucleotide-sugar interconversion and amino sugar catabolism
rationale: 'Sugar metabolism and interconversion' is broad enough to also describe the sibling 'Sugar and amino sugar metabolism', which shares amino sugar catabolic process and general sugar metabolism; the revised name emphasizes the nucleotide-sugar biosynthesis/interconversion focus (nucleotide-sugar, GDP-mannose, GDP-fucose, UDP-N-acetylglucosamine) that distinguishes this theme.

name: Ionotropic receptor activity and clustering
rationale: The generic phrase 'synaptic transmission' overlaps with the sibling 'Neurotransmitter release and synaptic transmission'; the members here specifically concern ionotropic receptor (GABA, AMPA, kainate) activation and clustering, distinguishing it from the release/transport-focused sibling.

name: Lipid and energy metabolic homeostasis
rationale: Covers bile acid, dietary lipid, triglyceride, ketone and digestive processes that together regulate whole-body fuel and lipid balance, broader than any single child but excluding unrelated biology like signalling unrelated to metabolism.

name: EGFR and MET driven PI3K/AKT signalling
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'RTK signalling via PI3K/AKT axis' and to sibling 'Receptor tyrosine kinase signalling'; specifying the receptor family distinguishes it.

name: Peroxisomal protein targeting and turnover
rationale: Covers the peroxisomal import/biogenesis child plus direct members: general protein targeting and membrane docking (both exemplified here by peroxisomal machinery) and pexophagy, the turnover route for the organelle; broader than the child alone but still anchored to peroxisome-related trafficking rather than all protein sorting.

name: Lipid droplet biogenesis and turnover
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and it is more specific than the parent by covering biogenesis and turnover processes distinctly.

name: Adipocyte lipid storage
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically about adipocyte-based lipid storage, not overlapping with bile acid, cholesterol/HDL, dietary absorption, ketone regulation, or general triglyceride/phospholipid storage themes.

Methylation covers a broad enzymatic chemistry across DNA, RNA, protein and small molecules, while MITF-M target gene programmes are melanocyte-specific transcriptional outputs; the only umbrella covering both would be a vacuous term like 'gene regulation' that fails to exclude most of biology.

Hippo pathway regulation and ERK/MAPK cascade regulation are two distinct signalling systems with no shared biology beyond both being kinase cascades controlling growth, so no single tight name covers all members.

name: Chromatin organization and genomic imprinting
rationale: Repeats parent 'Epigenetic and chromatin regulation'; members center on chromatin structure, imprinting, and histone demethylation rather than protein methylation broadly, distinguishing it from the sibling on transcription/RNA processing machinery.

name: Muscle and vascular contractile physiology
rationale: Distinct from siblings like vascular tone/injury response, muscle growth/regeneration, and cardiac muscle proliferation themes, which each cover narrower aspects; this theme's focus on contractile physiology of both muscle and vasculature is not repeated elsewhere.

name: Anterior neuroectoderm and body axis patterning
rationale: Union covers whole-embryo axis/germ-layer establishment (child) plus regional subdivision of the neural plate into forebrain, midbrain-hindbrain and posterior domains (direct members), so the parent must span both early axis formation and neural regional patterning without narrowing to either alone.

name: Epithelial cell-cell adhesion and EMT
rationale: Covers cadherin/junction-based adhesion (both children) plus the direct member epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, which represents loss of that same adhesion; tighter umbrellas like 'cell-cell adhesion junctions' alone would exclude the EMT member.

name: Aggrephagy and stress granule clearance
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than its parent, naming the specific mechanism (aggrephagy and stress granule clearance) within the broader quality control theme.

name: Cell cycle checkpoint control
rationale: Overlaps parent 'Chromosome segregation in mitosis' and sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation control'; narrowing to checkpoint regulation distinguishes it.

name: Nuclear pore complex-mediated transport and envelope reassembly
rationale: Excluding the weakly included NPIP locus group (0.33), all members concern trafficking through the nuclear pore complex (protein export, viral PIC import, IP3/IP4 transport) or reconstruction of the nuclear envelope and its pores after mitosis.

name: Synaptic receptor trafficking and signaling
rationale: Covers the child (synaptic transmission and receptor assembly) plus direct members on receptor diffusion trapping and AMPA glutamate signaling; the mRNA A-to-I editing member is unrelated but weakly included (0.33) and is treated as an outlier not driving the name.

name: TOR/mTOR nutrient signaling in starvation response
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Integrated stress response...' which also covers stress/starvation response members; narrowed to TOR/mTOR nutrient-sensing pathway specifics that are this theme's distinguishing content.

name: Water homeostasis and osmoregulation
rationale: All members concern water balance: renal water reabsorption via vasopressin/aquaporin signalling, intracellular water/osmotic homeostasis, and aquaporin-mediated water transport; regulation of body fluid levels is included as it centers on the same renal water/fluid balance machinery despite broader secondary detail.

name: Death receptor-induced caspase-8 activation
rationale: All four members concern extrinsic apoptotic signalling through death receptors (FAS, TRAIL-R, TNFR) assembling FADD/caspase-8 complexes, including its inhibition and diversion to necroptosis.

name: Ketone body and gluconeogenic precursor metabolism
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Fatty acid oxidation and ketone body metabolism' since both contain fatty acid oxidation and ketone body metabolism members; this theme's distinct members (oxaloacetate, glycerol, alditol, alanine) point to gluconeogenic precursor metabolism rather than fatty acid oxidation.

name: Glycogen storage and galactose metabolism disorders
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Carbohydrate metabolism and transport disorders' which shares glucan metabolic process and general carbohydrate metabolism disease scope; this theme's members are specifically glycogen storage diseases and galactose metabolism defects.

name: Non-canonical NF-kappaB signalling
rationale: All members concern activation or regulation of the NIK/IKK-alpha/p100-p52 non-canonical NF-kappaB branch.

name: Spindle positioning and centrosome organization
rationale: Members cover spindle assembly, spindle/MTOC positioning, cortical anchoring of positioning complexes, and centrosome maturation/protein localization to the cytoskeleton, all converging on spindle orientation and centrosome-based organization; the weakly included regulation of centriole elongation (0.38) is excluded as it concerns centriole length control rather than positioning.

name: Bone matrix glycosylation
rationale: Overlapped with siblings 'Phosphate homeostasis and biomineralization' and 'Skeletal tissue development and mineralization' on the mineralization aspect; narrowed to the distinguishing glycosylation component of bone matrix.

name: Stem and progenitor cell differentiation
rationale: No parent to collide with; closest sibling 'Regulation of progenitor proliferation and self-renewal' addresses proliferation control rather than differentiation, so the name remains distinct.

name: Xenobiotic, steroid and amine clearance
rationale: Both children concern conjugation/catabolism and transport of small molecules for excretion (xenobiotics/steroids and biogenic amines), and the direct member oxalate transport fits the broader theme of small-solute clearance/transport, so 'clearance' covers all without over-specifying mechanism.

name: GPCR-linked eicosanoid signal transduction
rationale: Nearly duplicates parent name; narrowing to receptor-level signal transduction distinguishes it from sibling focused on mediator synthesis/metabolism.

name: Cell fate commitment
rationale: Covers both children (mesoderm and embryonic cell fate commitment) and representative members like somitogenesis and cell fate determination, all concerned with lineage commitment during development, without restating either child's specific scope.

name: Ubiquitin ligase activation and chromatin protein turnover
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader degradation process) and sibling (chain conjugation/removal); this theme specifically covers ligase activation and chromatin protein turnover.

name: General hematopoietic and leukocyte lineage commitment
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Hematopoietic differentiation and homeostasis' and overlapped with 'Myeloid and megakaryocyte differentiation' and 'Lymphocyte and monocyte/dendritic immune cell identity'; narrowed to broad lineage commitment processes distinct from those specific lineage or homeostatic siblings.

name: Centromeric sister chromatid cohesion maintenance
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader structural maintenance) and sibling (condensation regulation); no collision.

name: NK and gamma-delta T cell cytotoxicity
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader) and sibling (NK cell cytotoxicity alone vs NK plus gamma-delta T cells here); no collision.

name: Viral entry and virion assembly
rationale: Distinct from parent (assembly-specific replication processes vs entry/virion assembly) and from sibling (virus-host interactions is a broader interface concept), so no collision exists.

name: HIV Nef-mediated immune receptor downregulation
rationale: All three pathways describe Nef stripping surface immune receptors (MHC class I, CD4, CD8) via clathrin adaptor-mediated endocytosis to evade immune surveillance.

name: Epidermal differentiation and appendage keratinization
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader architecture/homeostasis) and sibling (adhesion); no collision.

name: BCL-2 family regulation of intrinsic apoptosis
rationale: Repeats parent 'Intrinsic apoptotic signalling'/'Regulation of mitochondrial intrinsic apoptosis' without adding distinction; members center on BH3-only/BCL-2 regulation, which better specifies the theme.

name: Methylation
rationale: No parent to collide with, and 'Methylation' is clearly distinct from 'MITF-M target gene programmes'.

name: Vascular and lymphatic endothelial growth regulation
rationale: Name is distinct from parents (which focus on shear/hypoxia response mechanisms) and sibling (wound repair specific remodelling); this theme covers general vascular/lymphatic growth regulation.

name: Chondroitin and hyaluronan biosynthesis disorders
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Glycosaminoglycan metabolism and associated disease' and echoed the parent's broad GAG scope; narrowing to chondroitin/dermatan and hyaluronan biosynthesis matches its actual members (DS-GAG biosynthesis, hyaluronan metabolism, CHSY1/SLC26A2/SLC2A10 defects).

name: Myeloid and megakaryocyte differentiation
rationale: Distinct from siblings and parents; specifically names myeloid/megakaryocyte lineage differentiation, unlike general lineage commitment or monocyte/neutrophil biology siblings.

name: Host-virus interaction and immune evasion
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Nucleic acid sensing and antiviral defence' via 'antiviral defence'; narrowed to focus on host-virus interplay/evasion distinct from sibling's sensing/interferon signalling focus.

name: Neurite and cell shape morphogenesis
rationale: Distinct from siblings like neuronal development, gliogenesis, and cytoskeletal regulation themes; no parent to collide with.

name: p53-mediated cell cycle arrest
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'p53-driven senescence and apoptosis' and 'Genome stability and cell division control'; narrowing to cell cycle arrest specifically distinguishes it from p53's apoptotic/senescence functions and from general genome stability.

name: Myosin light chain phosphorylation control
rationale: Repeats parent 'Cross-bridge cycling regulation' scope and overlaps sibling 'Muscle contraction regulation'; narrowed to the specific smooth muscle regulatory mechanism via MLC phosphorylation/calcium-calmodulin-MLCK signaling.

name: Amino sugar and GPI anchor metabolism
rationale: The sibling 'Sugar metabolism and Golgi processing' lists the exact same top members (UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis, nucleotide-sugar metabolism, N-acetylneuraminate catabolism), so the original name equally describes it; narrowing to amino sugar catabolism and GPI anchor metabolism, which are unique to this theme, separates them.

name: Cholesterol and lipoprotein homeostasis
rationale: Repeats parent's broad scope ('whole-body energy homeostasis'); members focus on cholesterol/lipoprotein regulation, distinguishing from bile acid and dietary lipid siblings.

name: Mitochondrial amino acid and nucleobase catabolism to citric acid cycle intermediates
rationale: No siblings present and name is distinct from both parents, providing specific detail about mitochondrial localization and TCA intermediate products not mentioned in either parent.

name: Endoderm-derived organ morphogenetic patterning
rationale: Overlaps heavily with siblings 'Endoderm organ development and epithelial specification', 'Endoderm-derived epithelial organ development', and 'Endoderm lineage specification and derivative development'; narrowed to emphasize morphogenetic patterning specifically.

name: tRNA pseudouridylation and turnover regulation
rationale: Repeats parent theme name 'tRNA modification and processing' nearly verbatim; new name reflects specific members (pseudouridine synthesis, tRNA turnover regulation) distinguishing it from the parent and from the sibling's snoRNP/snRNA focus.

name: Skeletal, craniofacial and appendage morphogenesis
rationale: Distinct from all siblings including 'Skeletal tissue development and mineralization' and 'Embryonic axial patterning'; no overlap with a parent since it is a root.

name: Skeletal tissue mineralization and development
rationale: Union covers cartilage/bone cell differentiation, mineralization regulation, and matrix secretion underlying skeletal and dental tissue formation, broader than either child but excluding unrelated processes.

name: Dietary lipid absorption and lipoprotein assembly
rationale: Name is distinct from parents and sibling; covers dietary lipid absorption and chylomicron/lipoprotein assembly, unlike sibling's HDL remodeling focus.

name: Mesodermal cell fate commitment and specification
rationale: All three members concern the signalling (WNT/BMP/FGF/NODAL) and transcriptional control (MESP1, SOX17, NuRD) governing commitment/specification of mesodermal fate during gastrulation.

name: Regulation of angiogenesis and endothelial proliferation
rationale: Six of seven members directly concern control (positive or negative) of vascular/endothelial cell proliferation and vessel growth (angiogenesis, vasculature development, wound-healing angiogenesis); the hallmark angiogenesis set fits directly. The weakly included 'cellular response to endogenous stimulus' (0.52) and 'positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation' (0.91) are broader but still touch growth-factor-driven proliferation overlapping with this vascular theme, so are covered loosely rather than excluded.

name: Ketone body and acyl-CoA metabolism
rationale: The 'fasting' framing is not supported by all members and no other theme uses this name, but it should be more specific to the ketone body/acyl-CoA focus rather than broad 'central carbon' metabolism, which risks overlap with 'Glycolysis and pyruvate/NAD(P)H cofactor metabolism' and 'Nucleotide, phosphate and central carbon metabolism'.

name: Spindle microtubule and cytokinetic apparatus assembly
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Mitotic spindle and cytokinetic ring organization'; revised to emphasize assembly of the physical machinery components rather than ring organization.

name: Homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks
rationale: Distinct from parent 'Strand invasion intermediate repair' and sibling 'DNA repair'; already specific enough.

name: Homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks
rationale: All members concern homologous recombination repair machinery (resection, RAD51 loading, strand exchange) or its defects, plus alt-NHEJ as a backup route used when HRR fails.

name: DNA replication elongation
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'DNA replication and repair synthesis'; narrowed to the elongation phase of replication to distinguish from repair synthesis and licensing parents.

name: Nucleotide metabolism disorders
rationale: Overlapped with siblings covering nucleotide metabolism/transport; this theme is specifically about inherited disorders of nucleotide metabolism, distinguishing it from the transport- and energy-focused siblings.

name: Hormone-driven puberty and sexual maturation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Gametogenesis and reproductive development'; narrowed to focus on hormonal control of pubertal maturation rather than gametogenesis itself.

name: Arp2/3-mediated actin nucleation and lamellipodium formation
rationale: No siblings present, and the name is distinct from and more specific than the parent, which covers macropinocytosis broadly; this theme specifically addresses Arp2/3-mediated nucleation and lamellipodia.

name: Calcium sensitivity of contractile filaments
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Excitation-contraction coupling' (calcium/contraction) and 'Calcium-dependent muscle growth regulation'; narrowed to filament-level calcium sensitivity distinct from calcium release coupling and growth signaling.

name: Somatic hypermutation and antibody effector functions
rationale: Overlapped with both siblings ('antibody diversification' matches one, 'humoral response' matches the other); narrowed to specific mechanisms not covered by either sibling.

name: Postsynaptic receptor signaling transmission
rationale: Overlaps with siblings 'Presynaptic neurotransmitter release and transport/reuptake' which already cover release; this theme should be distinguished by focusing on postsynaptic transmission events.

name: Water and polyol channel transport
rationale: Covers the child (water homeostasis/osmoregulation) plus direct members on polyol and glycerol transmembrane transport, all mediated by aquaporin/aquaglyceroporin-type channels; mitochondrial uncoupling (0.27) is weakly included and not reflected in the name.

The two grouped btm modules are heterogeneous mixes of chromatin, mitotic, and metabolic proteins bound only by loose functional overlap, while the reactome item is a specific, mechanistically distinct SUMO conjugation step; no single description covers all three without becoming an uninformative catch-all.

name: Chemosensory and mechanosensory receptors
rationale: Repeated the parent's scope without adding specificity; renamed to mirror parent content directly since name added only vague 'biology' term with no distinguishing detail.

name: Endodermal epithelial differentiation
rationale: Most members describe transcription-factor-driven differentiation of gut, pancreatic and hepatic epithelium (intestinal epithelial maturation, HNF network, exocrine pancreas development, epithelial cell maturation, intestinal stem cell homeostasis, and the mislabeled 'leukocyte migration' entry which actually describes intestinal epithelial identity). The weakly included HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_DN (0.62) reflects loss of this same differentiated identity in cancer, fitting the theme's inverse.

name: Anteroposterior CNS regionalization and neuron specification
rationale: Overlaps heavily with sibling 'Neural tube dorsoventral patterning and regional neurogenesis', which also covers regional patterning and differentiation; the distinguishing feature of this theme's members is anteroposterior axis regionalization (forebrain, midbrain-hindbrain, posterior neural plate) and motor/dopaminergic neuron specification.

name: Sperm-egg fertilisation
rationale: Distinct from parent (which covers meiosis and fertilisation broadly) and sibling (gametogenesis and meiotic division); it specifically covers sperm-egg fusion.

name: Sperm-egg fertilisation
rationale: All members cover sperm's journey to and through the zona pellucida, acrosome reaction, motility regulation, and gamete fusion during fertilisation.

name: SLC-mediated amino acid transport disorders
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere and repeats parent theme; members include specific SLC transporter defects and transmembrane transport processes, distinguishing it from generic amino acid transport.

name: Renin-angiotensin blood pressure regulation
rationale: No siblings and name is distinct from parent, adding blood pressure regulation context not present in parent name.

name: Renin-angiotensin blood pressure regulation
rationale: All three pathways describe hormonal control of arterial pressure and blood volume via the renin-angiotensin(-aldosterone) axis and its chemical mediators.

name: Receptor tyrosine kinase endocytic attenuation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader trafficking/attenuation umbrella) and sibling (internalization/recycling/degradation mechanics); specifies RTK-specific endocytic attenuation of signaling.

name: Photoreceptor phototransduction biology
rationale: Repeats 'photoreceptor' from parent 'Photoreceptor and pigmentation biology' without distinguishing from the pigmentation half; narrowed to phototransduction mechanisms.

name: Coagulation factor deficiency disorders
rationale: Repeats parent's 'coagulation factor' scope without differentiation; revised to specify deficiency/defect disorders as distinct focus from the activation cascade mechanism itself.

name: Defective F8, F9, and VWF function
rationale: Repeated the parent theme name; members specifically involve F8, F9, and VWF defects, distinguishing from the sibling's broader coagulation cascade/hemostasis theme.

name: TNF and NF-kB signalling
rationale: Both children and the representative members concern TNF receptor family signalling and its NF-kB (canonical and non-canonical) branch points, including regulation and apoptotic outcomes; no direct members extend beyond this axis.

name: GPCR signalling in lipid mediator and nucleotide responses
rationale: No sibling collisions and name is more specific than parent, focusing on GPCR-mediated responses rather than general lipid mediator signalling and metabolism.

name: Regulation of calcium ion transmembrane transport
rationale: All three members concern the regulation (including positive regulation) of calcium entry/transport across membranes via channels, transporters and their regulators.

name: Centrosome and spindle positioning
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and distinct from both parents (chromosome segregation and midzone/contractile ring assembly).

name: Prostaglandin and endocannabinoid-related lipid metabolism
rationale: Bioactive lipid mediator metabolism is broad enough to also describe the sibling "Specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator biosynthesis", which also covers bioactive lipid mediator synthesis; the members here center on prostaglandins, N-acylethanolamines, and monoacylglycerols rather than SPM/protectin biosynthesis, which separates it.

name: Neutrophil degranulation and oxidative burst
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Neutrophil and phagocyte antimicrobial killing', which covers antimicrobial peptide-mediated killing; this theme's members specifically concern degranulation and respiratory burst/NADPH oxidase mechanisms, which distinguishes it.

name: Cyclic GMP-PKG signalling
rationale: Too similar to parent name 'Cyclic nucleotide second messenger signalling' and overlaps conceptually with sibling cAMP/PKA-CREB signalling; renaming to specify the cGMP/PKG branch distinguishes it.

name: Anteroposterior neural tube patterning
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Regional brain patterning outcomes'; specifying anteroposterior axis distinguishes it from the sibling's forebrain/cerebellar focus.

name: Photoreceptor ciliary trafficking and development
rationale: The child covers photoreceptor development/maintenance broadly, while the direct members add ciliary protein localization, centriole/cilium elongation, and VxPx-mediated cargo targeting to the cilium — all centered on ciliary trafficking supporting photoreceptor structure. The umbrella joins developmental maintenance with the ciliary transport machinery that underlies it.

name: Apical actin bundle assembly
rationale: The child covers cortical cytoskeleton and polarity broadly, while all direct members specifically concern microvillus/actin bundle assembly and its regulation; 'apical actin bundle assembly' generalises the child's cortical actin theme to include the microvillus-specific and general actin-bundling regulation members without invoking septins or unrelated cortex biology.

name: Nucleocytoplasmic export of RNA and protein cargo
rationale: No sibling conflicts and distinct from both parents, which focus on mRNP export/quality control and viral exploitation specifically.

name: Mitotic chromosome segregation and checkpoint control
rationale: All three concern kinetochore-spindle attachment, the spindle assembly checkpoint, and anaphase/chromosome segregation machinery; the DNA damage checkpoint arm in the second pathway is a minor extension of the same control logic.

name: Protein quality control and turnover
rationale: Covers both children (folding/chaperone quality control and degradation/quality control) plus the direct member on ribosome rescue, which addresses stalled translation as another quality-control checkpoint feeding into degradation.

name: Type 2 immune and hypersensitivity responses
rationale: Distinct from siblings like T-helper 1/2 differentiation (which focuses on lineage commitment) and other innate/adaptive signaling themes; this one specifically covers Type 2 effector and hypersensitivity biology, not overlapping in scope.

name: Peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'Peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism and biogenesis' and overlapped conceptually with sibling 'Peroxisome biogenesis and protein import'; renamed to specify the oxidative chain-shortening process distinct from biogenesis/import.

name: HDL particle biogenesis and remodeling
rationale: Duplicate name used elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to specifically reflect HDL assembly and remodeling processes, distinguishing it from siblings dealing with triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, chylomicron/VLDL assembly, and macrophage cholesterol handling.

name: Muscle cell differentiation and regeneration
rationale: Both children cover myogenic differentiation/regeneration and its regulation; there are no direct members, so the parent generalises only slightly by dropping the 'regulation of' qualifier to unify the two.

name: Polo-like kinase and p53-mediated cell cycle regulation
rationale: Both siblings' members (mitotic cell cycle, checkpoint control) show 'Cell cycle phase transitions and checkpoints' would equally describe them; this theme is distinguished by its specific Polo-like kinase and TP53-driven checkpoint mechanisms.

The unnamed child is a heterogeneous mix of chromatin/transcription, RNA processing, membrane trafficking and cytoskeletal regulators with no unifying biology beyond generic housekeeping, so any parent covering it plus ubiquitin-mediated degradation would be near-vacuous.

name: Redox and hypoxia-linked apoptotic regulation
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Mitochondrial membrane permeability and calcium dynamics in apoptosis', which also covers calcium/membrane permeability; revised to emphasize the distinct redox/ROS/RNS and hypoxia-driven regulation present in this theme's members.

name: DNA repair and chromosome segregation
rationale: Too broad and vague relative to parent's checkpoint focus; siblings are specific mechanisms, so renamed to specify the actual processes covered (DNA repair, chromosome segregation) rather than a generic umbrella term.

name: Spindle formation and cytokinesis
rationale: Nearly identical to parent name 'Mitotic spindle attachment and cytokinesis'; also overlapped sibling 'Mitotic chromosome segregation and checkpoint control' via shared chromosome separation members. Narrowed to spindle assembly and cytokinesis, excluding checkpoint/segregation focus.

name: Intestinal lipid digestion and absorption
rationale: Too broad relative to parent 'Dietary lipid absorption and lipoprotein metabolism'; narrowed to specify lipid focus, distinguishing it from sibling 'Plasma lipoprotein metabolism' which covers post-absorptive transport.

name: Digestion and absorption of dietary nutrients
rationale: Nearly repeated the parent name; members include hexose absorption and general digestion, not just lipid/cholesterol, so a broader nutrient-focused name distinguishes it from the parent.

name: Lipid and cholesterol homeostasis regulation
rationale: Both children plus representative direct members (ketone metabolism, foam cell differentiation, HDL clearance) all concern regulatory control of lipid or cholesterol levels and trafficking, uniting metabolic and transport regulation without invoking any specific mechanism absent from most members.

name: Meiotic division machinery
rationale: Repeats the parent 'Mitotic and meiotic division machinery' and overlaps with mitosis-focused siblings; if this theme actually covers meiosis-specific machinery, renaming clarifies that distinction.

name: Cardiac and skeletal muscle contraction regulation
rationale: Repeats parent 'Cross-bridge cycling regulation' scope and overlaps with sibling 'Smooth muscle contraction regulation'; narrowing to striated muscle distinguishes it.

name: Metanephric collecting duct and tubule development
rationale: All three concern development and morphogenesis of the metanephric kidney's collecting duct and tubule epithelium, driven by shared WNT/PAX/hedgehog patterning and PKD1/AQP2 functional markers.

name: NMDA and AMPA receptor plasticity signaling
rationale: Too similar in scope to parent 'Long-term potentiation signalling'; specifying NMDA/AMPA receptor mechanisms distinguishes it from the parent's broader LTP scope and from the sibling's structural focus.

name: cAMP/PKA-CREB signalling
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and sibling, specifying cAMP/PKA-CREB pathway rather than generic cyclic nucleotide signalling.

name: Synapse formation and structural maturation
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Axon and dendrite morphogenesis' and sibling 'Neurite growth'; narrowed to synaptic structure formation specifically, distinguishing from axon/dendrite outgrowth processes.

name: Mitochondrial dynamics and protein import
rationale: Covers the child (protein import/organization) plus direct members on fission, mitophagy regulation and RHOT1-mediated mitochondrial transport, all aspects of mitochondrial structural maintenance and turnover; excludes unrelated organelle biology.

name: Rho GTPase cytoskeletal signalling
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Small GTPase signal transduction' since Rho-family GTPases fall under 'small GTPases'; specifying Rho GTPase family clarifies distinction from the broader sibling.

name: Very long-chain fatty acid and isoprenoid metabolism
rationale: The name overstates peroxisomal catabolism generically which isn't a distinct sibling issue, but is too broad/vague; members are specifically VLCFA, isoprenoid/ether lipid, and sterol precursor pathways, distinguishing from 'Glycerolipid and phospholipid metabolism' and 'Steroid hormone and sterol metabolism' siblings.

name: Cardiac and skeletal muscle patterning
rationale: Repeats parent 'Cardiac and skeletal muscle growth regulation' scope and overlaps with sibling 'Muscle cell proliferation and differentiation'; narrowing to patterning/morphogenetic aspects distinguishes it from the growth-regulation and proliferation/differentiation themes.

name: Cardiac and skeletal muscle development
rationale: All members describe the developmental programme by which mesodermal progenitors commit to and differentiate into contractile muscle cells and tissues, spanning cardiac (all at 1.00) and broader muscle lineages (muscle cell/tissue/structure development, inclusion 0.76-0.89).

name: TOR pathway nutrient sensing
rationale: Overlapped heavily with siblings 'Cellular stress response' and 'Stress adaptation and nutrient sensing'; distinguishing feature is the TOR/MTOR signaling and translation regulation members.

name: RNA polymerase II transcription initiation and elongation
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader coupling process) and sibling (spliceosome/3' end formation); no collision.

name: RNA polymerase II pause release and elongation, including HIV Tat-dependent transcription
rationale: Name is unique and does not describe the sibling, which concerns termination and 3'-end processing rather than pause release/elongation and HIV Tat-dependent transcription.

name: Wnt/beta-catenin destruction complex signalling
rationale: Name duplicated elsewhere in the hierarchy; revised to reflect the specific focus on beta-catenin degradation and Wnt/Hedgehog crosstalk in these members, distinguishing it from the Notch sibling.

name: VEGF-driven angiogenesis and vascular repair
rationale: Repeated the parent's phrase 'Vascular and lymphatic development and repair' nearly verbatim; members are specifically VEGF signaling and angiogenesis/repair processes, distinguishing it from the sibling's broader vascular/lymphatic development focus.

name: Bile acid and cholesterol export
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Plasma lipoprotein remodeling and lipid absorption' in scope of plasma lipid metabolism; renamed to reflect the hepatic secretion/export processes distinguishing it from remodeling and absorption.

name: Skeletal and dental mineralization
rationale: Covers the child theme's skeletal/dental morphogenesis plus direct members on tooth mineralization, amelogenesis and matrix secretion supporting mineralization; broader than the child alone but still specific to hard-tissue mineral deposition rather than general development or ECM biology.

name: Lymphocyte cytotoxicity and antigen-driven activation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically covers cytotoxic and antigen-driven lymphocyte activation, unlike T cell activation/differentiation or lymphocyte effector regulation siblings.

name: COPI/COPII vesicle transport and secretion
rationale: Repeats parent's general theme and would describe sibling's vesicle-mediated transport members; own members are specifically about COPI/COPII coat-mediated transport and secretion pathways, distinguishing from vacuole/lysosome-specific sibling.

name: Nucleotide degradation and salvage
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Nucleotide, nucleoside and analogue metabolism'; narrowed to the degradation/salvage pathways distinct from that broader nucleoside/analogue focus.

name: Aromatic amino acid catabolism and sulfur metabolism
rationale: Sibling 'Amino acid metabolism and one-carbon biosynthesis' also involves amino acid catabolism (shares tryptophan/tyrosine catabolism); this theme is distinguished by aromatic amino acid catabolism and sulfur compound metabolism rather than generic amino acid catabolism.

name: Excision and mismatch repair pathways
rationale: Duplicate name in use elsewhere; also repeated the parent. This theme's members are specifically base-excision, nucleotide-excision, mismatch, and cross-link repair, unlike the sibling's strand-break and synthesis focus.

name: Actin-driven cell shape remodeling
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Neurite and cell shape morphogenesis' and sibling 'Neuronal projection outgrowth and regeneration'; narrowed to actin/cytoskeleton-based shaping distinct from projection outgrowth.

name: Chromatin and epigenetic regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; siblings focus on genome stability, p53-driven responses, and protein stability, while this theme uniquely covers chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms.

name: Serine/threonine kinase signalling
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Regulation of protein phosphorylation signalling', which also covers kinase regulation broadly; renamed to specify serine/threonine kinase and PI3K/AKT/mTOR focus of its members.

name: Aldosterone-mediated sodium and water regulation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'fluid balance'; narrowed to the specific hormone-driven ion/water mechanism, distinguishing it from the angiotensin signalling sibling.

name: Neural circuitry of behaviour and reward
rationale: Covers both children (neuromodulatory behavioural regulation and drug/reward responses) plus the BDNF-TRKB signalling member, which supports neuronal/synaptic plasticity underlying behavioural and reward circuits.

name: Nuclear RNA export and surveillance
rationale: Covers nuclear mRNA export (child), the direct member mRNA export from nucleus, NMD as a coupled surveillance mechanism, and ribosomal subunit export as a related nuclear-to-cytoplasm export event; broader than mRNA export alone but restricted to nuclear export/quality control of RNA and ribonucleoprotein cargoes.

name: Muscle contraction and potassium homeostasis
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Muscle contraction and calcium homeostasis'; needs to specify the distinct ion focus of this theme.

name: Sensory organ development and function
rationale: Covers sensory perception plus auditory hair-cell morphogenesis and saliva secretion regulation, both involving sensory organ development/innervation and secretory function tied to sensation; broader than 'sensory perception' alone to include organ morphogenesis and glandular control.

name: Regulation of cell-matrix adhesion turnover
rationale: All four pathways concern regulating the assembly, strength or disassembly of integrin-based cell-substrate/focal adhesions, including negative regulation and focal adhesion disassembly.

name: DNA repair pathways
rationale: Duplicate name already used elsewhere; members are specific excision/mismatch/break repair pathways, distinguishing it from siblings focused on genome stability, cell cycle, and telomeres.

name: Chylomicron and VLDL assembly
rationale: Collides with parent name 'HDL particle assembly and clearance' pattern; 'lipoprotein transport' is redundant given members focus on assembly, and dropping it distinguishes from HDL clearance sibling while remaining true to chylomicron/VLDL assembly members.

name: RHO GTPase regulation and Golgi vesicle budding
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Small GTPase signalling and localization control', which covers the same generic GTPase-mediated signal transduction terms; the revised name reflects the RHO/RHOBTB3 GTPase activity regulation and Golgi vesicle budding specific to this theme's members.

name: DNA damage repair
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and though similar in theme to the parent, it does not literally repeat it; insufficient information to narrow further without overstepping.

name: Spindle and centrosome localization
rationale: Overlapped sibling 'Mitotic and meiotic chromosome segregation' via shared chromosome segregation theme and echoed parent's 'spindle organization'; members focus on spindle/centriole/centrosome localization, which distinguishes it.

name: Intrinsic apoptotic signalling
rationale: Collided with parents 'Mitochondrial apoptosis and its regulation'/'Apoptotic signalling'; renamed to contrast with sibling 'Extrinsic apoptotic signalling' and clarify pathway type rather than location.

name: Aromatic and non-proteinogenic amino acid catabolism
rationale: Core members at high inclusion (tryptophan and tyrosine catabolism, aromatic amino acid metabolism, non-proteinogenic amino acid metabolism/biosynthesis) converge on the breakdown and interconversion of aromatic and non-protein amino acids into signalling molecules, nitrogen carriers and TCA intermediates. Weakly included members (general amino acid metabolism 0.27, vitamin B6 metabolism 0.31, serine metabolism 0.34) touch cofactor and one-carbon chemistry adjacent to this but are not required for the name.

name: Transendothelial leukocyte migration
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Chemokine-driven leukocyte chemotaxis'; renamed to specify the adhesion/transmigration step distinct from chemokine-gradient sensing.

name: p53-driven senescence and apoptotic pathways
rationale: Overlaps significantly with sibling 'p53-driven DNA damage response and cell cycle control'; sharpened to focus specifically on senescence and apoptosis outcomes rather than the broader DNA damage response, distinguishing it clearly.

name: Amyloid-beta driven neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation
rationale: Union covers amyloid-beta/lipoprotein signalling plus hippocampal neuron apoptosis, neuroinflammatory suppression and dendritic spine loss, all downstream neuronal/glial consequences of amyloid-lipoprotein biology; broader terms like 'neuron apoptosis' alone would miss the amyloid/lipoprotein child.

name: Sinoatrial node development and electrical coupling
rationale: Covers the child (conduction system function) plus direct members on sinoatrial node cell differentiation/development and electrical coupling between cardiac cells; kept tighter than general cardiac development since all members concern pacemaker cell origin or intercellular electrical communication.

name: Extracellular matrix glycosaminoglycan metabolism
rationale: Nearly repeated the parent name; specifying glycosaminoglycan/ECM matrix components distinguishes it from the parent and from the transport-focused sibling.

name: Phosphate group transport and metabolism
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism and transport'; narrowed to emphasize phosphate-specific handling that distinguishes this theme.

name: B and dendritic cell adaptive immune responses
rationale: The child covers B cell identity/receptor markers; direct members add B cell-related functions (IL-21 production, immunoglobulin affinity selection, negative regulation of B cell immunity, adaptive immune memory) plus a dendritic cell signature. The umbrella must span both lineages' contribution to adaptive humoral immunity while excluding innate-only or unrelated biology.

name: Toll-like receptor 2 and lipopolysaccharide signalling regulation
rationale: Nearly duplicates sibling 'Innate immune inflammatory signalling' which shares 'inflammatory response' and 'Toll signaling pathway'; this theme's distinct focus is TLR2/LPS-specific regulation, which separates it.

name: Hedgehog signalling and GLI regulation
rationale: Four of five members directly concern Hedgehog pathway signalling and its GLI/Smoothened restraint machinery (negative regulation of smoothened signaling, HALLMARK_HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING, Signaling by Hedgehog, Degradation of GLI2). The Wnt pathway member (0.35) and the DVL-interacting protein member (0.46) fall below the 0.5 threshold and are excluded from the name.

name: Mitochondrial and cytosolic tRNA aminoacylation
rationale: Covers mitochondrial translation (via aminoacyl-tRNA synthesis) plus the direct members on cytosolic tRNA charging and general protein metabolism; broad enough for 'Metabolism of proteins' while staying centered on the aminoacylation/translation machinery shared by all members.

name: Purine deoxyribonucleoside and dGMP metabolism
rationale: Repeats parent's 'Purine ribonucleoside salvage and catabolism' and overlaps sibling 'Purine and nucleoside salvage metabolism' which also covers ribonucleoside metabolism/salvage; this theme is distinguished by deoxyribonucleoside and dGMP catabolism specifics.

name: Mitotic division and cytokinesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (chromosome segregation) and sibling (segregation fidelity); this theme covers division/cytokinesis machinery, not segregation.

name: Neuronal development and synaptic transmission
rationale: No parent to repeat, and no sibling covers neuronal development plus synaptic transmission specifically; remains distinct.

name: Cell-cell junction assembly
rationale: Overlapped both the parent name and the sibling 'Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesion', whose members (cell adhesion, membrane; cell cell adhesion) are indistinguishable from this theme's; the members here emphasize junction organization/assembly rather than cadherin-specific adhesion, which separates it.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression and protein complex assembly
rationale: No siblings and distinct from parent; name already specific to mitochondrial gene expression and complex assembly rather than RNA processing crosstalk.

name: Antimicrobial peptide defence
rationale: Distinct from parents (metal sequestration and general humoral effectors framing) and sibling (complement activation); already specific to antimicrobial peptides.

name: Antimicrobial peptide-mediated humoral defence
rationale: All four members describe secreted antimicrobial peptides and effectors (defensins, cathelicidin, lactoferrin, lysozyme, complement, granule proteases) acting extracellularly in body fluids and at epithelial surfaces to kill or disrupt microbes.

name: Virus-host interactions
rationale: Both children plus all members concern host factors and defences governing viral entry, replication, and innate sensing across the viral life cycle.

name: HDL metabolism and cellular cholesterol efflux
