rationale: Distinct from parent (broader transport regulation) and sibling (homeostasis focus); this theme specifically covers HDL metabolism and efflux mechanisms.

name: Glycosaminoglycan and glycoprotein metabolism
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and though related to the parent, it addresses metabolism broadly rather than repeating the parent's disorder focus.

name: Cardiac electrical conduction and coupling
rationale: Name is not a duplicate elsewhere and, while related to siblings, its focus on action potential regulation and conduction coupling distinguishes it from 'Cardiac pacemaker excitability and conduction' (pacemaker-specific) and 'Regulation of cardiac membrane excitability' (general membrane repolarization/depolarization).

name: Glucose and glycogen energy metabolism
rationale: Covers the glycogen storage child plus glycolysis/pyruvate direct members; oxygen transport (0.74) is included as the O2 supply side linked to aerobic glucose metabolism, though it is the weakest fit.

name: Insulin signalling in glucose and glycogen metabolism
rationale: Covers the child (insulin-driven glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis) plus direct members on IRS activation and signal attenuation, which are upstream/downstream regulatory steps of the same insulin signalling cascade controlling glucose handling.

name: Proteostasis and protein degradation
rationale: Both children and the direct members (ubiquitination signalling, ubiquitin-independent proteasomal degradation, stress granule disassembly) converge on maintaining protein homeostasis through degradation or clearance machinery, broader than either child alone but excluding unrelated processes like transcription or metabolism.

name: Neuronal morphogenesis in synapse maturation
rationale: Repeated parent's 'synapse formation and structural maturation' scope without adding specificity; renamed to emphasize morphogenetic processes within that maturation context.

The children already span an enormous and disparate set of cell-biology domains (neurodegeneration, circadian clocks, cytoskeletal transport, lipid mediators, insulin/glucose signalling, autophagy, ion homeostasis, muscle physiology, sensory biology), and the 65 direct members add yet another scattershot of GO/Reactome terms (bicarbonate transport, gastric acid secretion, protein tetramerization, viral entry, gap junctions, cotranslational targeting) with no shared mechanism or compartment; any umbrella broad enough to cover all of this would collapse to a near-vacuous word like 'cellular processes', so no honest specific name exists.

name: Protein phosphorylation and methylation signalling
rationale: Covers both children (kinase-mediated and regulated protein phosphorylation) plus the direct members: general phosphorylation and protein methylation, without invoking a mechanism narrower than 'signalling via covalent modification'.

name: Membrane shaping and lipid bilayer asymmetry
rationale: Five high-inclusion members concern building and remodelling membrane structure (plasma membrane and ER tubular network/organization) and controlling phospholipid distribution across the bilayer (scrambling, translocation). The low-inclusion proton-ATPase assembly member (0.26) is excluded as it concerns a distinct process of pump complex biogenesis rather than membrane shape or lipid asymmetry.

name: Ciliary regulation of embryonic patterning
rationale: No parent to collide with, and distinct from siblings like Hedgehog signalling in neural tube patterning and Embryonic axial patterning and organogenesis by its specific focus on ciliary mechanisms in patterning.

name: Viral hijacking of host translation machinery
rationale: All three concern viruses (calicivirus, influenza B, influenza A) exploiting host ribosomes and initiation factors to translate or reinitiate viral mRNAs, including influenza's broader RNA synthesis pathway that culminates in host-mediated translation of viral proteins.

name: Cardiac electrical repolarization
rationale: Covers the child (action potential repolarization) plus direct members on cardiac conduction, Na+ channel inactivation, and membrane hyperpolarization/K+ transport that set repolarization; the K+ transport member (0.30) is a weak boundary case but still fits this electrical-repolarization theme.

name: Addictive substance response circuitry
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from both parents, adding specificity about addictive substances rather than repeating either parent term.

name: Reward circuitry response to addictive substances
rationale: All five pathways describe neural signalling adaptations to drugs of abuse (nicotine, cocaine, ethanol, opioids) or the nicotinic receptors mediating such reinforcement, converging on dopaminergic reward circuitry, receptor signalling and transcriptional plasticity underlying addiction.

name: NAD+ and pyridine nucleotide metabolism
rationale: Overlaps with sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism and its regulation', which shares GTP biosynthetic process, phosphorus metabolic process, and nucleoside triphosphate biosynthetic process; narrowing to the NAD+/pyridine cofactor focus distinguishes it.

name: Vascular remodeling in wound healing
rationale: Repeated parent's scope without linking to fibroproliferative wound healing context; new name specifies vascular changes as part of that process.

name: VEGF signaling in endothelial differentiation
rationale: Name overlapped with sibling 'Vascular and lymphatic development and repair', which also covers VEGF response and angiogenesis; revised to emphasize the VEGF-receptor signaling and endothelial/lymphatic differentiation focus unique to this theme's members.

name: Nucleotide pool metabolism and salvage
rationale: All three children and representative members concern the synthesis, interconversion, salvage and catabolic clearance of nucleotide and nucleoside pools; no direct members exist to extend this beyond the children's shared scope.

name: Steroid and vitamin D hormone metabolism
rationale: Covers the child's adrenal/gonadal steroid synthesis plus direct members on vitamin D catabolism, receptor signalling regulation, and CYP24A1/CYP27B1 defects affecting vitamin D hormone activation/degradation; unifying theme is fat-soluble hormone (steroid and secosteroid) biosynthesis/catabolism.

name: Hematopoietic and leukocyte differentiation
rationale: Covers stem/progenitor homeostasis plus direct members on hematopoietic progenitor, leukocyte, lymphocyte and T cell differentiation, without restating the single child's stem/progenitor homeostasis focus.

name: Cardiac muscle structural development
rationale: Own members are dominated by cardiac muscle/cell development and differentiation, while 'Striated muscle structural development' could also describe the skeletal muscle sibling whose members include myofibril assembly and filament organization; specifying cardiac distinguishes it.

name: Cellular senescence
rationale: Core members define senescence, its regulation, oncogene-induced trigger, and heterochromatin/chromatin-based execution; UV response and MITF-dependent gene regulation are weaker inclusions (0.62, 0.37) but both converge on senescence induction or its control, so the shared theme remains cellular senescence.

name: Vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter exocytosis
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent 'Neurotransmitter release and receptor signalling' and sibling 'Synaptic transmission and plasticity'; narrowed to the specific mechanism of vesicle fusion/exocytosis distinguishing it from both.

name: Nucleocytoplasmic transport of RNA and protein cargo
rationale: The child covers nuclear RNA export and surveillance; direct members add protein export from the nucleus, IP3/IP4 small-molecule transport across the nuclear envelope, and Vpr's hijacking of host nuclear transport, so the umbrella must span macromolecular and ionic traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm rather than RNA alone.

name: Microtubule- and cytoskeleton-based organelle transport
rationale: Both children and all members describe motor-driven positioning and transport of organelles (mitochondria, lysosomes, vesicles) along the cytoskeleton, generalized beyond the neuronal-specific child but not into unrelated cytoskeletal biology.

name: Digestive nutrient uptake and sugar transport
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; specifically addresses digestive nutrient uptake and sugar transport, not overlapping with others.

name: Protein glycosylation and glycosylation disorders
rationale: Union covers general protein glycosylation, dystroglycan/glycosylation-linked disorders, and O-glycosylation of TSR domain proteins, all being forms or defects of protein glycosylation.

name: Vascular smooth muscle phenotype switching
rationale: Name overlapped conceptually with parent 'ECM remodelling in vessels' scope; narrowed to specify vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype switching, distinguishing from endothelial-focused siblings.

name: Histone pre-mRNA processing and prespliceosome assembly
rationale: The transcription termination portion overlapped with sibling 'RNA polymerase II transcription elongation and termination'; the revised name highlights the histone mRNA 3'-processing and prespliceosome assembly members that distinguish this theme.

name: Rho family GTPase cycles
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Small GTPase signalling' and overlaps sibling 'Rho and Ras GTPase activation and effector signalling'; members are specifically RHOA/RHO/CDC42/RHOF/RHOU cycles, distinguishing it as Rho-family cycle regulation.

name: Calcium-mediated and calcineurin signalling regulation
rationale: Covers the child (calcium ion transmembrane transport regulation) plus direct members on calcium-mediated signaling and calcineurin-mediated signaling, both up- and down-regulation; narrower terms like calmodulin or specific channels would exclude some members.

name: Epithelial architecture and homeostasis
rationale: Covers adhesion/junctional biology, keratinized epidermal differentiation, and stem-cell renewal of intestinal epithelium, all being aspects of how epithelial tissues are organized and maintained; broader terms like 'adhesion' alone would exclude keratinization and stem cell homeostasis.

name: Nucleotide excision repair and UV response
rationale: Repeated the parent 'DNA damage repair'; specifying UV-induced photoproduct repair via nucleotide excision distinguishes it from base excision repair and oxidative damage response sibling.

name: Interferon-gamma and cytoplasmic innate antiviral responses
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent by specifying interferon-gamma and cytoplasmic sensing mechanisms.

name: Mitochondrial proteostasis and biogenesis
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Mitochondrial dynamics and quality control' and sibling 'Mitochondrial organelle dynamics and quality control'; renamed to reflect distinct focus on protein quality and biogenesis rather than fission/fusion dynamics.

name: Cellular osmotic and salt stress response
rationale: Distinct from parent (vasopressin-mediated water reabsorption) and sibling (body fluid homeostasis); focuses on cellular-level osmotic/salt stress response mechanisms rather than systemic water balance.

name: Hyperosmotic and salt stress response
rationale: All members concern cellular sensing and adaptation to osmotic/salt/ionic stress (volume regulation, osmolyte and ion transport, pH control) and its link to survival versus apoptotic outcome, including the aldosterone-driven sodium handling response that shares this ion/osmotic-balance and apoptosis axis.

name: Mechanotransduction in hair cells and muscle
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifies mechanotransduction in hair cells and muscle rather than general sensory/chemosensory transduction or detection.

name: Mechanotransduction in hearing and balance
rationale: Core members cover hair-cell bundle morphogenesis, sound transduction, gravity/vestibular sensing, and the actin-myosin machinery underlying stereocilia and contraction; the weakly included general mechanical stimulus response (0.48) is subsumed as it overlaps largely with the same hair-cell and load-sensing systems.

name: Regulation of cytosolic innate immune signaling
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Cytosolic viral sensing and interferon induction' which shares interferon production and TLR3 members; this theme is distinguished by its focus on regulatory and receptor signaling processes (cPRR signaling, IL-18 production, IFN-mediated signaling regulation) rather than direct induction/sensing.

name: Fatty acid oxidation and ketone body metabolism
rationale: All five members concern mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation and/or the synthesis and utilisation of ketone bodies derived from it, unified by fasting energy metabolism.

name: rRNA and tRNA processing and modification
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from the parent, which covers snRNA/snoRNA processing rather than rRNA and tRNA.

name: HIF-mediated hypoxia response
rationale: No siblings present and name is more specific than both parents, distinguishing the HIF-mediated mechanism from the broader stress/hypoxia themes.
